MN202611_2g06yzx5ex.t:
The flooded mine is in Bogor in West Java

It's been three days since Rani last saw her father as he left for work on Monday. Early on Tuesday, she received news that he was trapped underground.

Rais, 50, had been working as an illegal gold miner in Bogor, Indonesia's West Java province. On Monday night, he and 25 other miners were digging in an open-pit mine about 100m (328ft) deep, when torrential rain caused a nearby river to overflow and flood the two shafts.

Authorities on Thursday confirmed that 13 people had died and their bodies were recovered from the site. At least 13 more are thought to still be missing.

Search-and-rescue operations are ongoing, with personnel using ropes to access the depths of the dark, narrow and slippery mine shafts, which are continually being flooded from below.

Above ground, ambulances and medical personnel are ready and waiting to transport victims.

"We are coordinating with all search and rescue personnel involved in the operation to monitor water conditions and assess access to the mine shaft," Desiana Kartika Bahari, head of the Jakarta Search and Rescue Office, said in a statement on Wednesday.

"The depth of the shaft, narrow access and limited lighting are key considerations in determining the search strategy so that personnel can operate safely."

Rescuers have been working day and night to find survivors in the flooded mine shaft

Small-scale gold mining is banned in Indonesia, but remains widespread in rural parts of the mineral-rich archipelago.

Multiple studies show that over the past ten years the illegal industry has rapidly flourished, often in correlation with rising gold prices. In early 2026, those prices reached an all-time high – spurring a gold rush that prompted mine operators across the country to expand their operations.

This included state-owned mining company Aneka Tambang (Antam), which owns the business permit for the area in which this week's flooded mine is located. Antam have said the mine was not theirs and was operating without their authorisation.

On Wednesday, while rescue operations there were underway, West Java Regional Police separately announced that they had uncovered 24 cases of illegal mining across the province between October and November alone.

But Bisman Bakhtiar, Executive Director of the Center for Energy and Mining Law Studies, told the BBC earlier this year that the actual number of illegal mines in Indonesia is higher than the government's figures.

"[The government figures are] what's been recorded. That means there must be more than that," he said, noting that law enforcement operations have had little impact on the sector.

"It's still very massive and very big because this has been going on for a very long time."

Others allege that the illegal industry is underpinned by corruption.

Laode M Syarif, former deputy chairman of the Corruption Eradication Committee, said that unofficial mining is difficult to eradicate because every illegal mine has "backing", usually from "police and military or high-ranking officials in local and provincial governments".

"As long as these backers are not dealt with firmly, illegal mining will continue," he said.

In many cases, though, the allure of these mines is simple: they offer an economic lifeline to people with few other viable prospects.

Despite the value of gold having dipped in recent months, countless illegal miners throughout Indonesia are still eagerly digging for paydirt.

But the lack of regulation and poor construction in the pits also means accidents are relatively common – whether from landslides, floods, or exposure to hazardous gases, all of which have claimed lives in recent years.

Relatives of the missing Bogor miners have been waiting near the site for news of their loved ones

Earlier this year, in the same area as this week's flooded mine, 11 illegal gold miners reportedly died after a carbon monoxide leak inside a shaft.

Elsewhere, in West Sumatra, nine people were killed at an illegal gold mine in May after heavy rain triggered the collapse of a 30-metre cliff, burying 12 miners in total.

There are numerous reports of other such incidents across the Indonesian archipelago. But the illegal nature of the small-scale gold mining sector obfuscates the true number of casualties.

Even this week, when asked how many miners were in the pits in Bogor when they flooded, M Adam Hamdani, head of emergency and logistics at the Bogor Regency Regional Disaster Management Agency, said the total casualty figure "is still unclear".

"Some say 20 people, others say 29 people," Hamdani told Indonesian news outlet Detik. "The problem is that no one reported it and no one wants to report it."

The Indonesian Ombudsman on Thursday urged law enforcement officials to conduct a thorough investigation of the incident and to address the larger systemic issue behind it.

"This should be a momentum for all parties to resolve the [illegal gold mining] problem comprehensively, not just taking action after the incident or closing the holes discovered," said Abdul Ghoffar, a member of the Indonesian Ombudsman.

"We need to uncover the entire [illegal gold mining] chain," he continued. "We must not allow only the miners in the field to be seen and prosecuted, while those who control the activities, provide capital and facilities, store, and market the mined products remain untouched.

"Law enforcement must target the actors and networks that keep this illegal activity going."

As rescue operations continue and more bodies are recovered, the picture is becoming less murky. But even if there are survivors among those who remain missing, time may be running out.

More than three days since the shafts flooded, the relatives of the anonymous men in the mines are desperately waiting to hear whether their loved ones survived.

As she waits for news of her father, Rani says: "I hope he's found soon."

MN202611_1amwnrwos1m.t:
Millions of drivers who were mis-sold car finance agreements could face further delays to compensation after the financial regulator said it had made some errors in its calculations.

Driver have already been told they must wait until at least 2027 to receive compensation, although some may be offered an early settlement.

Average payments of about £829 are expected under the rules published by the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA).

However, legal challenges to the scheme - which will be heard in February 2027 -mean compensation calculations and payments have been delayed.

The vast majority of new cars, and many second-hand ones, are bought with finance agreements. Customers pay an initial deposit to secure the vehicle, then a monthly fee with interest.

Compensation could be given to many of those who took out a car loan between April 2007 and November 2024.

The decision by the FCA, the financial regulator, applies to about 12 million car loans - about 37% of the total number during the period.

In 2021, the FCA banned deals where car dealers received commission from lenders, based on the interest rate charged to the customer. These were known as discretionary commission arrangements (DCAs) and customers were often not told about them.

The FCA said this provided an incentive for a buyer to be charged a higher-than-necessary interest rate, leaving them paying too much.

Other car buyers were also judged to have signed unfair contracts because the commission paid to the dealer was so high - accounting for 39% of the total cost of credit and 10% of the loan.

Some customers were not given accurate information about the best finance deal because of exclusive arrangements between car dealers and lenders.

Under the latest proposals, the FCA expects average payouts of £829 per mis-sold agreement.

The total cost of the compensation, including administrative costs, could hit £9.1bn.

How much individual consumers receive will depend on the degree of harm suffered.

The FCA has announced some claimants might be offered an early settlement, but only if it as good as what would be paid under the current proposed central scheme.

Complaints have already been made about four million finance agreements. Those people do not need to do anything.

The regulator urged anyone who has not yet complained to contact their car loan provider directly, rather than using a third-party claims management company.

The regulator's central compensation scheme allows people to complain and potentially receive compensation for mis-sold deals without the need for a lawyer or to go through the courts.

Motorists have also been warned to be on the alert for scammers posing as car finance lenders offering fake compensation .

The FCA has published this guidance on how to complain , external .

lenders will respond to claims, explaining if you are owed compensation and how much – but timing of those letters is now uncertain owing to the legal challenge

those who complain before the scheme gets up and running are likely to receive compensation faster

some people who complained by 30 June and are not owed compensation should be told by 18 November, if the agreement began on or after 1 April 2014 and you complained by 30 June 2026

some of those who complained by 31 August will be told if they are not owed compensation by 18 January 2027, if the agreement began before 1 April 2014

there are exemptions , external , and anyone who does not hear from their lender by the dates set out, isn't necessarily owed compensation

those who have not complained will be contacted by their lender. People will be asked if they want to opt in to the scheme to have their case reviewed

those motor finance borrowers who do not receive a letter - for example because lenders no longer have their details and cannot trace them - can still make a claim

Regulators have warned claims management companies and law firms involved in motor finance commission claims to make sure consumers do not have multiple representatives for the same claim and are not charged excessive termination fees.

FCA boss Nikhil Rathi told the BBC's Today programme there are "many law firms out there who would like to get 30% of any compensation", stressing that the regulator's scheme was "free to use" for consumers.

Millions of drivers were in line to receive compensation this year, and most of the remainder should have got compensation by the end of 2027.

But the FCA has confirmed that no compensation will be paid before 2027 as a result of legal challenges to the scheme.

The watchdog has now said it uncovered some mistakes in how it categorised a small group of loan agreements under its redress scheme, which could have a small impact on compensation levels.

"While the potential impact on average compensation is small – less than £10 per agreement, on average – we recognise this affects the ongoing litigation," the FCA said. That could leave average payouts somewhere between £819 and £839.

"We will discuss with the challengers and the court the impact on this deadline, and for the timeline of the litigation."

Consumer Voice has said the scheme leaves "too many people short-changed" . The FCA has also received challenges from three lenders: Volkswagen Financial Services, Mercedes Benz Financial Services, and Credit Agricole Auto Finance.

The UK's Upper Tribunal has agreed to hear legal challenges to the scheme, with a hearing scheduled for 16 February to 3 March.

It means that lenders will no longer need to calculate or pay compensation to people owed money under its scheme, until the legal process concludes.

The FCA said it would need to decide what to do next if the courts decided to overturn the programme. Without a scheme in place, the FCA has estimated that up to 19 million complaints would need to be handled individually, taking three years and costing lenders £6bn more.

It said it would "defend the scheme robustly as lawful and the best way to resolve such a widespread, long running and complex issue".

Ultimately, the industry is expected to cover the full costs of any compensation scheme, including any administrative costs.

Lenders - including some of the UK's biggest banks and specialist motor finance firms - have already set aside billions of pounds for potential payouts.

The FCA said a minority of claimants will be made early offers, but most will have to wait for the outcome of next year's court case.

With huge compensation payouts inevitable, Barclays will offer early settlements to some claimants, with others expected to follow suit.

However, the FCA said it had asked Barclays to pause making compensation offers while it worked the errors it identified in November.

The FCA has published a factsheet to help drivers , external work out whether they should accept early settlements from lenders.

Accepting would mean quicker payouts but remove them from any changes to the central scheme.

The body that represents the lending industry, the Finance and Leasing Association, said it had "concerns" about the central programme but that it was choosing not to raise a legal challenge.

Santander, Barclays and Lloyds also accepted the scheme, despite raising concerns that the level of redress is disproportionate to those who suffered harm.

Even if drivers are entitled to compensation from these lenders they will need to wait.

There were some concessions made to lenders in a scaled-down final compensation plan from the FCA.

The Supreme Court considered three test cases which influenced the FCA's decision and, ultimately, limited how broad the compensation programme could have been.

It focused on whether the car dealers had a duty to act on behalf of their customers, rather than in their own interests. The test case which was upheld was that of Marcus Johnson , who bought his first car - a Suzuki Swift - in 2017.

In his case, the Supreme Court said the terms of his finance deal were unfair due of the size of the commission payment, and the fact he appeared to have been misled over the relationship between the finance firm and the dealer.

Have you been turned down for compensation relating to a car finance deal? Share your experiences.

MN202611_nq7zig0vza.t:
Veruschka was a distinctive presence on the covers of magazines like Vogue and Life in the 1960s and 70s

Veruschka, the model and artist who became one of one of the first global fashion stars in the 1960s, has died at the age of 87.

She became known as the striking subject of fantastical photoshoots that helped expand the boundaries of fashion and beauty in the 60s and 70s, appearing on the cover of American Vogue 13 times.

Vogue's obituary , external described her as "the shape-shifting supermodel who defined an era", explaining: "One of the original supermodels, Veruschka was also among fashion's great performance artists."

She also made memorable appearances in classic swinging 60s film Blow Up and 2006 James Bond movie Casino Royale.

Veruschka was born Vera von Lehndorff into an aristocratic family in 1939 in Königsberg, then in Germany, now known as Kaliningrad in Russia.

Her father, Heinrich Count von Lehndorff, was executed in 1944 for his part in a failed plot to assassinate Adolf Hitler.

She studied art in Hamburg and Florence before beginning her career as a model "and soon became a legend", her sister Countess Catharina von Lehndorff wrote in a tribute , external .

"She worked with Yves Saint Laurent, Karl Lagerfeld, and Valentino, but also immersed herself in avant-garde photography projects in which she painted, staged, and deconstructed her body.

"Veruschka was never just a model – she was an artist, a boundary-pusher, a rebel. Her work is considered a feminist precursor to performance art."

MN202611_felgiyi3t4.t:
A delegation of French military experts specialising in engineering and explosive ordnance disposal has visited the Rwanda Defence Force (RDF) Engineer Command headquarters, in a move aimed at strengthening cooperation and sharing expertise in military engineering.

The delegation was received on November 26, 2026, by the Deputy Commander of RDF Engineer Command, Col Marie Claire Muragijimana.

The visit provides an opportunity for the two military institutions to exchange knowledge, explore areas of mutual interest and strengthen professional collaboration in military engineering, particularly in technical operations and explosive ordnance management.

Discussions are expected to focus on sharing technical experience, improving operational capabilities and identifying opportunities for future cooperation, including possible joint training programmes and professional exchanges.

Such engagement could contribute to strengthening the technical capacity of RDF engineering personnel, particularly in specialised areas that support military operations, infrastructure development and explosive hazard management.

The visit also reflects the importance of continued defence cooperation between the two countries, with military-to-military engagements providing a platform for exchanging expertise and building institutional relationships.

MN202611_1f8luc2eqsw.t:
The Competition watchdog says wide-ranging reforms are needed in the UK's private dentistry market to ensure people get a fair deal.

It says patients can struggle with costs and find it difficult to shop around and compare prices.

In some areas the cost of a composite white filling is equivalent to more than a third of weekly income.

The British Dental Association says it is essential that there is a thriving private market but it is also vital that the government fixes NHS dentistry.

The Competition and Markets Authority's (CMA) interim report on private dentist services says millions of people are struggling with the costs of private dental care, with some delaying or going without treatment.

Private dentist services are now used by about 60% of UK patients for some care

At large dental groups prices rose by around 7% a year on average between 2023 and 2025, ahead of inflation and wage increases

A composite while filling is equivalent to about 36% of average weekly disposable income in the North East of England and 35% in Wales

There is wide variation in prices even in the same local area. In Preston, composite fillings ranged from £80 to £223

An amalgam filling (sometimes known as a silver filling) costs anything between £72 and £159 in Caerphilly

The report argues it is difficult for patients to shop around for a good deal, with one in six practices in the UK not publishing prices online.

The watchdog also says private dentists can have financial incentives to promote treatments and this can create a risk that patients are sold services not in their best interests.

There is also evidence that some practices have targets to switch NHS patients to private care.

The CMA says there can be substantial variation in profit margins between practices.

Underlying many of these issues is a shortage of dentists.

The UK has fewer dentists per person in the population than most European countries, with a high vacancy rate in practices and that can hold back the expansion of services.

The market isn't working well for dental patients according to Sarah Cardell, chief executive of the CMA.

"Many people are struggling with affordability, and those on lower incomes and in certain parts of the UK are hardest hit," she said.

"We're proposing a wide-ranging package of measures to change the way the market operates and will work with governments across the UK to finalise these recommendations ahead of our final report in March."

The British Dental Association (BDA) said it would work with the competition watchdog to come up with practical measures but said governments in the UK should make fundamental reforms to NHS dentistry.

Eddie Crouch, chair of the BDA, said: "It is essential that we have a thriving private dental market.

"But successive governments have left millions with no options when it comes to securing NHS care.

"When it comes to giving patients access to affordable care ministers hold almost all the cards."

The People's Party of Alberto Núñez Feijóo is narrowly ahead in most opinion polls

After eight years of Socialist-led government under Pedro Sánchez, Spain is at a crossroads.

Snap elections are taking place on Sunday 29 November, and voters face a choice of continued left-wing rule or a conservative-led government, with the likely support of far-right Vox.

Sánchez called this vote eight months early after MPs rejected planned changes to Spain's housing laws.

He was responding to nationwide protests after an 87-year-old woman called Maricarmen Abascal was evicted from her rented flat in Madrid and later died.

But his government lost the support of a centre-right party called Junts from the north-eastern region of Catalonia which sought to protect the rights of property owners.

Housing remains one of the hot-button issues for voters, but they are also focused on the high cost of living, corruption and immigration. And the election takes place within weeks of a devastating rail disaster that has shattered confidence in Spain’s high-speed rail network.

Alberto Núñez Feijóo's conservative People's Party is narrowly ahead of the Socialist PSOE in most polls.

He has spoken of Spain being probably at "the most significant moment in our country for the past 50 years", and he aims to "repair the state, regenerate democracy, reunited the nation and recover Spain's ambition and self-esteem". But it is unlikely he could do anything without the backing of Vox, who are third in the opinion polls.

For more on Feijóo, Sánchez and who else to watch in this election - read here .

Spain has a population of almost 50 million, and almost 39 million people have the right to vote for the Congress and the upper house, the Senate. The polls open at 09:00 (08:00 GMT) on Sunday and close at 20:00 (19:00 GMT). Provisional results will start appearing an hour later.

Spain saw its first general strike for 14 years this month over a shortage of housing and high rental costs

Spain's property prices and rents have soared by more than 80% from 2015 to 2025, and wages have not kept pace.

Spain has a combination of high demand and scarce supply: the Bank of Spain estimates 700,000 homes are needed to ease the pressure.

The result is that millions of Spaniards have little chance to buy a house, while they live in fear of eviction if their rent is increased. On 11 November, four million Spaniards were galvanised into joining the first general strike since 2012, according to the unions.

Pedro Sánchez has embraced housing reform as a big campaign issue and left-wing parties have promised rent controls and protection against eviction, while the right is focusing on building more homes, tax breaks for homebuyers and planning deregulation.

Sánchez's wife Begoña Gómez has played an important role in the election campaign

Support for the Socialists is down from 2023, but even then he came second in the race and relied on the backing of other parties, mainly on the left, to stay in power.

Securing a majority requires 176 seats out of the 350 in Spain's Congress. This time the other left-wing parties whose support he needs, in particular the Broad Front (Frente Amplio), have fallen back and the big questions now are more about Feijóo's conservatives.

"It is a demobilisation of the left. Sánchez's party is not doing well," says Jacobo Ramos Folch, Policy Analyst and visiting professor at the University of Navarra.

"That lack of majority is really a reality – and the rise of Vox. What is changing that shift of majorities is the rise of Vox."

Vox have been around since 2013 but polls suggest this time they could almost double their 33 seats in Spain's lower house, the Congress.

Their big themes are "national priority" – putting Spanish citizens first for subsidies and welfare, along with repatriating migrants "in an illegal situation" and "remigration" of foreigners who do not contribute to Spain.

Pedro Sánchez (left), Alberto Núñez Feijóo (centre) and Santiago Abascal (right)

Migration has become a key challenge for Spain, and Alberto Nuñez Feijóo has accused his rival of being a "problem for Europe when it comes to immigration" after the influx of tens of thousands of migrants into the exclave of Ceuta from neighbouring Morocco in July.

This month too, the Canary Island of El Hierro has seen record arrivals, with 2,000 people landing there on 24 November. Abascal has spoken of "another invasion".

And yet a recent CIS survey put it far behind housing, cost of living, healthcare and working conditions.

The PP and Vox have bitterly criticised the Socialist-led government for a drive to legalise unauthorised migrants this year that attracted 1.2 million applications.

Feijóo's party wants to see more controlled immigration. Vox has called for mass deportations.

Clashing political visions reflect a divided Spain ahead of election

Feijóo has accused the Socialists of being "the most corrupt party" that Spain has ever seen, and a number of cases have involved Sánchez's inner circle and family.

People should distinguish between real and "fictitious" corruption allegations, says Sánchez.

His former transport minister José Luis Ábalos has been given 24 years in prison over multiple corruption offences.

Leading party figure Santos Cerdán awaits trial for alleged bribery and denies wrongdoing.

Sánchez's wife Begoña Gómez faces trial for alleged misuse of public funds and using her marriage to further her academic career. She denies wrongdoing. And his brother David Sánchez has been banned from public office for nine years for administrative misconduct.

Feijóo has made clear his objective is to form a majority and make "parliamentary support agreements" with Vox. As far as a coalition is concerned, he says he will respect the will of Spanish voters, but maintains Abascal has never talked to him about running any ministries.

The PP leader is clear that Vox's national priority policy would run counter to Spain's constitution and European Union treaties: "No-one can sign illegal agreements."

Even if they were to go into coalition, Camino Mortera-Martinez of the Centre for European Reform, and a former European affairs adviser to the Spanish prime minister is not convinced Vox would wield much influence.

"They're not going to get any of the core ministries. They're not going to get defence or home affairs or foreign policy or economy," she told the BBC. Even if they take over the education ministry, Mortera-Martinez argues education policy is largely devolved to Spain's regional governments.

The leader of Vox, Santiago Abascal, is hoping to double his party's seats in parliament

Since 2022, Vox has worked with the PP in a series of regional coalition governments, holding ministries such as culture and tourism. At the time Feijóo had reservations about Vox joining the conservatives in government in Castilla y León.

The following year they went into coalition with the conservatives in Valencia, Aragón, Murcia, and Extremadura, but pulled out of all five governments in 2024 when they refused to accept unaccompanied migrant children being moved to their regions.

They have since signed new coalition pacts with the PP in Extremadura, Aragón, Castilla y León and Andalusia.

Unlike many European countries Spain has 17 autonomous communities (and two cities) that have their own parliament and their own powers. Catalonia in the north-east and the Basque Country in the north have their own police forces.

The regions matter to Sunday's result. Catalonia alone has 48 seats out of the 350 in Spain's parliament, and the Socialists have recently come to rely on regional parties for support.

Sánchez's government relied on the support of Basque separatists Bildu and two Catalan parties, ERC on the left and Junts on the right. But when Junts refused to back his housing reform, he decided to dissolve parliament.

Spain is made up of 50 constituencies which each have a minimum of two seats.

The exclaves of Ceuta and Melilla both have one, and the other 248 seats are divided proportionally according to voter numbers.

Madrid province will have 38 seats, Barcelona 32 and Valencia 16.

To win a seat, a party has to win 3% of the vote in a province, but in smaller provinces with fewer seats parties generally need more than that.

MN202611_y27zkk0w1e.t:
The Norwegian low cost carrier Norse Atlantic Airways has suspended all flights as it rushes to resolve what it warned is a critical financial situation.

The airline said if no solution can be found, it intends to file for bankruptcy.

The airline uses a fleet of 12 Boeing 787 aircraft on long-haul routes from a number of European airports, including London Gatwick, Rome and Oslo.

Prior to the suspension of flights, it was advertising services from London to Orlando, Cape Town, Bangkok and Phuket.

One aircraft was meant to depart London for Orlando this morning, while another was meant to arrive from Cape Town this evening.

The suspension has also affected Pakistan International Airlines, which had been leasing aircraft and crews from Norse Atlantic.

PIA was forced to cancel services from London to Islamabad and from Manchester to Lahore last night.

In a statement on social media, PIA said all UK flights from today would be operated by aircraft from its own fleet.

Norse Atlantic Airways was set up in 2021 as a low-cost long-haul carrier.

It entered the market as a successor to Norwegian, which withdrew from long haul routes as a result of the Covid pandemic.

But it has struggled to make money, and its problems worsened this year, as fuel prices rocketed due to the war in Iran.

Unlike many other European carriers, Norse Atlantic does not hedge its fuel bills by buying supplies in advance at fixed prices.

This left it fully exposed when prices soared, with the cost of fuel roughly doubling at one point. Prices remain significantly higher than they were before the conflict began.

In the first half of the year Norse Atlantic made a loss of $94.6m.

In a statement to the Oslo Stock Exchange on Wednesday, the airline said its financial situation was critical, and it needed to find short term funding to continue its operations.

After suspending flights, the company said it was in discussions with investors regarding a possible takeover that "would include a financing solution".

However, it said if short term funding could not be found quickly, "it is the Board's intention to file for bankruptcy".

If Norse Atlantic were to collapse, it would be another major setback for the low-cost long-haul model, which has typically proved popular with passengers but difficult to sustain financially, especially on transatlantic routes.

MN202611_hfwrlpoycb.t:
Banki Nkuru y’u Rwanda (BNR) yatangaje ko kugeza mu mpera za Kamena 2026 yari ifite zahabu zingana na toni imwe, zifite agaciro k’amadolari ya Amerika agera kuri miliyoni 200, mu rwego rwo kongera ubwoko bw’ishoramari bugize umutungo wayo w’amadevize.

Guverineri wa BNR, Soraya Hakuziyaremye, yavuze ko gushora imari muri zahabu byatangiye mu mwaka w’ingengo y’imari warangiye muri Kamena 2026, bikaba byari mu murongo w’intego yari yashyizweho yo kutarenza 10% by’umutungo w’amadevize w’igihugu ushorwa muri zahabu.

Yagize ati: “Ibyo twari dufite muri zahabu byari bifite agaciro k’amadolari agera kuri miliyoni 200, kandi byari bihuye n’intego yacu ya mbere yo kutarenza 10% by’umutungo w’amadevize mu ishoramari muri zahabu. Inyungu twabonye zari nyinshi cyane.”

Yongeyeho ko inyungu yavuye muri iryo shoramari yagize uruhare mu gusobanura impuzandengo y’inyungu BNR yagaragaje muri raporo y’umwaka, ndetse n’inyungu yatangaje ko izasubizwa Leta nk’inyungu igenewe umuturage binyuze mu misoro.

Umuyobozi ushinzwe amasoko n’imari muri BNR, Boniface Mutabazi, yemeje ko mu mpera za Kamena 2026 banki yari ifite toni imwe ya zahabu, ni ukuvuga ibiro 1.000.

Ishoramari muri zahabu ni bumwe mu buryo banki nkuru z’ibihugu zikoresha mu kubika no kurinda agaciro k’umutungo wabyo w’amadevize, cyane cyane mu gihe isoko mpuzamahanga ry’imari n’ivunjisha rihindagurika.

BNR yatangiye gushora imari muri zahabu muri Nyakanga 2025, mu rwego rwo kongera ubwoko bw’imitungo igize umutungo w’amadevize w’u Rwanda no kuwurinda ihindagurika ry’amasoko mpuzamahanga.

MN202611_y8bqoc3o2y.t:
Fifa has confirmed it has been the victim of a cyber attack which resulted in personal and business information being stolen.

However, BBC Sport understands the data breach did not include any documents relating to the controversial Fifa Forward Enterprise proposal, president Gianni Infantino's failed World Cup sell-off plot.

Football Association chair Debbie Hewitt was this week granted access to the files upon condition of signing a non-disclosure agreement.

It is understood not to be a systems or technology failure at the world football governing body, with criminals able to gain access to the documents by impersonating and taking advantage of staff.

"Fifa can confirm that it has been the victim of a criminal cyber-attack resulting in unauthorised access to a limited set of personal and business information," Fifa said in a statement.

"Fifa is working closely with the relevant authorities, including law enforcement.

"Fifa condemns in the strongest possible terms the unlawful acquisition and publication of information, particularly personal data.

"Such actions constitute a serious and unacceptable violation of privacy and can have significant consequences for the individuals concerned."

Responsibility has been claimed online by a group called the Handsome Boy Hacking Club, which last week posted screenshots of Fifa files.

The group claims to have gained access to 12GB of data. Analysis indicates this is less than 0.1% of all data held by Fifa and was targeted at the company rather than individuals.

Iki cyemezo cyafashwe na Komite ishinzwe Politiki y’Ifaranga muri BNR (Monetary Policy Committee), ishingiye ku isesengura ryerekanye ko izamuka ry’ibiciro rikomeje kuba ikibazo, nubwo ubukungu bw’u Rwanda bukomeje kwihagararaho ku rwego mpuzamahanga.

Mu kiganiro n’itangazamakuru kuri uyu wa Kane, Guverineri wa BNR Soraya Hakuziyaremye, yavuze ko izamuka ry’ibiciro rikomeje guterwa ahanini n’ibiribwa bishya, mu gihe n’ibiciro by’ingufu ku masoko mpuzamahanga bikomeje kuzamuka bitewe n’umwuka mubi wa politiki n’intambara mu Burasirazuba bwo Hagati, by’umwihariko ingaruka ku bucuruzi n’ingendo z’ibicuruzwa.

Yagaragaje ko ibiciro by’ingufu ku rwego mpuzamahanga biteganyijwe kuzamukaho impuzandengo ya 32% mu 2026, mu gihe ibiciro by’ibicuruzwa bitari ingufu, birimo ibiribwa, biteganyijwe kuzamukaho 9%. Ibiciro by’ibiribwa byonyine biteganyijwe kuzamukaho impuzandengo ya 10% muri uyu mwaka na 7,2% mu 2027.

Iri zamuka rifitanye isano n’izamuka ry’ibiciro by’ifumbire n’ikiguzi cy’ubwikorezi, na byo byiyongera bitewe n’izamuka ry’ibikomoka kuri peteroli.

BNR igaragaza ko nubwo ibiciro ku rwego mpuzamahanga bikomeje kuzamuka, ihungabana ry’ifaranga ry’u Rwanda ugereranyije n’idolari rya Amerika ryagabanutse.

Mu mezi icyenda ya mbere ya 2026, agaciro k’ifaranga ry’u Rwanda kamanutseho 1,4% ugereranyije n’idolari, ugereranyije na 4% ryari ryatakaje mu gihe nk’icyo mu mwaka ushize. Guverineri yavuze ko ari igipimo cyo guta agaciro kw’ifaranga kiri hasi kurusha ibindi mu myaka itanu ishize.

Yavuze ko byatewe n’izamuka ry’amafaranga yoherezwa mu Rwanda n’Abanyarwanda baba mu mahanga, ishoramari rituruka hanze, ubwiyongere bw’amafaranga igihugu cyinjiza mu mahanga binyuze mu bicuruzwa byoherezwayo, ndetse n’ivugurura ryakozwe mu micungire y’ivunjisha ry’amafaranga ryatangiye mu 2025.

Ibi byafashije kugabanya ingaruka z’izamuka ry’ibiciro by’ibicuruzwa bitumizwa mu mahanga ku bukungu bw’u Rwanda.

Mu gihembwe cya gatatu cya 2026, ibyoherezwa mu mahanga byiyongereyeho 61,7% ugereranyije n’igihe nk’icyo mu mwaka wabanje, mu gihe ibitumizwa mu mahanga byiyongereyeho 19,5%. Ibyo byatumye icyuho hagati y’ibyo u Rwanda rwohereza mu mahanga n’ibyo rutumizayo kigabanukaho 7,4%.

Ku bijyanye n’ubukungu bw’imbere mu gihugu, Guverineri yavuze ko umusaruro mbumbe w’u Rwanda (GDP) wazamutseho 9,4% mu gihembwe cya kabiri cya 2026 ugereranyije n’igihe nk’icyo mu mwaka ushize.

Yavuze ko nubwo imibare y’umusaruro mbumbe w’igihembwe cya gatatu itari yatangazwa, icyegeranyo cya BNR gikurikirana ibikorwa by’ubukungu cyagaragaje izamuka rya 16%, bigaragaza ko ibikorwa by’ubukungu byakomeje kwiyongera.

Iri zamuka ryatewe ahanini n’urwego rwa serivisi n’inganda, cyane cyane ubwubatsi, ubucuruzi, ubwikorezi na serivisi z’imari. Icyakora, ubuhinzi bwazamutse ku kigero kiri munsi y’icyari cyitezwe, bikaba biri mu byagize ingaruka ku izamuka ry’ibiciro by’ibiribwa.

Nubwo ubukungu bwakomeje kwiyongera, ibiciro byakomeje kuzamuka. Mu gihembwe cya gatatu cya 2026, izamuka rusange ry’ibiciro ryageze kuri 15,8% ku mpuzandengo y’amezi atatu y’icyo gihembwe. Mu Ukwakira 2026, ryageze kuri 19,5%, rivuye kuri 17,2% mu mezi yabanje.

Iri zamuka ryatewe ahanini n’ibiribwa bishya, ibiciro byabyo byazamutse bigera hafi kuri 40% mu Ukwakira. Ibiciro by’ibindi bicuruzwa na serivisi bitari ibiribwa n’ingufu byo byari kuri 11,5%.

BNR ivuga ko izamuka ry’ibiciro rishobora gukomeza guterwa n’ingaruka z’ikirere cya El Niño, zatinze ibikorwa byo gutera imyaka mu gihembwe cy’ihinga A, bikaba bishobora kugira ingaruka ku musaruro w’ubuhinzi. Indi mbogamizi ni intambara yo mu Burasirazuba bwo Hagati, ishobora gutuma ibiciro bya peteroli ku rwego mpuzamahanga birushaho kuzamuka.

Uretse kuzamura inyungu fatizo ikagera ku 9,5%, Komite ishinzwe Politiki y’Ifaranga yanemeje ko amafaranga amabanki asabwa kubika muri BNR azamurwa akava kuri 5% akagera kuri 7%.

Icyo cyemezo kigamije kugabanya amafaranga menshi ashobora kuba ari mu mabanki, bityo bikarinda ko ubwiyongere bwayo bwongera umuvuduko w’izamuka ry’ibiciro.

Guverineri yavuze ko kuzamura inyungu fatizo bigamije kugarura izamuka ry’ibiciro ku kigero cya 5% mu gihe gito, mu rwego rwo kubungabunga agaciro k’ifaranga no kurinda ubushobozi bw’Abanyarwanda bwo kugura ibicuruzwa na serivisi.

BNR iteganya ko izamuka rusange ry’ibiciro rizagenda rigabanuka, rikagera ku kigero cyemewe kiri hagati ya 2% na 8% guhera mu gihembwe cya kabiri cya 2027.

Yavuze ko BNR izakomeza gukurikirana uko ibiciro n’ubukungu bihagaze, ikaba yiteguye gufata izindi ngamba mu gihe izamuka ry’ibiciro ryakomeza kurenga ku byo yari yateganyije.

MN202611_1n5extd7ua7.t:
Over-70s will have to take eye tests every three years or face losing their driving licence under new road safety plans.

Mandatory eyesight tests are part of the Department for Transport's (DfT) road safety strategy, expected within weeks.

Around 6.5 million over-70s hold drivers' licences, with 1.6 million of those aged 80 or over.

To drive legally in the UK, you must be able to read a standard number plate from 20 metres away, wearing glasses or contact lenses if required.

Government sources told the BBC ministers will recommend over-70s be made to regularly prove their eyesight meets the minimum standards. Those who do not, or who fail to meet the minimum standard face losing their licence.

The change follows a consultation which launched early last year , set to recommend a shake-up of the rules for older drivers.

Under the current rules, over 70s have to renew their licence every three years, but only have to self-certify that their sight.

Dennis Reed, of campaign group Silver Voices, which represents older people, said it was "discriminatory to just pick an age out of the hat and say 'everybody over 70 has to go through this, but nobody else does'".

But he said the group is not opposed in principle to regular eye tests for older drivers.

The changes being considered were first reported by the Daily Mail , external .

Drivers over 70 to face eye tests every three years

The NHS provides free eye tests for over 60s, but they are not detailed enough to approve someone to drive.

The BBC understands this system is also being looked at, with the free tests likely to be expanded to become more rigorous.

A Government source said "beefed up measures" were long overdue.

"One life lost on the roads is one too many," they added. "There have been several arguably preventable fatalities on Britain's roads caused by drivers with failing eyesight in recent years.

The DfT said no decision has officially been made on mandating eyesight tests for drivers aged 70 and over.

A spokesperson said: "We recognise the importance of driving for older people's independence but need to balance this with our priority to keep everyone safe on our roads and avoid tragic accidents.

"Mandatory eye tests for drivers over 70 as part of our Road Safety Strategy are one way to do this.

"We are carefully reviewing consultation results," they added. "Older drivers who are fit to drive and have good enough vision have nothing to worry about."

MN202611_vz3mnbe4jp.t:
Minisiteri y’Uburinganire n’Iterambere ry’Umuryango (MIGEPROF), yagaragaje ko nubwo u Rwanda rumaze gutera intambwe ishimishije mu gushyiraho politiki, amategeko, inzego na serivisi bigamije gukumira no kurwanya ihohotera rishingiye ku gitsina ndetse no gufasha abarikorewe, ariko hakiri imbogamizi zishingiye ku myumvire n’imigenzereze ishimangira ubusumbane hagati y’abagore n’abagabo.

Izi kandi ziyongeraho izindi zishingiye ku myumvire ipfobya ikanihanganira ihohotera hamwe n’imyumvire ituma abana batabona amakuru n’uburere bibafasha kwirinda, kuko hakigaragara umuco wo guceceka no guhishira abakora ibyaha.

Ibi ni bimwe mu byatangajwe n’ubuyobozi bw’iyo Minisiteri kuri uyu wa 25 Ugushyingo 2026, ubwo hatangizwaga ubukangurambaga bw’iminsi 16 yahariwe gukumira no kurwanya ihohotera rishingiye ku gitsina.

Ni ubukangurambaga bufite insanganyamatsiko igira iti “Speak Out! Prevent Child Defilement”, ugenekereje mu Kinyarwanda bishatse kuvuga ngo “Wiceceka! rwanya icyaha cyo gusambanya abana.”

Imibare y’Ikigo cy’Igihugu cy’Ibarurishamibare igaragaza ko abangavu batewe inda hagati ya 2020-2025 bavuye kuri 5% bakagera kuri 8%, mu gihe iya Minisiteri y’Ubuzima igaragaza ko nibura abangavu bagera kuri 60 baterwa inda buri munsi.

Ubwo yari mu nama nyunguranabitekerezo itangiza ubu bukangurambaga, agendeye kuri iyi mibare, Minisiteri w’Uburinganire n’Iterambere ry’Umuryango, Consolee Uwimana, yavuze ko ihangayikishije, cyane kuko inyuma yayo, hari abangavu bahura n’ihungabana, abatereranwa, abahagarika amashuri n’abisanga mu nshingano zo kurera kandi na bo bari bagikeneye kurerwa.

Yagize ati “Buri mwana usambanyijwe, ni ubuzima buhungabanyijwe, ni icyizere gikomerekejwe, ni inzozi n’ejo hazaza hashyizwe mu kaga. Abana n’abandi bahohotewe, tubatege amatwi, tubashishikarize gutanga amakuru ku nzego zibishinzwe, no kudaterwa ubwoba cyangwa gushukwa ngo bareke kuvuga ibyababayeho.”

Aha kandi Minisitiri yanagaragaje ko ababyeyi n’abarezi, bakwiye kumenya no kwita ku mibereho y’abana babo, bakabaganiriza, babereka urukundo ari na ko babarinda aho bari hose.

Ati “Abaturanyi ntitukirengagize amakuru cyangwa ibimenyetso by’ihohotera. Aho turikeka dutange amakuru ku nzego zibishinzwe. Abagabo n’abahungu, ni mube ku isonga mu guhindura imyumvire n’imyitwarire ibangamira umutekano w’abagore n’abana. Inzego z’ibanze, iz’ubuzima, iz’umutekano n’ubutabera, zitange ubufasha bwihuse,bwuzuye kandi bwubahiriza uburenganzira n’icyubahiro by’uwahohotewe.”

Ruswa ishingiye ku gitsina ni ikibazo gikomeje kugaragara mu nzego zitandukanye zirimo n’amashuri makuru na za kaminuza mu Rwanda, aho bamwe mu bafite inshingano zo kwigisha no gusuzuma abanyeshuri bakekwaho gukoresha ububasha bafite mu gutanga amanota kugira ngo basabe abanyeshuri kubaha ibyo bakeneye bishingiye ku gitsina.

Ubushakashatsi bwakozwe n’Umuryango urwanya ruswa, akarengane no guharanira iyimikazwa ry’imiyoborere myiza mu Rwanda (Transparency International Rwanda/TIR), bugaragaza ko amashuri makuru ari mu nzego zugarijwe n’iki kibazo, kikabangamira uburenganzira bw’abanyeshuri ku burezi no kubona amanota ashingiye ku bumenyi bafite.

Umuyobozi Nshingwabikorwa wa TIR, Apollinaire Mupiganyi, yagaragaje ko amashuri makuru na za kaminuza bikwiye kongera ubukangurambaga no gushyiraho uburyo bwizewe abanyeshuri n'abatangabuhamya bashobora kunyuramo batanga amakuru ku ihohoterwa na ruswa ishingiye ku gitsina.

Yagize ati: “Abanyeshuri bagomba kwizezwa ko ibirego byabo bizumvwa, bigafatwa nk'iby'ingenzi kandi bigakurikiranwa, aho kubihinyura, kubasuzugura cyangwa kubikoresha mu kubahima.”

Marie Goreth Nizigama, Uhagarariye UN Women mu Rwanda, yagaragaje ko u Rwanda ari intangarugero n’icyitegererezo ku mahanga mu bikorwa byinshi bitandukanye, asaba ko hakorwa ibishoboka byose kugira ngo ikibazo cy’ihohotera rishingiye ku gitsina gifatirwe umwanzuro.

Ati “Nibaza ko natwe nk’abafite uburinganire mu nshingano turi hano, n’izindi nzego aho ziri, twakomeza gukorera hamwe, kuko nta kuntu Igihugu cyaba gifite icyerekezo n’impinduka mu bukungu, kikayobora Afurika, ariko ibyo bintu bigakomeza.”

Mu Rwanda, Itegeko Nº 54/2018 ryo ku wa 13 Kanama 2018 ryerekeye kurwanya ruswa rihana ruswa ishingiye ku gitsina, aho uhamijwe icyaha ashobora gukatirwa igifungo kiri hagati y'imyaka itanu n'icumi.

Nubwo hariho amategeko ayikumira, raporo ya Transparency International igaragaza ko gukurikirana no guhana abayikora bikiri imbogamizi, kuko ibirego by'iyi ruswa bitagaragara cyane mu byaha bikunze kurangira abaregwa bahanwe.

Iyi minsi 16 yatangijwe none, izarangwa n’ubukangurambaga bugamije gukumira no kurwanya ihohotera rishingiye ku gitsina, buzakorerwa ahantu hatandukanye harimo mu mashuri mu nsengero hakazatangwa n’ubutumwa bugenewe abaturage muri rusange.

Mu biganiro bizatangwa hazibandwa cyane ku ngingo zirimo gusobanura icyo umwana ari cyo, igihe gusambanya umwana bivugirwa, icyo gusambanya umwana ari cyo, impamvu zitera isambanywa ry’abana, n’ingaruka ziterwa n’ihohotera rishingiye ku gitsina n’irikorerwa umwana.

MN202611_6qcipq5f6k.t:
Lenacapavir has received WHO's approval for HIV prevention

Uganda is set to receive its first supplies of a cheaper version of a ground-breaking injection to prevent HIV, raising hopes of expanding access to the drug across Africa, where the burden of the disease remains highest.

The first global shipment of the generic drug, known as lenacapavir, arrived in Zambia on Wednesday, with deliveries to Uganda expected in the coming days, the Global Fund has said.

The drug, administered as an injection twice a year, is nearly 100% effective at preventing HIV infection and is expected to cost just $40 (£30) per person annually.

Zimbabwe is due to receive supplies early next year, with several other countries expected to follow.

The arrival of the generic drug comes just a year after the original version, developed by US pharmaceutical giant Gilead Sciences, became available in sub-Saharan Africa.

The original version cost about about $28,000 annually in the US, putting it beyond the reach of many of those in developing countries.

Focus on Africa podcast: Lenacapavir offering new hope for HIV prevention?

Landmark deal paves way for cheaper HIV protection jab

Lenacapavir works by targeting the protective protein shell of HIV, disrupting the virus's ability to multiply and establish an infection in the body.

In a landmark clinical trial involving more than 5,000 adolescent girls and young women in Uganda and South Africa in 2024, none of those who received the injection contracted HIV.

Health experts say the injection offers a major advantage over existing HIV prevention pills, known as pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP), which must be taken every day and can carry social stigma.

The World Health Organization (WHO) recommended the drug for HIV prevention in July 2025 .

The Global Fund described the arrival of the drug in Africa as a "major breakthrough" in the fight against HIV, saying cheaper supplies would help reach millions more people at risk of infection.

"These deliveries mark an unprecedented acceleration and expansion in access to a highly effective, quality-assured generic HIV prevention medicine in low- and middle-income settings," the group said in a statement on Wednesday.

More than 189,000 people across 10 countries have already received their first injection of lenacapavir, according to the Global Fund.

The organisation expects 24 countries to have received supplies by the end of this year and, working with the US government, plans to reach at least three million people by the end of 2028.

It is eventually expected to be available in 120 low- and middle-income countries.

Sub-Saharan Africa accounts for nearly two-thirds of people living with HIV globally, with adolescent girls and young women disproportionately affected.

South Africa has the world's largest HIV-positive population, with nearly eight million people living with the virus. It is among the countries expected to receive the cheaper injection.

Some 41 million people worldwide were living with HIV last year, while 570,000 died from HIV-related illnesses, according to the WHO.

The rollout comes amid concerns that sweeping cuts to US foreign aid under President Donald Trump's administration could undermine decades of progress in tackling HIV in Africa, where many countries rely heavily on international funding for prevention and treatment.

The UN aims to end Aids as a public health threat by 2030.

MN202611_1h64kj4wvbi.t:
The National Bank of Rwanda (BNR) has raised its benchmark interest rate by 75 basis points to 9.5%, marking its highest level since 2009 as monetary authorities step up efforts to contain rising inflation.

The new rate, announced on November 26, 2026, represents an increase from 8.75%, where it had remained for the previous three months.

The adjustment is equivalent to a 0.75-percentage-point increase.

The decision takes the benchmark rate above the 9% threshold for the first time in 17 years, reflecting growing concerns over inflationary pressures and their impact on household purchasing power and business operating costs.

Inflation has continued to accelerate, with the Consumer Price Index (CPI) rising by 19.5% year-on-year in October, compared with 17.2% in September, according to the National Institute of Statistics of Rwanda (NISR).

Food and non-alcoholic beverage prices recorded an annual increase of 28.9%, while transport costs rose by 22.4%. Housing, water, electricity, gas and other fuels increased by 14.2%, adding to the pressure on household budgets.

The central bank’s medium-term inflation target is 5%, meaning the October urban inflation rate was 14.5 percentage points above that objective.

The latest increase extends a monetary tightening cycle that has seen the benchmark rate rise considerably throughout 2026. It stood at 7.25% in February, increased to 8.25% in May and reached 8.75% in August before the latest adjustment to 9.5%.

The central bank uses its benchmark rate to influence borrowing costs, credit demand and spending across the economy. Raising the rate generally makes borrowing more expensive for commercial banks, businesses and individuals, while encouraging savings.

The measure is intended to moderate demand and help bring inflation under control. However, higher interest rates can also increase the cost of loans for businesses seeking financing and households servicing variable-rate borrowing.

The latest decision therefore comes at a time when policymakers face the challenge of controlling rising prices while maintaining economic growth and supporting investment.

MN202611_kbzj8jsfpd.t:
DJ Ralph Lawson rediscovered a tape that Daft Punk gifted him in 1997

Daft Punk have become household names after storming the charts with One More Time and Get Lucky - with an intimate set in 1990s Leeds lingering in the memories of attendees. Now, those recollections have been reignited by the discovery of a lost mix by the French electronic duo hidden for several decades.

"It all started when I opened a show for Daft Punk in 1997," says Ralph Lawson, standing on the top floor of the Mint XL club in the city centre.

The 2,500-capacity venue is empty aside from staff testing out a staggering number of lights, bouncing off the spotless floors.

It is a far cry from Ralph's first clubs when he started DJing back in 1991.

He is a co-founding resident DJ at the legendary Back to Basics club - a DIY house music event that became one of Europe's longest-running club nights, hosting global stars until sunrise.

Mint evolved from an intimate Leeds club into festivals, large-scale productions and the new Mint XL club

Ralph is holding up a digital audio tape (DAT) - a discontinued method of recording high quality audio. On its side are the handwritten words: "Daft Punk Mix Feb '97."

"Daft Punk got so big so quickly, they were on such big stages at festivals that they did not really DJ," remembers the music producer.

The French pair were rapidly rising to fame when they were booked for Back to Basics, but they were pipped to the headline slot by drum and bass pioneer Goldie.

Daft Punk were on their rapid rise to stardom when they visited Leeds in 1997, but did not top the bill

By the time the night arrived, Ralph recalls "there were queues around the block".

Despite accidentally jogging one of their records during the set, Ralph got on well with both Thomas Bangalter and Guy-Manuel de Homem-Christo - even if the latter only uttered a few words to him.

"I would not say I was best mates with them, but I could get on a guest list," says Ralph.

Whatever their relationship, it was strong enough that Daft Punk sent Ralph a gift in the post - an hour-long mixtape for his radio show on Kiss 105 FM.

This is the only picture Ralph has of Daft Punk playing their DJ set in Leeds

After it was played out on air, Ralph forgot about its existence for decades. He finally rediscovered it during a root around in some old storage boxes, but there was a problem.

"I took it out and there were two bits of tape hanging out."

Despite being in a dry studio, mould had found its way in.

When Ralph tried to play the tape it immediately ripped

Spurred on by his social media followers begging for him to salvage the mix, Ralph found a company that preserves tapes in Bristol.

"The problem with DAT is that it is incredibly fragile," says Adrian Finn, from Greatbear, one of the people tasked with fixing the broken tape.

He estimates the team spent hours across multiple weeks on this "difficult job", carefully disassembling the tape, repairing the rips and getting rid of the mould.

"It's nice to make people happy through this kind of restoration work," says Adrian, who admits he was dancing around "a little bit" while listening back to the mix.

"I thought it was good and glad it played back with hardly any errors."

Adrian Finn from Greatbear in Bristol was one of the people tasked with fixing the mixtape

Back at Mint XL in Leeds, Ralph cannot help but grin as he recounts attempting to play the mix for a second time.

"I was literally floored," he laughs, toppling over in delight once the kick drum blasted out of his speakers.

Ralph had no idea what the first track of the hour-long mix would be, so when it was one of his favourites - Everybody Dancing by the late American DJ Romanthony - he knew it would be "very special".

Ralph dropped to the floor in celebration when he heard the tape for the first time

It is the "rawness" of the vinyl mix - complete with crackles and impressive manual transitions - that Ralph adores.

"It's a testament to the times," he says.

"Not as polished as things are now, where people can see precisely how in time they are and have visual cues."

While the discovery may be a success for the nostalgia and memories of 1990s clubbing, Ralph also hopes the tape and the meaning behind it will inspire the next generation of DJs, music curators and artists.

"I want them to think, 'I could get behind the decks or find the next Daft Punk and put them on at our night', and there's the space for them to do that in Leeds."

Will another French electronic music duo stop by in Leeds on their way to global stardom? Who knows.

But producers like Ralph are adamant that the city's famous club scene can easily foster many more like them.

MN202611_xg833qtt1w.t:
U Rwanda rwakiriye Abanyarwanda 106 biganjemo abana n’abagore bari bamaze igihe baba mu mashyamba ya Repubulika Iharanira Demokarasi ya Congo (RDC), bavuga ko bari barambiwe ubuzima bushaririye bari babayemo muri icyo gihugu.

Abakiriwe banyuze ku mupaka wa Rusizi I, kuri uyu wa Kane tariki ya 26 Ugushyingo 2026, bakaba bagizwe n’abagore 28 hamwe n’abana 78, biganjemo abavukiyeyo n’abandi bagiye bakiri bato.

Mu buhamya batanze bakigera mu Rwanda, bavuze ko muri RDC bari babayeho nabi mu buzima bwo kutiga n'inzara, ku buryo n’imyenda bambutse bambaye ari iyo bahawe mbere y’uko bambuka umupaka kugira ngo bahagere nibura basa neza.

Muhoza Arankunda, utahanye umuryango w’abantu umunani, avuga ko iwabo bahungiye muri icyo gihugu ari muto kuko bamujyanye bamuhetse, gusa ngo kuva yahagera nta buzima bwiza yigeze ahagirira, kubera ko n’aho umugabo yagiye gukorera mu bucukuzi bw’amabuye y’agaciro yaguyeyo.

Ati “Kuva 1994 mama akingeza muri RDC, twabaga mu nkambi, ndakura maze gukura njya gushaka, ariko tubaho mu buzima bw’intambara ugasanga n’ijoro barakwinjiriye bakakujyana, bakakwiba. Mabukwe ni we wambwiye ngo ni nzane abana, none nsanze mu Rwanda ari heza cyane, abana baziga n’ubuzima bwo gukora burahari. Nakwifuriza bene mama basigayeyo ngo bose batahe.”

Uwase Gasigwa w’imyaka 28, avuga ko ubuzima bari babayemo bwari bugoye kuko bahoraga biruka.

Yagize ati “Twahoraga turi kwiruka, twaba turi nka Inumbi tukumva ngo bageze iyo ruguru, tukaba turamanutse tukajya ahitwa i Gisongati, tugahora muri ubwo buzima bwo kwirikanka. Jye najyaga kwikorera injerekani y’amata nkayikura ahitwa i Gisongati nkayigeza i Karemi bakampa amafaranga 2,000. Abasigayeyo nabagira inama yo kugira ishyaka ryo gutaha kuko mu Rwanda mbonye ari ahantu heza cyane.”

Icyo abenshi bahurizaho ni uko batagize amahirwe yo kwiga, ku buryo n’abagize amahirwe yo kugera mu ishuri bagarukiye mu wa 2 w’amashuri abanza.

Bakimara kwambuka umupaka wa Rusizi I, bakiriwe n’inzego zitandukanye zirimo inzego bwite za Leta hamwe n’abandi bafite aho bahuriye no kwita ku mpunzi, babaha ikaze hamwe n’ubutumwa bw’ihumure.

Umuyobozi w’Akarere ka Rusizi, Phanuel Sindayiheba, yavuze ko abenshi mu batashye ari abahunze Igihugu nyuma ya Jenoside yakorewe Abatutsi, bagiye batwarwa n’Interahamwe hamwe na X-FAR, bakaba bari bamaze igihe bafite amakuru y’ibihuha ku Rwanda ari nabyo byababuzaga gutaha.

Nubwo benshi mu batashye bafite abana batagize amahirwe yo kujya ku ishuri, Umuyobozi w’Akarere ka Rusizi, yavuze ko bimwe mu by’ibanze bagomba gufashwa birimo ko abana babo bagomba kujya ku ishuri.

Yagize ati “Abana bavukiye mu buzima bubi, ntibabashije kujya kwiga, ariko bakimara kugera hano, turabafasha iby’ibanze kandi kuko tukiri mu gihembwe cya mbere cy’amashuri, bazafashwa kujya mu ishuri na bo bige nk’abandi Banyarwanda.”

Abatashye biyemeje kubwiza ukuri abo basizeyo by’umwihariko abagabo, kuko basanze mu Rwanda ari amahoro, kandi Igihugu cyiyubatse, kandi cyifuza ineza y’Umunyarwanda wese, kugira ngo na bo batahe bafatanye n’abandi kwiyubakira Igihugu.

Abanyarwanda batahutse bavuye muri RDC, babanza guhabwa ubufasha bw’ibanze mbere yo gusubizwa mu miryango no mu turere bakomokamo. Ibyo bakorerwa birimo kubandikisha, kubaha aho bacumbika by’agateganyo, kwita ku buzima bwabo no kubafasha kubona ibyangombwa bibafasha gusubira mu buzima busanzwe.

Bajyanwa mu bigo byakira abatahutse, birimo Nyarushishi mu Karere ka Rusizi na Kijote mu Karere ka Nyabihu, aho bacumbikirwa mu gihe hategurwa kubasubiza mu miryango yabo.

Muri rusange kuva muri Mutarama 2025, Abanyarwanda bamaze gutaha bava muri RDC baragera ku 10,000 biganjemo abagore n’abana bagiye bataha mu byiciro bitandukanye banyuze ku mipaka irimo La Corniche, Rusizi I hamwe na Bugarama.

MN202611_1b0tb41d3z3.t:
Guverineri wa Banki nkuru y’igihugu (BNR) Soraya Hakuziyaremye, yagiranye ikiganiro n’abanyamakuru kuri uyu wa Kane tariki 26 Ugushyingo 2026, agaragaza uko politiki y’ifaranga ihagaze, uko igipimo cy’inyungu fatizo (Central Bank Rate - CBR) cyazamutse kikagera kuri 9.5% kivuye kuri 8.75%, uko ubukungu bw’u Rwanda buhagaze muri rusange, ariko avuga no ku biciro bya peteroli ndetse n’ibiciro by’ibiribwa ku isoko.

Ku bijyanye n’ibiciro bya Peteroli, ari nabyo bikunze gutuma ibiciro by’ibindi bicuruzwa ku isoko bizamuka, Guverineri wa BNR yavuze nubwo intambara yo muri Iran itararangira kandi ari nayo yatumye ibiciro bya Peteroli bizamuka ku isoko mpuzamahanga, ariko kubera ko u Rwanda rwakoze ibishoboka rugashyiramo nkunganire, ibiciro by’ibikomoka kuri Peteroli mu Rwanda ngo byagumye hamwe ntibyakomeza kuzamuka muri aya mezi atandatu ashize.

Ku biciro by’ibiribwa ku isoko, Guverineri Hakuziyaremye Soraya avuga ko byazamutse ahanini bitewe n’uko ibihembwe by’ihinga bishize bitagenze neza, kubera ko imvura yaguye itinze cyane, ugereranyije n’uko byari biteganyijwe, ariko ashimangira ko hari icyizere ko isarura niritangira, n’ibiciro by’ibiribwa ku isoko bizahita bitangira kugabanuka.

Yagize ati,” Ikirimo gukorwa kugira ngo uyu muvuduko w’ibiciro ugabanuke, icya mbere ni ukugabanya umuvuduko w’izamuka ry’ibiciro ku biribwa.Tuzi ko byatewe cyane cyane n’uko umusaruro w’urwego rw’ubuhinzi utari uhagije nk’uko twabiteganyije dutangiriye kuri ‘season A’ y’umwaka cyangwa ibihembwe by’ihinga byakurikiyeho, turabona ko kubera n’ihindagurika ry’ikirere,nanone imvura ntabwo yatangiye kugwa ku gihe ngo iyi ‘season A’ tuvuga ko izagenda neza,ariko ikigaragara ni uko Leta yashyize imbaraga nyinshi mu kugira ngo umuhinzi ashobore kubonera ifumbire ku gihe kandi itamuhenze cyane nubwo igiciro cyayo kiyongereye cyane ku masoko mpuzamahanga”.

“Hari kandi no kuba guhera mu kwezi kwa Gatandatu, mubona ko ibiciro by’ibikomoka kuri peteroli ku isoko ry’u Rwanda bitazamutse kubera ya nkunganire Leta ikomeza gushyiramo,ibyo nabyo biba bifashije kugira ngo igiciro cy’ubwikorezi kidakomeza kwiyongera cyane, bikiyongera kuri cya giciro cy’ibiribwa, ku buryo twizera ko, ubwo umusaruro uzaboneka gutangira mu kwezi kwa 12 kurangira, ukwa mbere n’ukwa Kabiri (2027), tuzabona ko ibiciro by’ibiribwa,bizatangira kugabanuka, ari nayo mpamvu twerekanye ko twizeye ko umuvuduko w’izamuka ry’ibiciro guhera mu gice cya Kabiri cy’umwaka utaha, ari ho tuzabona ko uwo muvuduko uzaba wagarutse ku kigero gisanzwe…”.

MN202611_1ifrcsek998.t:
The BBC said it is "determined to ensure the BBC is a place where everyone can be themselves and feel accepted"

The government's antisemitism adviser has launched an investigation into the BBC over allegations of a "hostile work environment" for Jews.

Lord Mann told BBC Radio 4's Today programme he had decided to open the investigation "because there seems to be a growing feeling of discomfort among Jewish staff".

He said: "If that's true, and that's what I'm going to attempt to find out, and if that is widespread, then that's a really serious problem that has to be addressed. And I don't hear and see that being addressed, and at a senior level."

The BBC said it takes "any and all allegations of discrimination extremely seriously – there is no place for it at the BBC".

The corporation said it had introduced compulsory antisemitism training for all staff, and said "we actively encourage colleagues to report any incidences or concerns they have".

The BBC statement added that it is "determined to ensure the BBC is a place where everyone can be themselves and feel accepted".

Lord Mann, who was appointed by former Prime Minister Theresa May as an independent adviser on antisemitism in 2019 , external , said anyone contacting him would have "total anonymity guaranteed".

"I have no agenda against the BBC," he told Today, calling himself "an entirely blank sheet of paper".

"Some of the things that I'm being told have been quite disturbing sometimes, how little the senior manager of the BBC seem to get it, and so I'm opening this up," he said.

"Look, there is a problem. The question is - is the problem just a few people? Is it a problem that's easily solved? But if it's an institutional problem, that's much deeper and more difficult to solve. It may be. I'll report the facts."

The former MP said he had previously "made suggestions" to the corporation after he had "repeatedly met" Jewish staff.

He said the things "the BBC has done to try and sort things out have not worked".

His agenda was "ensuring the BBC meets its charter obligations", saying "people are fearful... of expressing their concerns internally, that's the problem".

Lord Mann's remit as the government's independent adviser on antisemitism includes "to engage proactively with the Jewish community and institutions".

He said he plans to have his investigation "totally completed and reported to the BBC and the government before Easter".

He previously conducted a review into antisemitism and racism in the NHS , which was commissioned by the health secretary and which reported in June.

The Guardian recently reported , external that BBC deputy director general Rhodri Talfan Davies said he did not accept that an independent inquiry into antisemitism was needed.

"We have very, very robust processes – we review them regularly," he told members of the Broadcasting Press Guild earlier this month.

"Of course in any large organisation there can be instances of discrimination, which you deal with when they arise, but there is no evidence of any systemic issue within the BBC that would merit anything like that.

"I don't believe there is institutional discrimination of any sort in the BBC, but I think as an organisation you always have to look harder and review how you go about identifying issues, and that work is never done."

The Board of Deputies of British Jews said in a statement that it welcomed the review into "deeply concerning" experiences of Jewish staff at the BBC.

"The BBC is an important national institution and should be setting the gold standard for an inclusive workplace and impartial broadcasting," it said.

"We stand ready to support both Lord Mann and the BBC in addressing these concerns, rebuilding confidence within the Jewish community and ensuring that the BBC sets an example for other broadcasters to follow."

Last month, Oscar-winning producer Lucie Kon said the BBC had given her a £400,000 payout after she raised antisemitism concerns.

The BBC said it did not uphold allegations of antisemitism but accepted there were "shortcomings" in how it treated Kon, which had a "personal impact" on her. The corporation did not specify what the shortcomings were.

In January, the BBC apologised for its use of language during coverage of Holocaust Memorial Day, saying programmes should have referred to "six million Jewish people" having been murdered by the Nazi regime, rather than "six million people" or "six million mostly Jewish people".

Last September, the BBC's broadcast of Bob Vylan's controversial set at Glastonbury broke editorial guidelines in relation to harm and offence , with the corporation's complaints unit ruling that some comments could "fairly be characterised as antisemitic". The band denied being antisemitic.

MN202611_y0jrrjco8d.t:
The Med Emre (pictured in 2023) is a Malta-flagged vessel

An oil tanker carrying up to 7,000 tonnes of diesel has sunk off the coast of Ibiza, leaving one crew member dead, authorities have said.

The Med Emre, a Malta-flagged vessel, was carrying 17 crew members who were all rescued. However seven were taken to hospital and one was later pronounced dead, Balearic Islands emergency services confirmed.

The six crew receiving treatment reportedly suffered minor injuries, such as hypothermia, Spanish media reports.

The possible environmental damage is being assessed by a plane and Spain's pollution control vessel, Clara Campoamor, which is owned by the country's national maritime rescue service.

"There is still little information available about a possible fuel spill," Balearic Islands' President Marga Prohens wrote on X.

The Med Emre sank 25 nautical miles (46 km; 29 miles) from Ibiza's coastline and 57 nautical miles from Valencia. It is unclear what caused the sinking.

The chemical tanker was en route from Algeciras, in southern Spain, to Barcelona in the north-east.

Rescuers in Valencia received a distress call around 22:30 local time (21:30 GMT) on Wednesday, according to Spanish media. Minutes later, the vessel reported a leak and the crew said it was leaning at a 90-degree angle.

The injured crew members have been taken to hospitals in Valencia and Can Misses Hospital in Ibiza, President Prohens said.

Ibiza's marine environment was added to the Unesco World Heritage List in 1999. In particular, it is home to dense prairies of Posidonia oceanic seagrass, which is found only in the Mediterranean basin and plays a vital role in supporting local marine biodiversity.

In 2002, Spain experienced one of its worst environmental disasters when the Prestige oil tanker ran into trouble off Galicia's coastline . It spilled more than 60,000 tonnes of heavy fuel oil into the sea.

MN202611_36997y25os.t:
Watch: Fire and smoke billows out of refinery owned by energy company Bangchak Corporation

Seven people have been injured - four of them critically - after an explosion at an oil refinery in Bangkok, local government officials have said.

A fire broke out after the blast at the Phra Khanong facility run by energy giant Bangchak Corporation in the east of Thailand's capital at around 14:45 (07:45 GMT).

The company said the fire was brought under control and put out within 30 minutes, adding that the cause of the incident was being investigated.

Black smoke could be seen across Bangkok's skyline after the blast, while officials told residents to leave the area.

A alert sent to mobile phones by Bangkok authorities confirmed the fire was under control, but urged people to avoid the location.

Eyewitnesses shared video clips on social media of flames and smoke rising above the refinery.

The city-run Erawan Emergency Medical Centre said it was treating four "red" cases and three "yellow" - less severe - cases.

Bangchak Corporation said it had shut down production at the site, which can process up to 120,000 barrels of oil a day. The company has a second refinery in Chonburi province, about 50 miles (80km) from Bangkok, handling a capacity of about 180,000 barrels daily.

An explosion occurred at the Bangkok refinery in July 2012, sparking a fire but no reported injuries.

MN202611_1eqrrutkobn.t:
Myanmar's president Min Aung Hlaing has led the country since he seized power in a 2021 military coup

Myanmar will not comply with "inappropriate" parts of the genocide ruling by the International Court of Justice (ICJ), its leader Min Aung Hlaing has said in his first public comments since the court decision.

The ICJ's landmark ruling last week found Myanmar guilty of committing genocide against its Rohingya minority in a 2017 military crackdown that killed thousands and forced more than 700,000 to flee.

Myanmar denied committing genocide, saying its forces had responded to attacks by armed groups. It is the first state to have been found in violation of the 1948 Genocide Convention.

Min Aung Hlaing said "the term 'genocide' had seriously affected the country's reputation", state media report.

"Myanmar would take actions appropriate for a responsible country but would not comply with requirements it considered inappropriate," the country's coup leader-turned-president said at a meeting on Wednesday, according to state media.

The statement did not specify which parts of the ruling the country objects to.

The genocide case, brought by The Gambia in 2019, centred around so-called "clearance operations" initiated in 2017 in Rakhine State, where many of the Rohingya Muslim minority resided.

The ICJ determined that about 10,000 Rohingya were violently killed during the operation, while more than 700,000 are thought to have fled to Bangladesh by foot or by sea. The court found that approximately 815,000 had been targeted in some way.

The verdict was reached by a majority of nine votes to six among a panel of judges from around the world.

The ICJ also found in favour by majority that Myanmar had violated several other parts of the 1948 Genocide Convention.

The ruling is final and cannot be appealed.

The ICJ ordered Myanmar to pay proportionate reparations, but said an exact figure should be determined at a later date.

The court also ordered Myanmar to stop ongoing violations and immediately investigate those suspected of breaking the Convention.

But the ICJ does not have the power to enforce these demands. Instead it has to rely on the UN Security Council and political pressure to make its rulings stick.

While the ruling was largely symbolic, it was welcomed by Rohingya communities and human rights groups who have long called attention to the suffering faced by the Rohingya.

More than a dozen countries have acknowledged the ICJ ruling, and the UK has announced sanctions on several senior Myanmar military leaders .

Myanmar has been devastated by civil war since Min Aung Hlaing led a military coup to oust civilian leader Aung San Suu Kyi in 2021. The move turned Myanmar into an international pariah, and its military regime has faced sweeping international sanctions.

Since then, Min Aung Hlaing has been trying to reintegrate Myanmar into the international community, but it remains largely shut out of key diplomatic arenas.

MN202611_bz2lirvhzl.t:
Dozens of Palestinians have been killed in Gaza in near daily air strikes over the past month

A Hamas political official and his wife were among eight Palestinians killed in three Israeli air strikes across the Gaza Strip on Thursday.

Local sources told the BBC a residential apartment in Deir al-Balah was targeted at dawn, killing Khaled Abu Nada - the deputy education minister - and his wife, Abeer Mohammed Ismail Abu Nada.

A Hamas Civil Defence spokesman said that rescue teams and medical personnel had transferred eight bodies to Al-Aqsa Hospital in central Gaza and Al-Shifa Hospital in Gaza City.

In a joint statement, Israel's prime minister and defence minister said the operation was "part of a series of targeted killings" against Hamas officials.

Thursday's strikes also reportedly killed three Palestinians on al-Nafaq Street, east of Gaza City. Their identities have not yet been established, eyewitnesses said.

In a separate strike on Shati refugee camp, west of Gaza City, three Palestinians working for Hamas's security services were killed. They were identified as Yasser al-Lahham, Iyad Ahmed and Ibrahim al-Mashal.

Khaled Abu Nada and his wife Abeer Mohammed Ismail Abu Nada were killed in the air strike

In a post X, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu confirmed the death of Khaled Abu Nada and said about 80 Hamas officials have been killed in the last month.

"No one in Hamas's leadership will succeed in evading us," he said, adding that the military would "continue to pursue our enemies and protect the security of Israeli civilians".

The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) said it had carried out a strike on a "senior" Hamas operative, and would provide further details later.

The attacks came a day after Mohammed Abu al-Ouf, 47, the head of Hamas's internal security service in northern Gaza, his wife and their two teenage daughters were killed in Israeli air strike on their apartment in Shati refugee camp in Gaza City.

On Tuesday, the overall commander of Hamas's internal security service was among 10 Palestinians reportedly killed in Israeli strikes.

Violence has continued in Gaza since Israel and Hamas agreed to a US-brokered ceasefire in October last year. Israeli strikes take place almost daily in areas under Hamas's control, which are home to 2.1 million people, most of them displaced.

At least 1,705 people have been killed in Gaza over the past 13 months, according to the territory's Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the UN.

Israel says six of its soldiers have been killed in Gaza during the same period.

The Gaza war was triggered by the Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on 7 October 2023, when about 1,200 people were killed and 251 others were taken hostage.

Since then, more than 74,772 people have been killed in Israeli attacks in Gaza, the health ministry says.
