For the last few years, "turkey bombers" Esther Keim and Heidi Hastings have taken to the skies to airdrop Thanksgiving turkeys to residents in off-grid communities in south-central Alaska.

Hastings pilots the plane while her best friend Keim drops the turkeys out the plane window, delivering to families who may not otherwise get one of the birds, since they are cut off by snow and ice.

MN202611_8x2oy8zc1a.t:
Thirty-one people have been killed and 21 others injured after a large fire broke out on a busy highway in Cairo.

Footage circulating on social media showed billowing flames and black smoke towering high into the night sky, with multiple nearby vehicles torched.

The fire occurred on a section of a ring road in the Warraq neighbourhood, north of the old city centre. Egypt's health ministry said the injured were being treated at hospitals nearby.

Officials have not given an account of how the fire broke out, but state-owned media reported that a high-voltage cable fell in front of a fuel tanker, causing the driver to lose control and the tanker to overturn, dousing nearby vehicles with petrol.

MN202611_sg18ipffy7.t:
Kenyan President William Ruto and DR Congo counterpart Felix Tshisekedi

When President William Ruto and his Congolese counterpart, Félix Tshisekedi, sat down in Oyo on Sunday, 22 November, under the mediation of Republic of Congo President Denis Sassou-Nguesso, the cameras captured warm handshakes and talk of African solidarity.

But behind closed doors lay a stubborn reality that had poisoned relations between Nairobi and Kinshasa for nearly five years: in Tshisekedi’s diplomatic playbook, disagreement is treated as betrayal, neutrality as taking sides, and an independent foreign policy as outright hostility.

For Nairobi and many other governments, working with Kinshasa remains an exhausting exercise in walking a tightrope, where anything short of total submission invites backlash.

When in November 2022, Kenya stepped up, deploying the Kenya Defence Forces (KDF) to lead the East African Community Regional Force (EACRF) under Major General Jeff Nyagah, it expected gratitude. Instead, Kenyan troops faced hostility. Kinshasa demanded an offensive war against M23, directly contradicting the regional force’s mandate to oversee political and ceasefire arrangements.

At the February 2023 EAC summit in Bujumbura, Tshisekedi publicly humiliated Maj-Gen Nyagah in front of President Ruto, accusing the Kenyan commander of favouring M23. Following intimidation and covert surveillance of his residence, Nyagah resigned in April 2023.

By December, the EACRF had been forced to withdraw early after Kinshasa refused to renew its mandate. This made it clear that Tshisekedi rejected Ruto’s suggestion that, having secured a six-month ceasefire, the regional force should now help move the conflict towards a political settlement.

This was not the only time Kenya’s neutrality and respect for the rule of law caused tensions with the DRC. In December 2023, when former DRC electoral chief Corneille Nangaa launched the Congo River Alliance (AFC), which includes M23, at a Nairobi hotel, Kinshasa recalled its ambassador and demanded immediate arrests, seemingly unable to grasp how a constitutional democracy works.

President Ruto rightly stood firm on the rule of law. “We only arrest criminals and deal with them, not issuing statements,” he told Kenyans on 17 December, adding: “Statements are issued almost every day against me, but I never arrested anyone.” Holding a press conference in a free society does not amount to endorsing rebellion, but Kinshasa refused to recognise the distinction.

Today, even as talks of reconciliation between Kinshasa and Nairobi continue, it remains uncertain whether the underlying cause of the crisis has been resolved. That cause lies within Kinshasa’s political culture, in which an obsession with Rwanda has hardened into the main dividing line in Congolese politics. Every politician, particularly those in the opposition, is expected to toe Tshisekedi’s line or risk being branded “pro-Rwanda” and accused of treason. To survive politically or appease Kinshasa, public figures are effectively expected to condemn Rwanda every day as proof of their patriotism.

Having normalised this zero-sum mentality at home, Kinshasa expected the same alignment abroad. But Ruto repeatedly refused to play along.

At the Africa CEO Forum in Kigali in May 2024, for instance, Ruto challenged the narrative promoted by Kinshasa and its Western allies.

“How is the M23 Kagame’s problem? It’s a Congolese problem,” he told interviewers, recalling an East African Community heads of state meeting at which Kinshasa was asked whether M23 fighters were Rwandan or Congolese. “And the DRC told us: ‘They’re Congolese.’ End of question. If they are Congolese, how does this become a Rwandan problem?”

Ruto’s point was that an insurgency involving Congolese citizens requires an internal Congolese political solution. Kinshasa, however, immediately cast his reasoning as pro-Rwandan bias.

Worse still, Kinshasa’s frustration spilled into dangerous ethnic rhetoric. Tshisekedi’s ally and MP Justin Bitakwira framed the conflict in eastern DRC as an existential war between Bantu and Nilotic peoples. Invoking the conspiracy theory of a “Hima Empire”, he urged viewers to scrutinise President Ruto’s physical features in an attempt to link Kenya’s head of state to Tutsi power.

As documented by the UN Group of Experts, this toxic narrative fuelled ethnic profiling across the DRC and put ordinary Kenyans directly at risk. And Kenyans have paid the price.

In June 2024, Kenyan marathoner Kennedy Kiptoo Lilan was detained in Kinshasa after Congolese soldiers mistook him for an M23 fighter based solely on his physical appearance. In January 2025, mobs protesting M23’s advance attacked Kenya’s embassy in Kinshasa, alongside other diplomatic missions accused of backing Rwanda.

By September 2025, the rhetoric had turned deadly. Sarinke Isaya, a Kenyan Maasai shoe vendor, was lynched and burned alive in Mambasa, Ituri, after locals treated his “Nilotic” features as evidence of Tutsi espionage. His killing came amid a wider wave of arbitrary arrests targeting Kenyan and Tanzanian Maasai traders, as well as Somali truck drivers.

After the meeting in Oyo, it is unclear whether two things are now clear to Congolese leaders. First, that Kinshasa cannot dictate the foreign policy of other countries. Kenya does not need to become Rwanda’s enemy to prove its friendship with the DRC. Second, that nothing can justify violence against ordinary Kenyan citizens in the DRC.

Genuine regional partnership requires mutual respect and a commitment to protecting each other’s citizens.

MN202611_1gqlb1mkor.t:
Pellegrino Matarazzo became manager of La Liga side Real Sociedad in December 2025

From kicking a ball around in the parks of New Jersey to lifting the Copa del Rey with Real Sociedad, Pellegrino Matarazzo's journey to managing the La Liga side has been anything but conventional.

He studied applied mathematics at Columbia University, played football in Germany's lower divisions and eventually became the first American manager in La Liga history when he joined the San Sebastian club in December 2025.

It is a journey that began in New Jersey, where Matarazzo grew up in an Italian-American family with football woven into its identity.

"My love for the game came from my family, from my dad, my uncles, the entire family with the Italian background loving the game," he explains.

With no MLS at the time, the family's footballing allegiances lay across the Atlantic, particularly in southern Italy, and Napoli became the team they gravitated towards.

"I spent my whole childhood playing football," Pellegrino told BBC Sport. "Whether that's for school teams, club teams, or just with the family on Sundays in the park.

"I continued to play through college, and then I realised that my curiosity was too big to not take that step overseas and that's what led me to where I am now."

Yet his academic path initially suggested a very different future.

Though Matarazzo graduated with a degree in applied mathematics, he insists it was never his great passion.

"It was just something I was good at," he says.

Instead, he decided to pursue his playing ambitions in Germany.

"I was always very ambitious but I never managed to play professional football above the third division at the time in Germany," he said.

"So there came a time where I needed to decide what to do next. Do I go back to the States and use my degree or do I remain in football?

An opportunity to obtain his coaching licences at a German club ultimately decided his future.

Pellegrino worked under Germany boss, Julian Nagelsmann, at Hoffenheim before being handed his first senior managerial role at Stuttgart.

There, he guided the club to promotion and established them in the Bundesliga. He later returned to Hoffenheim as manager, helping them avoid relegation before securing Europa League qualification.

In December 2025, was appointed Real Sociedad head coach.

"If I open doors, if I do something special for US managers down the line, then that's fantastic," he said.

"But I'm just doing my thing at the moment, looking to make progress in my own career and get better every day at what I do."

Matarazzo arrived at a difficult moment for Real Sociedad, who were struggling at the bottom of La Liga, but he believes understanding the people and the region was central to establishing his team's identity.

"The most important step was to really create the style of football and identity that fit both the people of Gipuzkoa [the province where San Sebastian is based] and the team," he explains.

"I really love the Basque culture. There are people that are very hardworking, intelligent, at the same time have the ability to remain humble and grounded despite success."

"Those are values that I also carry within me, which made it an easy transition."

He has also been working on his language skills, although admits the Basque language is a big challenge.

"Spanish is going well. It took me a bit of time to start learning, because I didn't have time to waste when I first moved, but speaking Italian certainly helps."

On the pitch, meanwhile, one player has been particularly important in establishing the culture he wants.

Captain Mikel Oyarzabal, who played a starring role in Spain's 2026 World Cup triumph, has many of the characteristics associated with the people of Gipuzkoa.

"He embodies that ability to stay grounded despite success, to work hard," Matarazzo says.

"He leads by example. He's not an emotional leader on the pitch, but he leads through clear communication and doing the work."

It is a relationship that makes the manager's job considerably easier.

And together they have already experienced something special.

Matarazzo arrived at Sociedad with an ambition to win a trophy, and Sociedad's Copa del Rey triumph in April delivered a landmark moment for the club.

It was their first trophy in five years, following their 2021 triumph in the same competition, which had been celebrated without fans in attendance because of Covid restrictions.

This time, players and supporters could finally celebrate the occasion together.

"It was an amazing dynamic that started in January and that we just exponentially increased to the explosion in Seville to win the title," Matarazzo recalls.

"It was an unbelievable moment for everyone."

Now, with European football offering another stage on which to demonstrate Sociedad's ambitions, Matarazzo is determined that success should not become a reason to stand still.

"We always want more and it's always a maximum possibility. We want more than what we had last year and we want to do well in La Liga, in the cup, in the Europa League and in the Super Cup."

Sociedad sit fifth in La Liga, 14 points behind league leaders Barcelona.

On Thursday, they take on Crystal Palace in the Europa League at Selhurst Park.

"We're expecting an emotional stadium with a team that has quality, despite their position in the Premier League table."

"It's Thomas Frank's first home game in charge so we will see what he's changed and his direction. But we are ready and that's part of football."

So what would the young boy from New Jersey make of it all?

"I think my younger self would be very curious as to what comes next, especially because it's never linear. My wife, my son and I have also sacrificed a lot.

"But I also think he would be very proud."

Watch: Why has Poundland collapsed into administration?

The blame game for the demise of Poundland is in full swing.

The number one target is US-based Gordon Brothers who bought the discount chain for £1 and have taken nearly £20m out of the business already.

Gordon Brothers stand to get paid back a further £22.5m, as their share of an existing £30m loan is set to be one of the first debts that the administrators will have to pay out of the proceeds of any sale of the business in whole or in part.

The team running Poundland blame the owners for strangling their ability to turn the business around, saying that their access to Poundland's own cash was restricted, leaving them unable to fully restock ahead of the crucial Christmas period.

They point to improving sales over October as proof the business had a future.

MPs also laid into the US firm with members of the Business Committee accusing it of "predatory capitalism" and "asset stripping".

Poundland collapses putting 11,000 jobs at risk

No-one appears to dispute the fact that Gordon Brothers' insistence that they get paid most of their £22.5m debt was a major stumbling block to a sale.

Potential buyers balked at paying out millions on a loan that Gordon Brothers inherited for nothing.

Martin Property Group offered £5m up front with the balance to be deferred, while Xyra Holdings offered £12.5m up front but, according to sources close to the deal, were thought unable to actually pay.

Unsurprisingly perhaps, Gordon Brothers dispute a lot of how they have been characterised.

First, they insist that they lent the business £85m to try to keep it alive for the 17 months since they bought it. Without them, this collapse would have happened in June last year.

The £20m taken out of the business since then has mostly been interest on that loan.

Despite brief periods of sales growth compared with a year earlier, Poundland was not generating enough cash to sustain itself. Sales were forecast to be £115m lower than predicted when Gordon Brothers bought the business - more than offsetting a £100m cost-cutting programme.

Like other retailers Poundland was hit by rising labour costs, employment taxes and business rates.

In the end, argue Gordon Brothers, none of the potential buyers could meet their terms and prove they had the money and expertise to make a go of it.

Such is the discrepancy between the two versions that the chair of the Business Committee wants Gordon Brothers and the management back in front of them to get to the truth.

It is still possible that a bidder may emerge in the coming hours and days to save the business as a whole but most industry observers think that looks unlikely.

Julie Palmer of insolvency specialists Begbies Traynor told the BBC: "This sort of direction of travel seemed somehow inevitable. Obviously, if one of those interested parties steps up and buys the whole business and assets, that's the best, quickest and cleanest outcome. I think realistically, though, there is a chance now that there will be a breakup."

Like previous busts such as Woolworths, BHS and Wilko, many of these stores will find new owners and they will need local, experienced staff.

But none of that will be much comfort to those workers facing grave uncertainty a month before Christmas, when they should be at their busiest and most needed.

Gordon Brothers specialise in situations of commercial distress. When they take on a distressed company, they try to make sure that the worst possible outcome is still one that makes money for them.

In this situation, the worst outcome would mean they get paid back £22.5m, earn interest on the loan they provided the company (secured against the company assets) and a few other miscellaneous fees.

Little wonder then that many people say they had little incentive to strain every sinew to secure a buyer. They argue they kept a business that would have collapsed last June going for another 17 months, which extended employment for thousands of workers.

But if, as some retail veterans have told the BBC, Gordon Brothers never really intended to turn this business around, why would the previous owners PepCo give them a no-lose gamble? Why didn't they do what Gordon Brothers are doing - profiting with no risk?

The answer is simple: Pepco have other businesses, which could have got tangled up in the administration of Poundland.

MN202611_1eo40kj5cg1.t:
Banki Nkuru y’u Rwanda (BNR) yatangaje ko umutungo w’urwego rw’imari mu Rwanda wazamutse ukagera ku kigero kingana na 68% by’umusaruro mbumbe w’igihugu (GDP), mu gihe inguzanyo nshya zatanzwe n’amabanki mu mezi icyenda ya mbere ya 2026 ziyongereyeho 40%, zigera kuri tiriyari 2,7 Frw.

BNR igaragaza ko umutungo w'urwego rw'imari mu Rwanda wageze kuri tiriyari 17.5 Frw ungana na 68% by'Umusaruro Mbumbe w'Igihugu.

Ibi byagarutsweho na Guverineri wa BNR, Soraya Hakuziyaremye, ubwo yagaragazaga ishusho y’urwego rw’imari n’ingaruka zishobora kuruhungabanya, mu kiganiro n’itangazamakuru cyibanze cyane ku myanzuro ya Komite ishinzwe Politiki y'Ifaranga ndetse n'ibyavuye muri Komite ishinzwe kubungabunga Ubudahungabana bw'Urwego rw’Imari (Financial Stability Committee).

BNR yagaragaje ko umutungo w’urwego rw’imari wiyongereye bitewe n’izamuka ry’amafaranga abitswa mu mabanki, ubwishyu bw’ubwishingizi, inyungu z’ishoramari n’imisanzu y’ubwiteganyirize. Amabanki ni yo afite umugabane munini, kuko abarirwa kuri 66% by’umutungo wose w’urwego rw’imari.

Mu mezi icyenda ya mbere ya 2026, inguzanyo nshya amabanki yemereye abakiriya ziyongereyeho 40%, zigera kuri tiriyari 2,7 Frw, mu gihe inguzanyo zari zisanzwe zitangwa zazamutseho 20,2%.

Ubwubatsi ni bwo bwakomeje guhabwa inguzanyo nyinshi, kuko bufite 24% by’inguzanyo zose zari zitarishyurwa zatanzwe n’amabanki, ibigo by’imari iciriritse n’ibindi bigo bitanga inguzanyo. BNR ivuga ko ibi bigaragaza uruhare rw’ishoramari mu miturire n’iterambere ry’imijyi, ariko ko kwibanda cyane kuri uwo mwuga bishobora guteza ibyago urwego rw’imari ruramutse ruhuye n’ibibazo.

Nubwo bimeze bityo, inguzanyo zitishyurwa neza zagumye ku kigero kiri munsi ya 5%. Mu mabanki zaragabanutse zigera kuri 3,2%, mu bigo by’imari iciriritse ziba 2,2%, mu gihe mu bigo by’imari bitanga inguzanyo bitakira amafaranga y’ababitsa zagabanutse ziva kuri 17% muri Nzeri 2025 zigera kuri 4%.

Guverineri Hakuziyaremye yagize ati: “Muri rusange, urwego rw’imari mu Rwanda rukomeje kuba ruhamye kandi rufite ubushobozi bwo guhangana n’ibibazo. Icyakora, hari intege nke zisaba ko dukomeza kuba maso, cyane cyane ibyago bishingiye ku mutekano w’ikoranabuhanga, uburiganya n’ikoreshwa ry’ubwenge buhangano.”

BNR yanagaragaje ko amabanki afite igipimo cy’imari shingiro kingana na 21%, kiri hejuru y’ikigero fatizo cya 15% gisabwa, mu gihe mu bigo by’imari biciriritse kiri kuri 30%. Ku bijyanye n’ubushobozi bwo kwishyura inshingano z’igihe gito, amabanki afite igipimo cya 280%, mu gihe ibigo by’imari biciriritse bifite 57%, byombi biri hejuru y’ibipimo fatizo bisabwa.

Mu bwishingizi, ubwishingizi bw’ibinyabiziga ni bwo bufite umugabane munini w’amafaranga yishyuwe, ungana na 34,7%, bukurikirwa n’ubw’ubuvuzi, ubw’ubuzima buri kuri 12% n’ubw’inkongi z’umuriro buri kuri 11%. Ubwishingizi bw’ubuhinzi bwo buracyari hasi, kuko bufite 1,2% gusa by’amafaranga yose y’ubwishingizi. Ku rundi ruhande, umutungo w’ibigega by’ubwiteganyirize n’izindi gahunda za pansiyo wageze kuri tiriyari 3,3 Frw. Ikigega cya Leta gifite hafi 93% by’uwo mutungo wose.

BNR yanatangaje ko ubwishyu bukorwa mu buryo bw’ikoranabuhanga n’ubundi buryo bw’ubwishyu bw’abantu n’ibigo, bwageze kuri tiriyari 28 Frw, bwiyongeraho hafi 31% ugereranyije n’umwaka wari ushize. Agaciro k’ubwishyu bw’ikoranabuhanga ugereranyije na GDP kageze kuri 353%.

Mu byago BNR ikomeje gukurikiranira hafi harimo ubwiyongere bw’uburiganya n’ibitero byo kuri murandasi, ibyago bijyanye n’ubwenge buhangano, ingaruka z’izamuka ry’ibiciro ku bushobozi bw’abafashe inguzanyo bwo kwishyura, ndetse no kwibanda cyane ku nguzanyo zijya mu bwubatsi n’imitungo itimukanwa.

Guverineri yavuze ko BNR izakomeza gukurikirana ubushobozi bw’abafashe inguzanyo bwo kwishyura, ireme ry’inguzanyo zijya mu bwubatsi n’imitungo itimukanwa, ndetse no gufatanya n’abandi bafatanyabikorwa mu guteza imbere isoko ry’imari, kugira ngo ibigo by’imari bibone uburyo butandukanye bwo gushora amafaranga yabyo.

Yashimangiye ko ingamba ziteganywa zigamije gukumira ibyago bitaragera ku rwego rwo guhungabanya imikorere y’urwego rw’imari, no gukomeza kurinda ko rukomeza guhama no kugira ubushobozi bwo guhangana n’ibibazo.

MN202611_1el8jdl0gs7.t:
Alejandro Garnacho is yet to start a game for Aston Villa this season

Alejandro Garnacho's time at Aston Villa has been brief - and it already looks to be over.

The latest snub by Villa boss Unai Emery was the most damming of all, with the on-loan Chelsea winger left out of Tuesday's Champions League defeat at Galatasaray.

"The players who were here I think are the best players to be here with us," said Emery.

Villa could have had 12 substitutes in Istanbul but Emery chose just 11 - including two goalkeepers - as Garnacho stayed at home.

The plan was for the Argentina international's loan move to become permanent for £43m should certain criteria be met.

They are believed to be based on a number of appearances staff felt were so achievable the club were in little doubt he would become a Villa player.

But now there is doubt he will ever play for them again.

Garnacho trained with Villa's first team on Monday but did not travel to Istanbul

"First start after three months. Happy to be enjoying football again."

The post Garnacho wrote on social media after a pre-season game in July has - along with anything else related to Villa - been deleted from his account.

He has played just 34 minutes in the Premier League this season, and seven of Villa's 11 games ended without him getting on the pitch.

His last appearance - just a three-minute cameo - came in the 1-1 draw against Fulham on 31 October.

Including Saturday's 0-0 draw with Sunderland , Garnacho has been omitted from the past three matchday squads - a strong sign Emery has lost faith in him.

But he may have been fighting a losing battle from the off, having arrived at Villa unfit.

Sources have acknowledged the 22-year-old was not at the level required and were surprised how off the pace he was when he signed in July.

He initially trained on his own, and questions over the signing were already being asked, with eyebrows raised by some internally given his inconsistent form for both Chelsea and Manchester United .

Yet he had been on Villa's list of targets - albeit a long list - while he was at Stamford Bridge as Emery was keen to sign a pacy winger in the summer.

Garnacho's problems were compounded by a head injury suffered in Thailand in pre-season, and even a boot camp during the international break in September and October, and scoring in friendlies against Sevilla and Southampton have not helped.

One of the issues Villa have is there is no exit clause, and both teams would have to agree to end the season-long loan deal early.

This time last year, Emery had already decided not to sign Harvey Elliott permanently in a £30m deal , leaving the on-loan Liverpool midfielder in limbo for the rest of the season.

And it appears Emery has already come to the same conclusion with Garnacho.

With Villa unable to find a solution with Liverpool , Elliott wasted a precious year of his career. Those close to him recognise the damage last season did, playing just nine times after being named Player of the Tournament at the European Under-21 Championship in 2025.

He is now at Valencia and is yet to start in La Liga this season.

The risk of going on loan to Villa became a topic of conversation in the game because of Elliott's plight, with sources suggesting players would think twice about joining the club. Garnacho's situation only increases those concerns.

Three times in two seasons, Emery and Villa have signed a high-profile player on loan only for it to fail.

Jadon Sancho's expensive loan from Manchester United last season - Villa paying a guaranteed 80% of Sancho's wages of more than £200,000 a week - ended with him having made just nine Premier League starts and scoring once in 39 appearances - 21 of those as a substitute.

Sancho may have played more than Elliott and Garnacho - and came off the bench in their Europa League win - but what value did Villa really get?

Of course, Marcus Rashford and Marco Asensio enjoyed positive loan spells previously - Rashford returning to the England squad while at Villa - but they are exceptions to the rule.

Nicolo Zaniolo, Clement Lenglet and Axel Disasi have joined in recent years and barely merit footnotes, while Douglas Luiz's loan return last season did not prompt a return to the heights he had reached previously at Villa.

The club have constantly complained about financial restrictions with some justification, but questions can certainly be asked about the money spent on many of their signings.

The blunt truth is there is no clear path.

Teenager George Hemmings has just signed a new deal and has earned praise from Emery for understanding the way he wants his players to work.

Ibrahim Mbaye and Alysson are also ahead of Garnacho, leaving him well behind even before regulars John McGinn, Johan Manzambi and Emi Buendia are factored in.

There was interest from abroad in the summer, with Roma keen, and it seems increasingly unlikely we will see Garnacho at another Premier League club soon.

Fifa rules allow players to play for two clubs in a season - or three if they move to a team whose season overlaps like the MLS - meaning Garancho could feature for another, unlike Elliott as he had already played for Liverpool and Villa.

Garnacho, whose character has not been called into question while at Villa, cost Chelsea £40m when he signed from Manchester United in 2025 but failed to make a consistent impression, with eight goals in 43 games. When he joined Chelsea he signed a contract until 2032.

Prior to that, United boss Ruben Amorim had told him to leave.

Now nothing, it seems, will persuade Emery that Garnacho is worth persevering with - leaving the winger's career continuing to drift.

MN202611_9ak349czl3.t:
Egyptian authorities have arrested a man accused of causing a tanker crash and massive fire that killed 31 people on a busy Cairo highway.

The public prosecutor's office said the motorist had confessed to driving at 110km/h (68mph) along a section of ring road, to the north of the old city centre, and clipping the tanker with the side of his car as he changed lanes.

Sources close to the investigation were earlier quoted by state media as saying a high-voltage cable had fallen in front of the fuel truck, causing the driver to lose control.

Twenty-one others were injured in the crash in the Warraq neighbourhood on Wednesday evening, with hospitals treating patients for burns and smoke inhalation.

The public prosecutor's office said on Thursday that "upon questioning the suspect and confronting him with the findings of the investigation... he confessed to committing the act".

"He added that, while moving between traffic lanes and overtaking vehicles, the left side of his car collided with the right rear side of the tanker. This caused him to lose control of the steering wheel and his car veered to the far right of the road."

At the same time, one of the fuel tanker's tyres burst, causing it to veer into the highway's central reservation, hit the concrete barrier and overturn, spilling fuel and igniting a fire, the prosecutor's office said.

Egyptian authorities have not named the suspect accused of causing the fatal crash, but they said he had been travelling with his father at the time.

The raised motorway - a major artery for traffic around the Egyptian capital - was reopened by emergency services hours after the crash occurred, with the burnt-out wrecks of cars shifted to the side by bulldozers and diggers.

A cabinet minister said on Thursday that 10 million Egyptian pounds (£139,000; $182,000) had been donated to the families of the victims, while the nation's sports minister said all state-run celebratory activities would be cancelled in the aftermath of the crash.

Egypt has suffered several deadly fires in recent years. Road collisions are also common, attributed to poor maintenance and violations of traffic laws, and leading to thousands of road deaths a year.

More people face higher mortgage repayments when they roll off a fixed deal than previously estimated, new figures from the the Bank of England show.

About 6.5 million owners are forecast to see their monthly repayment jump by £100 on average when they move onto their next deal by the end of 2029, new data in its Financial Stability Report reveals.

That is more the double the £45-a-month hike that the Bank estimated in its last report in July.

In the shorter term, about one million of those homeowners, who are on mortgage rates below 3% and due to refinance by the end of next year, will see an average £200 increase in their monthly repayments.

For borrowers, the interest rate on a fixed mortgage does not change until it expires, usually after two or five years, and a new one is chosen to replace it. The vast majority of homeowners and buyers have this kind of mortgage.

Since the Iran war began, global economic uncertainty has been pushing up the cost of deals, with the average rates on two and five year fixed mortgages at their highest for about three years.

On Thursday, the average rate on a two-year deal was 5.99%, and at 6% for a five-year deal, according to the financial information service Moneyfacts.

Analysts have described the situation as "brutal" for homeowners coming to the end of their fixed deals.

However, the Bank's report points out that the average £100 increase in monthly repayments was half the rise experienced by those refinancing during 2023 and 2024.

Dawn Fazackerley-King is a Pilates instructor who lives near Ipswich and has previously spoken to the BBC about her struggles with the cost of living.

She was on a five-year fixed deal at 1.4%, which she took out in January 2022. But the mother-of-two is about to refix for two years and the best deal she can find is a 5.69% loan. That will push her costs up by about £200 a month.

It should be used as a guide only and does not represent the suitability, eligibility or availability of mortgage offers for users. For exact figures, users will need to approach an official mortgage lender.

Interest rates fluctuate based on the Bank of England's base rate and market conditions

She is far from alone, with one million homeowners facing a similar increase often because they are coming off deals that were agreed before interest rates began rising in 2022.

The Bank's report said that households facing higher payments "may need to reduce discretionary spending or draw down savings as higher energy and other essential costs feed through".

Most had savings buffers but lower-income households, including renters, had less wriggle room owing to spending a greater proportion of their income on essentials.

Early in November, the Bank raised the benchmark interest rate , which influences borrowing costs for individuals and businesses, for the first time in more than three years, from 3.75% to 4%.

The numbers could change were mortgage rates to fall, primarily if international economic volatility eased.

Even so, the Bank said around 350,000 were already projected to see monthly mortgage repayments fall when they fixed their next deal within three years.

The report also suggested there were no signs of an increase in borrowers defaulting on their loans, while UK households remained resilient.

"We have not seen the scale of mortgage arrears that we saw if you go back to earlier periods, the early 90s, the early 80s, actually even the financial crisis. And we are not seeing the scale of house repossessions, and that has to be a good thing," said the Bank's governor, Andrew Bailey.

However, separately, the Bank warned that cyber attacks had become a more prominent threat to the UK's financial stability.

Financial firms needed to "keep pace with the growing scale and sophistication of cyber threats", the report said.

MN202611_p25wgiysxc.t:
Liz Rich moved to the south Wales farmhouse for peace and quiet

The woman at the centre of a "real-life ghost story" that inspired a new TV drama says the scariest thing she saw was an "old lady" looking at her from her house.

Liz Rich moved from London to Bannau Brycheiniog, also known as Brecon Beacons , with her husband while pregnant in 1989 to a farmhouse now dubbed one of Britain's most haunted houses.

Within seven years Rich said their "idyllic, fairytale" home turned to hearing unexplained footsteps, seeing animals mysteriously die, apparitions - and an "old lady" who watched her from the house as she walked up the driveway.

Danny Robins, writer and creator of The Witch Farm , said: "It's one of the greatest ghost stories I've ever come across."

On Thursday Rich spoke to This Morning , external and said the scariest thing was: "I didn't like the old lady.

"The first time I saw her I was coming up the driveway with a push chair, and I glanced up at the play room window. It wasn't a nice room, it was on the top floor.

"I looked up and staring directly at me was this old woman, she was like a beige-grey colour. She was solid, wasn't see-through.

"She had a knitted cardigan and her hair was grey, but permed with the curly bits in it. I didn't like it."

The Witch Farm , a four-part drama by the BBC, explores the family's claims of poltergeist activity, of alleged possessions and even physical injury which affected them and the community.

Robins, who is best-known for his podcast Uncanny, said the idea for the new drama came after he made The Battersea Poltergeist podcast for the BBC, which he described as being based on "another real-life ghost story".

He said he was looking for a story "at least as exciting", adding "Liz really cut through".

He said: "I thought this was the big one."

Liz and Bill Rich moved into the home which is now dubbed one of Britain's most haunted houses

Rich said different events that left them increasingly scared were "gradual".

"I have a mind that tries to look for logical explanations. If something goes bang, I think a light bulb blown," she said.

"The first thing I couldn't explain were footsteps which was like someone wearing hobnailed boots.

"Bang bang bang, on the wooden stairs. That really worried me.

"They were to become a common occurrence, maybe daily."

The Witch Farm's creator Danny Robins (left) said Liz's story "really cut through"

At one point, Rich said they had an electricity bill so high it was "impossible" and as if "it was for a factory".

She said the house's electricity meter span was out of control and later landed them a bill of £750 for three months, which is the equivalent of about £2,000 in today's money.

This led the the couple to try an experiment.

"If you turn all the electrical appliances off in the house the little wheel would still keep going on, and then stop and pick up speed.

"We had experts and the electric board in, and they couldn't explain it. Eventually we got in a solicitor to help."

South Wales, 1989. Looking for a fresh start, a family instead finds a house with a past that refuses to stay buried. Danny Robins's chilling drama based on a terrifying true story.

Robins said the series was about "real people who went through hell" adding Rich was "still scared after all these years".

"Liz's story stumbled into my lap, basically.

"It was that thing I rarely feel, a sense of tingles down my spine. Sitting opposite somebody and you get that sense of fear from them, you see the whites of their eyes light up and you feel a little tremble in their voice."

He said he was "torn" about whether he believed in ghosts.

"I've never had my own experience, I've never witnessed something myself.

"I can't fully sign up for team believer, but I can't explain the stories I'm told and it chips away at you."

Rich said the family who has lived there for nearly 30 years have had "no problems" but the people living before her and Bill did.

The Witch Farm is available on BBC iPlayer, BBC One and BBC One Wales

A pregnant inmate has escaped from custody in the US state of New Mexico, after taking control of a police vehicle while returning to prison from a prenatal appointment, the state's corrections department has said.

Rebecca Taylor, 26, took control of the Dodge Journey and drove away when the team transporting her and another inmate stopped to pick up food in Albuquerque, local media reported.

The New Mexico Corrections Department said that the vehicle and her prison jumpsuit were later recovered, but Taylor remains on the run.

She had been imprisoned for multiple theft and burglary charges, the department said in a Facebook statement.

Local media reported that another inmate, also travelling back from a prenatal appointment, was able to get out of the car as Taylor took control on Wednesday morning.

The corrections department has said that a multi-agency search for Taylor is under way. The BBC has approached it for an update.

The Albuquerque Journal reported that Taylor is currently in her second trimester of pregnancy. For this reason, she was not restrained during transportation, department spokesperson Brittany Roembach said.

"It is the understanding right now that one officer was with the vehicle but not inside of the vehicle when this occurred," she was quoted as saying.

All prisons in New Mexico went into lockdown following Taylor's escape, but it was lifted at 06:00 on Thursday.

However the prison where she was being held, the Western New Mexico Corrections Facility, will remain on "modified movement", and no visitors are currently allowed.

The public has been told not to approach Rebecca Taylor if they see her, and call police straight away.

MN202611_sttgw8mdd2.t:
Poundland has collapsed into administration, leaving the jobs of its 11,000 staff in doubt in the run-up to Christmas.

The company has appointed consultancy Alix Partners to oversee a sale of part or all of the discount retailer, with questions remaining about the future of the the company.

This is the question that is most difficult to answer. In short, we don't know yet.

Poundland stores will continue trading for now and remain open as usual, at least in the short term.

Poundland collapsing has acted as a reset button on the process of selling the company.

Administrators are looking to either sell the business as a whole, or to break it up, the more likely outcome.

Before the collapse, Poundstretcher owner Fortress was interested in buying about 200 of the stores, and wanted to keep those trading under the Poundland brand.

But Fortress's position at the moment is unclear.

A source close to one of the bidders for the whole of Poundland when it was a going concern, Martin Property Group, has already said it is "unlikely" to make a fresh bid now due to "irreparable harm" having been done to the brand by the administration process.

Poundland's managing director Barry Williams believed Poundland was turning a corner and seeing a "strong recovery".

Although the chain was struggling when it was sold by Pepco last year for £1, in the year to September it recorded a profit of £18.1m, swinging back from a £68m loss in the previous 12 months.

Going into the vital Christmas period, first-quarter sales were up 3.3% .

The picture Poundland's management paint is of a retailer undergoing a turnaround until the owner, US investment firm Gordon Brothers, pulled the plug on funding for day-to-day expenses such as buying stock.

The Usdaw union, which represents shopworkers, said the owners forced Poundland into administration.

And Steve Smith, who co-founded Poundland in 1990, said "this shouldn't be happening really", adding that staff and suppliers have "worked so hard" to turn the business around.

Labour MP Antonia Bance said she had been "pretty appalled" by the conduct of Gordon Brothers over the past few weeks, and that it was going to make much bigger profits by breaking up the business rather than by keeping it going.

However, Gordon Brothers insisted the business was not turning a profit, and had missed budget forecasts.

A spokeswoman said while the management team had made £100m in cost reductions, the business had moved from a £70m loss to "around break-even" on paper.

"Break-even is different from generating the cash needed to buy stock, invest, and withstand increasing economic pressures," the spokeswoman said. "A few good weeks do not make a turnaround."

Poundland repeatedly missed budget targets over the year, the spokeswoman added.

Gordon Brothers was concerned that as inflation goes up next year, those pressures would have helped to make the business unviable, it said.

And Julie Palmer, managing partner at the insolvency agency Begbies Traynor, said Poundland's collapse "seemed somehow inevitable" and pointed the finger at challenges facing retailers - including higher costs to employ staff.

"There's plenty of other retailers that are feeling this cost squeeze at the moment, and this is the big name. But I think there will be another huge number of other retail failures as well," she told the BBC.

Stores are still trading while the administrators work out if the business is viable.

The funds locked up by Gordon Brothers - at the last count about £70m - have now been released by the administrators.

This has turned the taps back on, so staff will continue to be paid in the run-up to Christmas, and so will suppliers.

But here's the catch. The administrators have a legal obligation to maximise value for "secured" creditors. It means the owners, Gordon Brothers, are at the head of the queue for being paid back the loans that were stumbling blocks in the negotiations.

But more importantly for staff, if the administrators can get more value by breaking up the business than by selling it as a whole, then that is what they have to do, even if the business proves viable.

If the business is broken up and its stores are sold off, the new owners would not be obliged to keep staff on.

From 26 November refunds for goods which people just change their minds about will not be given (but if the item is faulty you will still get a refund).

The immediate reason Poundland collapsed was that Gordon Brothers locked up funds for the day-to-day running of the business, including to pay suppliers.

This meant that stock was running dry at Poundland.

But those funds have now been unlocked, meaning suppliers can be paid, and supply chains can be re-established, at least in the short term.

If an item is on the shelves, then shoppers can buy it.

Palmer said the administrators will have to get the best value for creditors, which could mean selling the business as it stands.

But if Poundland is broken up, administrators could sell the brand without the stores, or the brand along with some of the stores, or the stores without the Poundland brand to its competitors.

Some worry if Poundland disappears from the High Street, that is one less place that shoppers can find discount products. It is also one less chain providing competition and an incentive for other shops to keep prices down.

"Poundland is a place they go on the high street to get bargains and... given the cost of living challenges we face, that is of concern to us in government," Wes Streeting, the defence secretary, told the BBC on Thursday.

Poundland's customers, however, will likely turn to rival discount retailers in the hunt for bargains if the chain disappears from the High Street.

Nk'uko bigaragara mw'itangazo Ubushikiranganji bw'ubudandaji bw'Uburundi bwasohoye, ikilo c'amababi mabisi y'icayi kigiye kugurwa amafaranga 1000 y'Amarundi, mu gihe cahora ku 500.

Ubwo bushikiranganji buvuga ko iyo ngingo yafashwe mu ntumbero yo "kwishura ku myitwarariko y'abarimyi". Bumenyesha kandi ko yafashwe mu ntumbero ya reta yo "kugenda ibadugiriza buhorobuhoro amafaranga [bakura muri ico gisata]".

Haraciye igihe kitari gito abarimyi mu Burundi bidoga ko uburimyi bw'icayi ataco bubamariye kubera amafaranga bakuramwo atakibabeshaho. Bafatira ku kuntu ibiciro vy'ivya nkenerwa kw'isoko vyagumye biduga, mu gihe igiciro c'icayi kitakurikiye uwo murindi.

Ivyo vyunyuwe n'ingorane z'ikena ry'ifumbire. Vyageze n'aho bamwe mu barimyi batangura kurandura imirima yabo y'icayi, kugira bahatere ibiterwa mbumbarugo.

Ikigo ca reta kijejwe icayi mu Burundi, OTB, kimenyesha ko mu myaka 10 iheze, umwimbu w'icayi wasubiye inyuma ku rugero rwa 30 kw'ijana. Gishimangira ko muri ico kiringo nyene amahegitari arenga 1000, mu yarimwamwo icayi, yahebwe.

Mu kuduza igiciro c'ikilo gushika ku gihumbi, reta y'Uburundi yizeye ko abarimyi bagiye kwiyumva ko bashigikiwe gurtyo bongereze umurindi wo kuvyura uburimyi bw'ico giterwa. Yizigiye kandi ko bagiye gusubiriza ibiterwa bishaje, bananagure imirima bari barahevye.

Icayi ni kimwe mu biterwa njabukamazi vyahoze vyinjiriza Uburundi amafaranga mvamakungu, hambavu y'ipampa n'agahawa. Ariko ivyo bisata vyose bimaze imyaka bigenda bisubira inyuma, aho n'abarimyi babikoreramwo bakomeza kudebukirwa.

Iduga ry'ibiciro mu Burundi, ntiriraje ishinga abarimyi gusa. N'abaharanira uburenganzira basaba inzego z'igihugu kurihagurukira. Icegeranyo ishirahamwe OLUCOME rirwanya ibiturire n'isesagurwa ry'amatungo ya reta ryasohoye ku wa gatatu, cerekana ko mu mezi abiri aheze ibiciro vy'ibiribwa mu masoko vyaduze ku rugero rudasanzwe.

Nk'akarorero, ico cegeranyo kivuga ko ikilo c'ibiraya cagurwa 2000 mu kwezi kw'icumi, ubu kigurwa 4500. Ikilo c'ibiharage bisanzwe, ubu kigeze ku 5500 mu gihe cahora ku 3500. Umuceri urimwa mu Burundi mu kw'icumi wagurwa 5500, ariko ubu ugeze ku 6500.

MN202611_l163k1y0yn.t:
Arsenal co-chairman Josh Kroenke should probably turn his phone off if the Gunners fall behind against Manchester City on Sunday.

Chris Sutton's predictions guest this week, Kings of Leon drummer and City fan Nathan Followill, is good friends with Kroenke - and says he will be in touch if the game is going City's way.

"I'm super excited for this weekend and I've got my smack talk ready for Josh already," Followill told BBC Sport.

"I've heard about the City fans with their inflatable bananas and I need to get myself one. My wife is going to be like 'er, an inflatable banana just arrived in the mail - do you know anything about that?'

"We are going to win 4-2 so I will be texting Josh throughout the game... and, after Erling Haaland's second goal, I will send him a picture of me kissing the banana!"

AI has also made its predictions, and you can pick your own below.

The most popular scoreline selected for each game is used in the scoreboards and tables at the bottom of this page.

A correct result (picking a win, draw or defeat) is worth 10 points. The exact score earns 40 points.

Want to make more predictions? You can play BBC Sport's new Match of the Day predictor game every week, featuring six fixtures from domestic and European competition.

Followill got a behind the scenes tour of Etihad Stadium and City's training complex when Kings of Leon played next door at Co-op Live arena in 2024. "It's a beautiful stadium, and an amazing set-up," he said. "Their practice pitches are better than most college pitches in the US."

Followill has supported City for more than 20 years , external and his children have followed in his footsteps by becoming Blues, despite the best efforts of his next-door neighbour in Nashville, as well as Kroenke.

"When my kids were born, they both received a full Arsenal kit - head to toe - in the mail from Josh," he explained.

"Both times, they were returned to sender - instantly.

"My son and daughter are both City fans now, but my neighbour, Jeremy Connor, is Tottenham , and I mean flying the flag full on.

"When they lose, you can hear him screaming - and when they win, you can hear him screaming too.

"His son is trying to convert my son to Spurs and I am like 'that is never going to happen in this house!'"

Chris Sutton and Nathan Followill were speaking to BBC Sport's Chris Bevan.

The AI predictions were generated using Microsoft Copilot Chat - we simply asked the tool to 'predict this weekend's Premier League scores'.

Followill says it was eye-opening to watch City's boys and girls' teams play when he visited their training campus. "I had no idea how much they put into developing kids from the youngest ages all the way up," he said. "That was probably the most impressive thing for me - to see how many young kids were out there, with the ultimate dream of pulling on that blue shirt one day."

Chelsea have scored and conceded 20 goals so far this season, which kind of sums up where they are at.

Xabi Alonso's side have also lost as many league games - five - as Manchester United , and United are in crisis.

Alonso is not under pressure, or anything like that, but if they lose this game too, you can imagine the mood of the club - and it won't be good.

Apparently their fans were singing 'you don't know what you're doing' at him after their defeat by Leeds - which is what they sang at me when I was there.

Alonso needs to decide on a shape and a way of playing, and stick with it.

Anything could happen here, because Nottingham Forest 's form is hardly convincing either.

They tore Manchester City apart in their previous home game, before the international break, but can they really dig out another result like that here?

I think they will go about it in a similar way, and be aggressive and have a real go at Chelsea ... and I don't see Chelsea 's defence keeping them out.

Nathan's prediction: No-one thought Forest would beat us, and while Chelsea need a big result, I can see Forest getting a point here. 1-1

We talked about Leeds on the Monday Night Club and how they have upgraded their team with the players Daniel Farke bought over the summer.

Farke strengthened in the areas he needed to improve, but is still trusting some of the players who did well for him last season - the likes of Jayden Bogle and James Justin, who have been outstanding.

They are a really well-balanced team and they have good depth to their squad too. The only criticism would be that they are not usually free-scoring - they hit four against Chelsea but before then they had only managed 10 goals in their first 10 league games.

Leeds do not give much away at the back either, though, and I think that will be key in this game.

When I watch Coventry they are dynamic with their counter-attacks and I always fancy them to nick a goal like that.

Not this time, however. Leeds might take a while to break them down, but I think they will come out on top.

Nathan's prediction: Coventry play in sky blue too? Part of the reason I became a Manchester City fan was the kit, and I have always gravitated towards teams in light blue, so I am going to go with Coventry here. 0-1

I am at this game for 5 Live and I am not expecting much to change for Manchester United .

No-one thought it was going to be easy for Mauricio Pochettino to go in at United and turn things around. He has taken over a complete rabble.

United's draw in Lisbon on Wednesday was chaotic, but you also have to consider how Sporting have not got going in the Portuguese league or the Champions League this season.

That was not a great Sporting side. They are pretty average and Brentford will be a much bigger test.

The Bees are supremely well-organised and will be full of confidence, too, after putting four goals past Everton on Monday. They were against 10 men for the entire second half, but were 2-0 up by then anyway.

Pochettino needs something to cling to, but for him picking that backline must be like pinning the tail on the donkey. Whoever he picks, they are not very good.

I really want to be more positive about United, because I heard from quite a few of their fans last weekend, but this prediction is about as positive as I can be about them at the moment.

Nathan's prediction: It is tough for me to talk about United because in America we have a saying 'don't kick a man when he's down' and it's pretty rough for them right now... but I'm not going to lie, it is nice to see United this low in the table.

I don't think it is the manager that is the problem for United right now, so I don't think Pochettino coming in is going to be an instant fix. They've got some growing pains to get through, and I won't be disappointed to watch that.

When I watch the Premier League at home, Brentford always cracks me up because I am huge fan of The Office and I just imagine a bunch of David Brents out there, just running around the pitch, which is a very funny thing for me.

I know I just said don't kick a man when he's down, but I don't think United would be nice to us if we were down there... so, I think the David Brents are going to win. 1-2

I actually think Villa will win this game 2-1 but I want to make it clear the scoreline I have gone for is from my commentary colleague, Alistair Bruce-Ball, who is an Ipswich fan - a fake one, but still a fan.

I asked him about this game when we were in Belgium for Liverpool 's Champions League game on Wednesday. He will be at Portman Road on Saturday for 5 Live and he is backing the Tractor Boys to get something, so I am doing the same out of respect for him.

Ipswich really need a result too. They have gone five league games without a win and, with Hull and Coventry both winning last week, they are the lowest placed of the promoted sides.

That is never a good thing, and it feels like Gary O'Neil's side are in a precarious position at the moment, where they are getting sucked towards the bottom three.

I've been surprised to see Villa hit a bit of a sticky patch too, with three successive league draws and no wins in six in all competitions, so it will be interesting to see if they are any better here.

Nathan's prediction: Villa have had some surprising results recently but I do think they will win this. 1-3

I was in Bruges to watch Liverpool in midweek and it was interesting to see two of their players who came in for some heavy flak last season, Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz, both shine.

Isak is looking like the player who Liverpool thought they signed in 2025. He is finding his rhythm, and Wirtz also seems to be in a really good place confidence-wise. When I watch them now, it feels like something is going to happen.

There are other positives for Reds boss Andoni Iraola too. I know there will be a debate about Bradley Barcola's end-product but I love watching him in full flow when he is running past defenders - there is no better sight in football than moments like that.

Rio Ngumoha is exciting as well, and he has such a good football brain which makes him even more dangerous.

Everything points to a Liverpool win, but I am hesitant to just go with that because Everton are coming off the back of a drubbing by Brentford . You can imagine David Moyes giving his side a miserable old week and getting stuck into his players.

I didn't think James Tarkowski should have been sent off in that game, but he will be suspended here. It is his absence that swings it for me because he is a real leader for Everton .

Nathan's prediction: Everton are usually the underdogs in this game but both teams are pretty level at the moment. One of our record producers is a huge Liverpool fan so he won't be happy with me... but I am going to say Everton will take it. 2-1

I was at Newcastle 's draw with Arsenal last week and, in fairness to Magpies boss Matthias Jaissle, he changed things around at half-time and got his reward.

Jaissle needed that half of football, because I don't think the Newcastle fans have been too convinced by his approach, but this is another very tough game for him.

Brighton probably still can't believe they lost to Hull last week - but lightning is not going to strike twice.

Nathan's prediction: I have to give a shout out to my statistician Lucy here, because there were a couple of teams I didn't know a lot about and she gave me some good insight. So, Brighton have scored a lot of goals this season and I think they will get more here. 3-1

Thomas Frank has got a huge task at Crystal Palace . They are conceding so many goals.

Losing Maxence Lacroix and Marc Guehi from their defence was like Robbie Williams and Jason Orange leaving Take That, because they were never going to be the same without them.

I still think Frank has got some decent attacking players, however.

The Hull keeper, Konstantinos Tzolakis, looks like a great signing. I don't know how he made some of his saves against Brighton and he probably doesn't know himself either.

Brighton should have buried them and I think Palace will get plenty of chances too.

Fair play to Hull for their spirit and the way they scrap for each other, but I still think they are going to go down.

Hull fans are probably wondering if I am ever going to predict they will win a game... the answer is no, at least not this week anyway.

Nathan's prediction: Palace have given up 27 goals in 11 games which is a lot. Hull have surprised a few people this season and I am backing them here. 0-2

Bournemouth are on a long winning run in the league but I've been impressed by Fulham whenever I've watched them.

Alvaro Arbeloa's side have not been great at home, with only one win at Craven Cottage so far, so I am going with them to get another draw - which would be their fourth in a row.

Nathan's prediction: Both these teams have picked up a lot, so this is a tough one to call. 2-2

Tottenham boss Roberto de Zerbi must think a lot of 18-year-old midfielder Luca Williams-Barnett after picking him for their win over Ipswich .

I love to see managers trust young players like that, especially because Spurs have had such a tricky season so far.

It will be interesting to see whether De Zerbi picks him again here, but I feel like the outcome of this game is more dependent on which Sunderland we see.

They picked up a good point at Villa last time out, but they never seem to be quite the same after they have played in Europe, like they are doing this week.

The Black Cats will be without injured duo Brian Brobbey and Granit Xhaka for this game too, so I don't think they will have enough to win it.

Nathan's prediction: Dave Stewart from Eurythmics lives in Nashville too and is a good buddy of mine - and he is Sunderland until death! He is such a die-hard fan that every time we have dinner, we will sit there and talk about 'Haway the Lads' and just shoot the breeze about Sunderland .

So I am going to back them in this one, because of Dave and also because of my neighbour Jeremy, who I mentioned earlier.

Jeremy was especially cocky when they had Harry Kane and he would just talk so much smack - I always knew if they were doing good because I'd get a text from him. So, because Jeremy is such a cocky little Spurs fan, I am saying Sunderland will win. 2-1

I always enjoy this game because of Gabriel's battle with Erling Haaland, but it is in midfield where I think it will be decided.

Manchester City have spent a lot of money on players in that part of the pitch but Enzo Maresca has not found the right combination yet.

Somehow Maresca has got to find a way of nullifying Declan Rice, but that will be very difficult because Rice is just an absolute machine.

You can never rule City out because of Haaland's ability to score goals but the only result I see here is an Arsenal win, and I am going for a classic Gunners scoreline.

Nathan's prediction: This is the big one! It's huge. I feel really good about it, too. Arsenal are riding so high at the moment, I feel like we might catch them snoozing.

I predict Haaland will get two goals, Phil Foden will get one too and we will end up with four. 2-4

After drawing a blank since week two, Chris finally picked up another win in week 11 - and it was his spot-on prediction for Liverpool to thump Manchester United 4-0 that sealed the deal.

That meant he got three correct results, including two exact scores - at Anfield, and Tottenham 's 2-0 win over Ipswich - giving him a total of 90 points.

In a tricky week for predictions, where Liverpool were the only team to start the weekend in the Premier League's top six who won, it was those exact scores that made all the difference.

Chris' guest, undisputed world champion boxer Lauren Price, the BBC readers and AI also all got three correct results.

But the BBC readers were the only ones to also get an exact score - in the Spurs game - giving them 60 points.

Lauren and AI both ended up on 30 points - AI did call Newcastle 's draw with Arsenal correctly, but it was wrong about Bournemouth 's win over Nottingham Forest , which everyone else got right.

Not many of you got that Liverpool -United scoreline correct, either.

From around 27,000 predictions, the most popular scoreline picked was a 2-1 home win and only 570 of you went for 4-0.

"When has AI ever gone for a 4-0?" said Sutton. "That's what the crowd wants. The crowd don't want AI - who wants mathematics?

"The crowd want gut-feeling and instinct. I think I should get 1,000 points for that prediction, because I was brave enough to go for it."

For the first time this season, there were SIX games where no-one made a correct prediction - who thought it was easy?

The biggest shock of the week was Leeds ' 4-1 victory at Stamford Bridge. Again from around 27,000 predictions, more than 3,600 (14%) of you did back Daniel Farke's side to win... but just 11 of you saw that scoreline coming.

Senne Lammens (left) joined Manchester United in the summer of 2025

After a first season at Manchester United that drew little but praise, goalkeeper Senne Lammens is under the microscope like never before.

A bad mistake that gifted Sporting their second goal on Wednesday, having earlier conceded a clumsy penalty, followed several other errors so far this season.

The 24-year-old Belgium international also made an error at the World Cup in the summer, spilling a shot that led to Spain's winning goal in the 88th minute of their quarter-final.

"I don't know [at what point Manchester United drop him]," legendary Manchester United goalkeeper Peter Schmeichel told CBS Sports on Wednesday.

"Mauricio Pochettino has come in and brought his own staff. That means he's got a new goalkeeping coach and maybe that is something that can change it for him.

"[At the World Cup] he came on against Spain and made a bit of a mistake. Mikel Merino scored and they got knocked out. I feel he's lost a little bit of confidence from that mistake and hasn't really recovered.

"As a goalkeeper, when you're not on your best form, you need your defenders in front of you to help you out. The sad truth is that they haven't been able to do that and that makes it so much worse. I like him a lot but today was not a great day for him."

Three penalties and a red card as Man Utd draw against Sporting

Director of football Jason Wilcox and United's data team overruled Ruben Amorim when they opted to sign Lammens from Royal Antwerp for £18.1m in September 2025.

Amorim wanted Argentina World Cup winner Emiliano Martinez, who was left waiting for a deadline day call that never came to seal a move from Aston Villa.

United felt Lammens had the attributes to become one of the world's best goalkeepers. At 24, he is still young. Schmeichel was 27 when he joined United in 1991. Edwin van der Sar was 34 when he left Fulham in 2005. Both had hundreds of senior appearances behind them. Lammens has just over 100, more than half of them with Royal Antwerp.

Although he made the odd error last season, Lammens did nothing to suggest Wilcox and co had got it wrong.

After releasing Turkey international Altay Bayindir, who replaced Andre Onana as first choice at the start of last season and is back on loan in Turkey with Trabzonspor, they signed 36-year-old Wales international Karl Darlow as back-up this term.

Darlow finished last season as first choice at Leeds. But he only started 30 league games in three seasons with the Elland Road outfit. Also on the bench in Lisbon was Tom Heaton. The 40-year-old has not played in a senior game since February 2023.

Mistakes earlier in the season – former United midfielder Paul Scholes claimed in September '"the jury is still out" on whether Lammens is truly top class – have brought increased analysis. His positioning for Dominik Szoboszlai's opening goal for Liverpool on Sunday was questioned externally, even if United focused their attentions on Bradley Barcola shoving into the wall.

Just 75 seconds after getting down to make an excellent save from Luis Suarez's first penalty, Lammens recklessly charged out and upended Maxi Araujo, even though Noussair Mazraoui seemed to be in a position to deal with it.

Then, after two Bruno Fernandes goals at the start of the second period had turned the Champions League tie in the visitors' favour, Lammens reached to collect a high ball and inexplicably dropped it in front of Suarez, who applied the overhead kick finish.

Understandably, there was sympathy in the dressing room.

"This team is a family," said striker Joshua Zirkzee. "There's no-one who will suffer by themselves.

"Senne is a great goalkeeper and mistakes happen. In this moment, we just give him space. I'm not sure if he wants to hear anything at all. But Senne's a great kid. He's got a good head on him. We didn't draw because of him, and we all know that next game he is going to be at the top of his game."

'One mistake from being dropped' - Ashley Young on Senne Lammens

Toni Jimenez is Pochettino's long-time goalkeeping coach.

His arrival triggered the exit of Craig Mawson, who had been with Manchester United since 2019. Connor King is Jimenez's assistant but a relative newcomer himself, having joined from Burnley in 2026.

By its nature, goalkeeping at the highest level can be a mental challenge as well as a technical one. As Onana discovered, flaws can quickly become major issues and once the spotlight is shining, the attention is fierce.

Lammens has given the impression privately of being strong. He has seemed remarkably unaffected by his World Cup torment – his mistake against Spain came after he was introduced as a 71st-minute replacement for injured veteran Thibaut Courtois with the quarter-final delicately poised at 1-1. But only he knows the full picture.

Jimenez will be Pochettino's guide over what to do about the situation, although for now, Lammens' head coach is behind him.

"This type of thing happens," he said. "That is football. Football is about making mistakes.

"I always want to support my player. I think we need to talk about responsibility. In this type of action our defensive line needs to cover the keeper better because it was very difficult.

"It's not to blame the defensive line, but it's two things that we need to improve, details that we need to work on. We need to manage his type of situation better."

Following Wednesday's draw in Lisbon, Pochettino highlighted "two things" that need to improve if United are to start winning matches on a regular basis.

The first of those is the club's preferred goalkeeper. Of the 17 Premier League goalkeepers to have played a minimum of 10 matches in all competitions in this campaign, Lammens has the second-worst save success rate, keeping out just 60.2% of the shots he has faced. Only Coventry's Carl Rushworth (54.4%) has fared worse so far this season.

Lammens also ranks bottom of those 17 goalkeepers for clean sheet ratio (6.3%).

And there is substance to the suggestion that Lammens has declined in 2026-27. He made just one error leading to a goal in the entirety of last season in contrast to two already in this campaign. The data also shows that he is currently preventing far fewer goals.

The second "thing", however, has significant bearing on the first.

Clean sheets and conceding fewer goals are clearly a collective responsibility, particularly for the "defensive line" that Pochettino referenced on Wednesday - and United's defence has collectively struggled this season.

They have now let in 36 goals in all competitions, the most of any team in Europe's top five leagues. They have also conceded five penalties and received five red cards - both the second-highest tallies among Europe's elite divisions.

So is Lammens more error-prone this season? Apparently yes. But he's also playing behind a defence that, on current form, may not inspire too much confidence in their goalkeeper.

Gérard Depardieu has faced a series of allegations in recent years on film sets and elsewhere

French film actor Gérard Depardieu is to stand trial for the alleged rape of actress Charlotte Arnould, a Paris appeals court has confirmed.

Arnould, who was 22 at the time, had reported the alleged rape several days after going to his house in Paris to rehearse a play.

She has waived her right to anonymity and her lawyer said Thursday's ruling was a "first" and the forthcoming trial would be historic.

Depardieu, 77, had contested his indictment on two counts of rape. In a letter published in Le Figaro in 2023, Depardieu strongly denied Arnould's allegations, saying "there was never any coercion or violence between us".

Depardieu was for decades a leading figure in French and international cinema for roles in Green Card, The Man in the Iron Mask and the Asterix films. He was awarded France's Légion d'honneur in 1996.

But in recent years a series of allegations have been made against him over his conduct on film sets and elsewhere in the wake of France's #MeToo movement, known as balance ton porc ( call out your pig).

Last year, he was given an 18-month suspended jail term after he was found guilty of sexually assaulting two women on a film set in Paris in May. He was also placed on the sex offenders register and ordered to pay compensation.

He dropped his appeal against the ruling last week and offered "sincere apologies" for his behaviour on the set of director Jean Becker's 2021 film Les Volets Verts (The Green Shutters).

Depardieu had been a friend of Charlotte Arnould's father and on 7 August 2018 she had gone to his home, where much of what happened was captured on the actor's own CCTV.

Arnould's case was initially dismissed for insufficient evidence, but after she filed a civil complaint, a judicial investigation was opened in the summer of 2020.

Speaking outside the Paris appeal court on Thursday, her lawyer Carine Durrieu Diebolt said the ruling was a victory for her client for whom it was "genuinely a relief".

The appeal court said that while Depardieu should stand trial for what took place on that day, he would not be tried for a further alleged rape at a hotel six days later.

Depardieu's lawyer David-Olivier Kaminski told reporters that court had partly ruled in his favour: "As soon as we get the ruling, we will look into the possibility of appealing to the Court of Cassation."

Meanwhile, Depardieu is under a separate investigation alongside French author Michel Houellebecq for "allegations of a sexual nature".

French authorities confirmed their inquiry last week, following reports of an alleged "gang rape" on the set of the film Thalasso in 2018.

If you have been affected by any of the issues raised in this story, details of help and support in the UK are available at BBC Action Line .

Abashinzwe ubugenzuzi bo muri Amerika bemereye kompanyi SpaceX kohereza mu isanzure ibyogajuru miliyoni imwe mu rwego rwo gufasha kubaka ibigo byo mu isanzure byo kubikamo amakuru yo mu ikoranabuhanga – ubu ni ubwa mbere uruhushya nk'urwo rutanzwe.

Iyo kompanyi, y'umuherwe wa mbere ku isi Elon Musk, irashaka gukoresha urumuri rw'izuba mu guha ingufu ibyogajuru bizajya bitunganya amakuru y'ubwenge buhangano (AI), ubundi bikohereza ibisubizo ku isi.

Ku wa gatatu, ikigo cy'Amerika kigenzura itumanaho (FCC) cyavuze ko uwo mushinga, uzwi nka Starmind, "uzafasha ubukungu burimo kwiyongera cyane bw'Amerika bushingiye ku bwenge bw'akataraboneka".

Ariko kompanyi Amazon, mucyeba wa SpaceX, yanenze iyo gahunda, ivuga ko ari "intego yo kwibonekeza aho kuba gahunda nyakuri", mu gihe abahanga mu bumenyi bw'ikirere bo muri Amerika bavuze ko icyo cyemezo "kizabangamira cyane" ubushobozi bw'abaturage bwo kwiga no kwitegereza ikirere na nijoro.

Harimo kwiyongera abantu barwanya ibigo by'amakuru (cyangwa 'data centres') byo ku isi, harimo no muri Amerika aho inzobere zivuga ko ibyo bigo byabaye kimwe mu byatumye ishyaka ry'abarepubulikani ritsindwa cyane mu matora yo hagati muri manda yabaye mu ntangiriro y'uku kwezi, aho abo mu ishyaka ry'abademokarate batsindiye kugenzura imitwe yombi – abasenateri n'abadepite – yo mu nteko ishingamategeko.

SpaceX yemera ko "ibigo by'amakuru byo mu isanzure" ari bwo buryo buhendutse cyane kandi bukoresha neza ingufu, bwatuma haboneka ingufu zirimo kwiyongera zo gukoresha mudasobwa z'ubwenge buhangano (AI), ingufu zirenze "ubushobozi bwo ku isi".

Mu itangazo yasohoye, umukuru w'ikigo FCC Brendan Carr yavuze ko uwo mushinga "ufunguye intambwe nshya ya gitwari mu bikorwa-remezo by'ikoranabuhanga bicyenewe kugira ngo Amerika ikomeze kuyobora no gutera imbere".

Carr yongeyeho ati: "Ubu ni bwo bwoko bw'ubuhanga bw'Amerika bushobora guhuza imbaraga zacu mu isanzure n'ikoranabuhanga rikataje, bukongerera imbaraga ubuyobozi bwacu mu by'ubukungu, ndetse bukongera uburumbuke hano iwacu."

Amakuru ya BBC Gahuza ako kanya kuri WhatsApp yawe

Ubwo yavugaga kuri iryo tangazo, Musk yanditse ku rubuga nkoranyambaga X ati: "Turabashimiye cyane. Iki kizaba igikoresho gikomeye cyane kuri Amerika no ku isi."

Uruhushya rw'ikigo FCC ruvuga ko kohereza ibyo byogajuru bigomba gutangira bitarenze mu Gushyingo (11) kw'umwaka wa 2033. SpaceX izasabwa ko bitarenze mu Gushyingo kw'umwaka wa 2035 izaba yamaze kohereza 10% by'ibyo byogajuru, nuko mu Gushyingo kw'umwaka wa 2038 ikazaba yamaze kubyongera ku kigero cya 50%.

Iyo kompanyi isanzwe yaravuze ko ishaka kohereza icyogajuru cyayo cya mbere cyo muri iyo gahunda ya Starmind mu mwaka utaha.

Ntibisobanutse niba ibyogajuru miliyoni imwe mu by'ukuri bizoherezwa cyangwa niba SpaceX yasabye uruhushya rw'umubare munini cyane uruta uw'ibyo izakoresha.

Cyo kimwe n'umuyoboro wa murandasi (internet) yihuta cyane ya Starlink wa kompanyi SpaceX, uca ku byogajuru byayo birenga 10,000, ibyogajuru bya Starmind bizakorera mu isanzure ryo mu gice cyegereye isi, mu butumburuke buri hagati ya kilometero 500 na kilometero 2,000.

Ibyogajuru byo muri iyo gahunda ya Starmind bizakorana na murandasi ya Starlink, ubundi byohereze amakuru ku isi.

A Rheinmetall facility in Kuwait was targeted by Iran, Italian and Kuwaiti authorities said

Two Italian nationals have died after an Iranian strike on a facility in Kuwait, Italy's foreign ministry has said.

The pair were technicians working for German arms manufacturing company Rheinmetall, the ministry added.

Kuwait's defence ministry earlier said that four people - the two Italians, a Kuwaiti national and Pakistani national - had been injured from falling shrapnel after a number of drones from Iran were detected and intercepted.

It comes just over a week after Kuwait said it had repelled overnight Iranian drone attacks on an airbase which hosts US forces - the first strikes in more than two months on the country.

Recent exchanges of fire between the US and Iran, and a deadlock in negotiations, have raised fears of a major escalation in the war.

The conflict began when US and Israel attacked Iran in late February, with Iran retaliating by launching missiles and drones at Israel and Gulf Arab states hosting US military assets and personnel.

Kuwait's Army said the latest attack was on a "vital site in the country" and was the result of "heinous Iranian aggression", while confirming the deaths of the two Italian nationals.

Meanwhile, Italy's foreign ministry said in a statement: "An explosion caused by a drone attack... occurred at a site where two Italian technicians from the company Rheinmetall Italia were working."

The two Italian nationals were working at an air defence detection station and performing maintenance work on systems used by the Kuwaiti Armed Forces, according to Italian press agency Ansa, citing Italy's foreign ministry.

Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni wrote on X: "On my own behalf and on behalf of the government, I express my deepest sympathy and offer my heartfelt condolences to the victims' families.

"My thoughts are with all those affected by the attack and their families."

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen wrote on social media: "We must step up pressure on Iran to end these unacceptable attacks against its neighbours and our partners in the Gulf.

"Today's events are a further reminder that security in the Gulf is a security issue for us all."
