Ingrid Karangwayire, Executive Secretary of BK Foundation, along with staff, partners and local population, installed a sign post identifying the trees planted on Nengo Hill.

BK Foundation, in partnership with the Rwanda Rural Rehabilitation Initiative (RWARRI), has planted thousands of trees in Rubavu District as part of a nationwide campaign aimed at restoring degraded land, controlling soil erosion and protecting the environment.

The exercise involved planting different species of trees, including fruit-bearing varieties, in several locations across the district, with particular attention to areas vulnerable to soil erosion and other environmental challenges.

One of the key locations was Nengo Hill, in Nyabagobe Village, Nengo Cell, Gisenyi Sector, where residents joined the exercise to plant trees on a hillside that has suffered significant soil erosion.

Residents said the initiative would help address environmental challenges that have affected communities in Rubavu, particularly during periods of heavy rainfall and strong winds.

Mukantwari Immacule, one of the residents who participated in the exercise, said Rubavu frequently experiences weather-related disasters, adding that the trees would help protect the soil from being washed away by rainwater.

She said the vegetation would help stabilise the hillside and reduce erosion, which has been a concern for residents.

Another resident, Hategekimana Vincent, said the trees would offer additional benefits beyond environmental protection, including providing timber in the future and improving the appearance of Rubavu town.

The exercise also extended to schools, where fruit trees, including avocado trees, were planted to improve students’ access to nutritious food.

Niyonsaba Martin, headteacher of Rambo Primary School, one of the institutions that received avocado trees, said the initiative would help learners understand the importance of protecting trees while benefiting from the fruits they produce.

He noted that trees contribute to cleaner air, while fruit-bearing varieties can supplement the meals provided to students at school, supporting better nutrition.

Uwizeye Belange, head of RWARRI, said the partnership with BK Foundation had initially targeted planting 70,000 trees in Rubavu and Rutsiro districts.

However, the target was increased to 90,000 trees following an expansion of the programme.

Karangwayire Ingrid, Executive Secretary of BK Foundation, said Nengo Hill was selected because of the significant soil erosion it had experienced.

She explained that the initiative prioritises locations already affected by erosion, as well as areas considered vulnerable to future environmental damage.

The activities in Rubavu are part of the Road to 1 Million Trees campaign, a partnership involving BK Foundation, RWARRI and Save Environment Initiative (SEI), which aims to plant one million trees across Rwanda.

The campaign includes planting different varieties of trees, including fruit-bearing species, to support environmental conservation while delivering benefits to communities.

Following the Rubavu exercise, the campaign is scheduled to continue in Rutsiro District on Friday, November 27, in partnership with RWARRI.

The activities will culminate in a national Umuganda tree-planting exercise on Saturday, November 28, in Mageragere Sector, Nyarugenge District, organised in partnership with Save Environment Initiative.

Through the initiative, the partners seek to expand tree cover, restore degraded areas, protect vulnerable hillsides and encourage communities to take a more active role in environmental conservation.

The one-million-tree target reflects the campaign’s broader ambition to combine environmental protection with practical benefits for communities, including improved soil protection, access to fruit and more sustainable use of natural resources.

Wesley Fofana played all 90 minutes of Chelsea's 4-1 defeat at home to Leeds United on Saturday

Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso says defender Wesley Fofana has apologised for a controversial interview he gave on YouTube.

Fofana has been criticised for comments he made in the interview with YouTuber Zach Nani in which he appeared to joke about his penalty miss in a Carabao Cup shootout defeat at Liverpool .

He did not have permission to hold the two-hour interview, which was aired after Chelsea 's humiliating 4-1 defeat at home to rivals Leeds on Saturday, but Alonso said the matter was now "closed".

"It was unfortunate. He has apologised. He knows it was not right, the moment, it was not right, the content," said the Blues boss, who was speaking before Friday's Premier League match at Nottingham Forest .

"We are here to take things seriously. He's said it will not be repeated. We don't want these kind of things and they won't be repeated."

Alonso refused to confirm whether Fofana had been punished by the club, but said "we have addressed that with him."

Interviewer defends Fofana after backlash

Okafor double delivers rare win for Leeds at Chelsea

'Fragile' and 'miles off it' - Alonso's Chelsea honeymoon is over

Fofana's comments followed criticism from fans of his performances this season, including in last weekend's humiliation at the hands of historic rivals Leeds .

But interviewer Nani defended Fofana against the backlash, saying: "People can clearly see he wasn't happy. He admits he didn't play well and says he needs to improve."

The interviewer also defended Fofana's explanation for putting himself forward to take a penalty against Liverpool , saying the defender believed it was his responsibility as one of the senior players on the pitch.

The 25-year-old France defender has often struggled for form and fitness since completing a £70m move from Leicester City in August 2022.

He has made 81 appearances for the club in four years, but has played nine times under new manager Alonso this season.

In that time Chelsea have struggled with defensive frailty, conceding 20 goals in their 11 Premier League games.

They are eighth in the table after falling to a third defeat in their last four league matches.

Uganda yiteguye kwakira icyiciro cya mbere cy'umuti uhendutse wo mu bwoko bushya bw'inshinge zifasha kwirinda kwandura virusi itera SIDA, bikaba bitanga icyizere cy'uko abantu benshi muri Afurika bazashobora kubona uyu muti, dore ko uyu mugabane ari wo wibasiwe cyane n'iyi virusi.

Ikigega Mpuzamahanga gishinzwe kurwanya SIDA, Igituntu na Malariya (Global Fund) kivuga ko icyiciro cya mbere ku isi cy'uyu muti uhendutse, witwa Lenacapavir, cyageze muri Zambia ku wa Gatatu, mu gihe biteganyijwe ko Uganda izawubona mu minsi iri imbere.

Uyu muti, uterwa mu rushinge inshuro ebyiri mu mwaka, ufite ubushobozi bugera hafi ku 100% bwo kurinda umuntu kwandura virusi itera SIDA, bikaba biteganyijwe ko uzajya utwara amadolari 40 gusa ku muntu mu mwaka.

Biteganyijwe ko Zimbabwe izakira uyu muti mu ntangiriro z'umwaka utaha, igakurikirwa n'ibindi bihugu byinshi.

Kugera muri Afurika k'uyu muti uhendutse bibaye nyuma y'umwaka umwe gusa umuti w'umwimerere, wakozwe n'ikigo gikomeye cy'Abanyamerika gikora imiti, Gilead Sciences, utangiye kuboneka muri Afurika yo munsi y'Ubutayu bwa Sahara.

Muri Amerika, umuti w'umwimerere waguraga amadolari agera ku 28.000 ku muntu mu mwaka, igiciro cyatumaga abantu benshi bo mu bihugu bikiri mu nzira y'amajyambere batabasha kuwubona.

Lenacapavir ikora yibanze ku gice kigizwe na protein kirinda virusi itera SIDA, ikayibuza kwiyongera no gufata umubiri w'umuntu.

Mu igeragezwa ry'uyu muti ryabaye intambwe ikomeye mu 2024, ryakorewe ku bakobwa b'ingimbi n'abagore bakiri bato barenga 5.000 muri Uganda no muri Afurika y'Epfo, nta n'umwe mu bahawe uru rushinge wanduye virusi itera SIDA.

Amakuru ya BBC Gahuza ako kanya kuri WhatsApp yawe

Inzobere mu by'ubuzima zivuga ko uru rushinge rufite akarusho gakomeye ugereranyije n'ibinini bisanzwe bikoreshwa mu kwirinda kwandura virusi itera SIDA, bizwi nka PrEP, bigomba gufatwa buri munsi kandi bishobora gutuma ababikoresha bahabwa akato.

Umuryango Mpuzamahanga wita ku Buzima (OMS/WHO) wasabye ko uyu muti ukoreshwa mu kwirinda kwandura virusi itera SIDA muri Nyakanga (7) 2025.

Ikigega Global Fund cyavuze ko kugera muri Africa k'uyu muti ari "intambwe ikomeye" mu kurwanya virusi itera SIDA, kivuga ko kuboneka kwawo ku giciro gito bizafasha kugera ku bandi bantu babarirwa muri za miliyoni bafite ibyago byo kwandura.

Mu itangazo cyasohoye ku wa Gatatu, iki kigega cyagize kiti: "Kohereza iyi miti ni intambwe itigeze ibaho mbere mu kwihutisha no kwagura uburyo bwo kubona umuti uhendutse, ufite ubuziranenge bwizewe kandi ukora neza mu kwirinda kwandura virusi itera SIDA, mu bihugu bifite amikoro make n'aciriritse."

Iki kigega giteganya ko ibihugu 24 bizaba byamaze kwakira uyu muti gushika mu mpera z'uyu mwaka. Ku bufatanye na leta ya Amerika, giteganya kugeza uyu muti ku bantu nibura miliyoni eshatu bitarenze impera z'umwaka wa 2028.

Biteganyijwe ko uyu muti uzaboneka mu bihugu 120 bifite amikoro make n'aciriritse.

Afurika yo munsi y'Ubutayu bwa Sahara ibarizwamo hafi bibiri bya gatatu by'abantu bose babana na virusi itera SIDA ku isi, aho abakobwa b'ingimbi n'abagore bakiri bato bibasiwe cyane kurusha andi matsinda.

Afurika y'Epfo ni cyo gihugu gifite umubare munini w'ababana na virusi itera SIDA ku isi, aho bagera hafi kuri miliyoni umunani. Iki gihugu kiri mu biteganyijwe ko bizakira uru rushinge ruhendutse.

Nk'uko OMS ibivuga, abantu bagera kuri miliyoni 41 ku isi babanaga na virusi itera SIDA mu mwaka ushize, mu gihe abagera ku 570.000 bishwe n'indwara zifitanye isano n'iyi virusi.

Ikwirakwizwa ry'uyu muti rije mu gihe hari impungenge z'uko igabanywa rikomeye ry'inkunga Amerika iha ibihugu byo hanze, ryakozwe n'ubutegetsi bwa Perezida Donald Trump, rishobora kudindiza intambwe imaze guterwa mu myaka ibarirwa muri za mirongo mu kurwanya virusi itera SIDA muri Afurika, aho ibihugu byinshi bishingira cyane ku nkunga mpuzamahanga mu bikorwa byo kuyirinda no kuvura abayanduye.

Umuryango w'Abibumbye ufite intego yo kuba warakuyeho SIDA nk'ikibazo kibangamiye ubuzima rusange bw'abaturage bitarenze umwaka wa 2030.

MN202611_186hmz23cx8.t:
Rwanda’s music stars Bwiza and Bruce Melodie have been encouraged to use their growing influence beyond entertainment to promote national pride, strengthen unity among Rwandans abroad and share positive stories about their homeland as they prepare to perform in Zambia.

The message was delivered by Rwanda’s Ambassador to Zambia, Emmanuel Bugingo, who welcomed the two artists upon their arrival at Kenneth Kaunda International Airport on Thursday afternoon, November 26, 2026, ahead of their much-anticipated concert scheduled for Saturday, November 28.

During their meeting, Ambassador Bugingo welcomed the musicians and assured them of his support throughout their stay, while emphasizing the important role artists can play in representing their country on international platforms.

He urged Bwiza and Bruce Melodie to always carry the pride of their country wherever they go, using their music, public influence and interactions with audiences to build connections and strengthen the image of their homeland.

“Always carry the pride of your country at heart. Your music and the platforms you have should go beyond entertainment to unite Rwandans, share positive stories about your homeland with the diaspora community and contribute to the development of your country,” he encouraged them.

The Ambassador also highlighted the potential of music as a powerful tool for bringing people together, particularly among Rwandans living abroad, while encouraging the artists to inspire a sense of belonging and shared responsibility towards their country’s development.

For Bwiza and Bruce Melodie, the Zambian performance presents an opportunity to take Rwandan music to a wider audience, connect with fans in the diaspora and showcase the country’s growing creative talent beyond its borders.

Their visit also reflects the role of cultural diplomacy in strengthening people-to-people relations, with musicians increasingly serving as informal ambassadors who can introduce their country’s identity, creativity and stories to international audiences.

As they prepare to take the stage on Saturday, the two performers are expected not only to entertain their fans but also to represent the creativity and cultural identity of their homeland

MN202611_1gn83haoqv0.t:
A delegation of French military experts specialising in engineering and explosive ordnance disposal has visited the Rwanda Defence Force (RDF) Engineer Command headquarters, in a move aimed at strengthening cooperation and sharing expertise in military engineering.

The delegation was received on November 26, 2026, by the Deputy Commander of RDF Engineer Command, Col Marie Claire Muragijimana.

The visit provides an opportunity for the two military institutions to exchange knowledge, explore areas of mutual interest and strengthen professional collaboration in military engineering, particularly in technical operations and explosive ordnance management.

Discussions are expected to focus on sharing technical experience, improving operational capabilities and identifying opportunities for future cooperation, including possible joint training programmes and professional exchanges.

Such engagement could contribute to strengthening the technical capacity of RDF engineering personnel, particularly in specialised areas that support military operations, infrastructure development and explosive hazard management.

The visit also reflects the importance of continued defence cooperation between the two countries, with military-to-military engagements providing a platform for exchanging expertise and building institutional relationships.

MN202611_lbkqg0cnum.t:
Laura Freigang has scored 17 goals in 45 appearances for Germany

Germany international Laura Freigang has been suspended from football for 16 months over issues with three drugs tests.

The 28-year-old will miss the Women's World Cup next summer and is banned from all football activity until after 7 October 2027.

The 16-month suspension begins from the date of notification by the German Football Association (DFB), which took place in June.

The World Anti-Doping Agency (Wada), the National Anti-Doping Agency (Nada), DFB and Freigang reached a dispute resolution agreement.

The dispute said Entracht Frankfurt forward Freigang committed three reporting and/or testing failures between 11 March 2025 and 23 February 2026.

Freigang can return to training two months prior to the end of the suspension period but cannot play matches until after 7 October.

All personal records of appearances, goals, assists or other statistics from 23 February 2026 are nullified, though Frankfurt's results are unaffected.

This season Freigang has scored six goals and provided two assists in 11 starts in the Frauen-Bundesliga.

Since joining the club in 2020, the striker has scored 107 goals in 187 appearances and was in the Germany squad for October's friendly victories over Australia and Japan.

In a club statement , external , Franfurt said they will "begin discussions shortly to determine the terms of her future employment relationship".

Freigang's current contract is due to expire on 30 June 2027.

Frankfurt's director of women's football Katharina Kiel said: "The agreement now reached provides clarity and planning security in a process unprecedented for Eintracht Frankfurt - for us as a club, but above all for Laura.

"The way she and the team have handled the situation in recent months, and how Laura personally led by example with her performance on the pitch during a very difficult time, deserves the highest recognition.

"The identified shortcomings, despite the agreement to settle the dispute, have resulted in a suspension, which means the loss of a key player."

MN202611_1npaky63hf0.t:
Disgraced former BBC News presenter Huw Edwards has given his first interviews since being convicted in 2024 for making indecent images of children.

Edwards is seen saying he believes "silence is toxic" in a clip of a podcast released by the Observer newspaper, and he has also been interviewed for a Channel 4 documentary.

Edwards, formerly the BBC's most senior news presenter, pleaded guilty in July 2024 to three counts of making indecent images of children and was given a suspended six-month prison sentence.

A government minister, Anna Turley, told LBC , external she was "deeply uncomfortable" with the interviews, and that "for too long, so many of these people in the public eye have been able to have a sort of free pass".

During the court case, Edwards admitted having 41 images, which were sent to him on WhatsApp – including some showing a victim aged between seven and nine.

In a trailer for the Channel 4 programme, director Patrick Forbes asks what he was doing, to which Edwards replies: "Oh, you want me to analyse what I was doing? I mean, seriously?"

Asked again, he replies: "I'd lost the plot."

The interviewer challenges him by saying: "Well, come on," to which Edwards angrily replies: "No, not come on."

Despite that apparent combative stance, Edwards wrote on his blog on Thursday: "I want viewers to know that I did not avoid a single question, and that I answered each as honestly as I could, including those about deeply personal matters: my relationships, my temperament, my sexuality."

Explaining his reasons for giving the interviews, he said: "My difficulties became front-page news, and the account that took hold was, in places, misleading or simply untrue.

"Those promoting false narratives are also, unsurprisingly, the ones questioning my right to set the record straight.

"I was left with a choice: to let that faulty account stand forever, or to offer my own."

In a statement, Forbes said it was "an important film to make".

"It's rare to find a subject that touches on so many significant contemporary issues – whether it's celebrity culture or the power of the media – as well as enduring questions about crime and punishment," he said.

In the clip for his separate interview with the Observer and its Tortoise Investigates podcast, Edwards is seen saying: "Lots of the advice I've had is just be quiet, don't say anything."

Interviewer Ceri Thomas, a former editor of the BBC's Today programme and Panorama, said he was "just deeply curious about how it was that a man of such prominence had got himself into this unbelievable, terrible fix".

Rosamund Urwin, chief news correspondent for rival paper the Sunday Times, who jointly led the paper's 2023 investigation into Russell Brand, wrote on social media: "An 'unbelievable terrible fix' is quite the euphemism for someone viewing child abuse images of victims as young as 7."

Tortoise Media, which owns the Observer, has a deal to make some podcasts available on BBC Sounds, but the BBC said the Huw Edwards series would not be among them.

Channel 4 and the Observer said Edwards had received no payment for the interviews or had any editorial input.

MN202611_xi0bxot8ei.t:
Sir Paul Smith was hosting an event during his book tour

Fashion firm Paul Smith has told the BBC it is committed to animal welfare after protesters disrupted a talk by the brand's founder in his home city.

Two supporters of People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals (PETA) interrupted the event hosted by Sir Paul Smith at Nottingham's Broadway Cinema on Wednesday.

The protest follows investigations by PETA into alleged animal cruelty at mohair production facilities in South Africa and Lesotho, including one it said had links to a Paul Smith supplier.

The company said it upholds the highest standards of animal welfare across its supply chain.

The animal rights group said the pair were removed from the event by security.

In a statement, Elisa Allen, PETA's vice president of programmes, said the brand had failed to act, prompting PETA to take its message directly to the man behind the label.

PETA has called on the brand to stop using mohair in its clothing

Mohair is a fibre made from the hair of Angora goats and is commonly used in clothing.

Smith said all its mohair was certified under the Responsible Mohair Standard (RMS) and that it would take relevant action if suppliers were found to be in breach of its animal welfare standards.

A spokesperson for Paul Smith said: "At Paul Smith, we uphold the highest standards of animal welfare across our supply chain, and all our suppliers are required to adhere to these standards."

"Every batch of mohair used by Paul Smith is certified to the Responsible Mohair Standard (RMS), the internationally recognised standard for responsible mohair production.

"If there is evidence that a supplier has not upheld these standards, we will take appropriate action in line with our ethical commitments."

PETA said its investigators had filmed goats being injured during shearing, including at mohair facilities under the RMS.

Allen said: "Hundreds of fashion brands have already ditched mohair, and Paul Smith must do the right thing and follow suit.

"PETA also urges shoppers to do their part by leaving cruelty on the rack and opting for animal-free materials such as cotton, hemp and bamboo."

Other brands, such as Helmut Lang, G-Star, Gap, Fred Perry, Barbour, UNIQLO, and Zara, have already banned mohair.

MN202611_10deke67gv0.t:
Sir Gregor Smith has cited health reasons for his decision

Sir Gregor Smith, who has resigned as Scotland's chief medical officer, was appointed to the role when his predecessor resigned for breaking Covid rules.

He leaves the position having become caught up in a very different controversy.

Smith said he had taken a "personal decision" to stand down because he did not have the "good mental health" necessary to continue.

One government source suggested to me that Smith had taken the right decision and that it was better than anyone having to ask him to go.

John Swinney insists medical chief was not told to go amid growing NHS Grampian scandal

'My wife would still be alive if NHS Grampian had followed medical guidelines'

Chief medical officer Gregor Smith resigns on mental health grounds

He came under pressure because he knew about the 2022 report into liver and pancreas surgery at Aberdeen Royal Infirmary which identified 19 potentially avoidable deaths.

That report was never published by the Scottish government or NHS Grampian.

Politicians and journalists have not unreasonably wanted to know what he did with the information and why.

By his own account, it was almost accidental that he had any involvement in responding to the report.

He told a Holyrood committee that it was "unusual" for this kind of issue to be referred to him.

He said he was contacted by a senior official at NHS Grampian who also proposed an action plan that included temporarily suspending this type of surgery.

Smith seems to have considered this "appropriate" and called a wider meeting to discuss the matter and ensured the then health secretary, Humza Yousaf, was briefed.

He was kept informed until surgery restarted on the advice of an external expert in May 2023 and according to what Smith told MSPs on Wednesday he was "not directly involved in any further work".

His disengagement became problematic because we now know this type of surgery was suspended on two further occasions. Cases are currently being referred to NHS Lothian.

Strictly speaking, it is not the chief medical officer's job to supervise the performance of any surgical department.

But had he chosen to keep an eye on things, or ensure someone in the Scottish government did, the current crisis might have been averted.

Dr Mohammed Habib leaked a 2022 report into concerns at NHS Grampian

The 2022 review certainly did not end concerns with how liver and pancreas surgery was being performed in Aberdeen.

These concerns have now been laid bare by one of the surgeons in that team, Dr Mohammed Habib, who went public last week.

That has prompted the Scottish government to order an independent review, led by an experienced KC, to find out who knew what, and when, what they did and why.

Ministers are not convinced that somehow the report - or at least its key findings - could not have been made public by NHS Grampian.

They are not satisfied with some of the answers they have been given from the health board including the idea that patient confidentiality prevented them going public.

The review will have big questions to ask of officials at both NHS Grampian and in the Scottish government. It will also be able to question the role of ministers too.

Labour wants Holyrood to commission the review so that the Scottish government is not seen to be marking its own homework.

Both they and the Conservatives seem to want to expand the terms of the review to take account of other distressing stories emerging from NHS Grampian.

Dr Habib is worried about the outcomes in 62 liver and pancreatic cases where he believes there may have been either avoidable death or other avoidable harms.

There will be a full debate about what form the inquiry should take at Holyrood on Tuesday.

It's not clear how long the review process will take, what further investigations may be required or indeed if anyone else may leave their jobs over what's gone wrong in NHS Grampian and how problems have been handled.

MN202611_1x78quy1nbs.t:
Campaigners worried the mining could impact sea turtles in the area

The Trump administration's plans to begin deep-sea mining in the Pacific have hit a second legal setback after a federal judge ruled plans to lease areas of sea-floor off the Northern Mariana Islands violated the Endangered Species Act (ESA).

The court's decision follows a similar ruling over a proposed lease sale off American Samoa.

Opposition groups who lodged the Northern Mariana Islands lawsuit said they were concerned deep-sea mining could cause long-term damage to the ocean ecosystem.

The US government has said it wants to start deep-sea mining to enable access to critical minerals and to counter China's growing influence over crucial components needed for electronics.

The administration had planned to put up for sale leases for the Northern Mariana Islands on 16 December 2026.

It is not clear what will happen next as the administration chose not to recognise the first court ruling and went ahead with the sale of two leases covering 13 million hectares (more than 30 million acres) off American Samoa.

Opponents have vowed to challenge that sale.

Ruling on the Northern Mariana Islands case, District judge Jill Aiko Otake said the defendants, the National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS), which provided the expert opinion behind the lease sales, and Howard Lutnick, who was named in his capacity as head of the department that oversees the agency, had failed to consider the potential effects that could follow once the leases were issued.

The ruling explained that while these leases would only authorise the leaseholder to conduct preliminary surveying activity, they might eventually allow the leaseholder to actually mine the ocean's floor.

The potential impact of that mining had not been addressed in the biodiversity assessment which was used to sign off the lease sales, the ruling said.

Using machines to mine for minerals in the deep ocean is highly controversial.

Some scientists have raised concerns that deep-sea mining could damage little-understood deep-ocean ecosystems, though industry supporters argue the environmental effects remain uncertain and require further study.

Deep-sea mining uses vacuum technology to suck up nodules from the muddy sediment. , external However, this process also removes organisms that grow on them, including corals and sponges, many of which cannot grow anywhere else.

In one study of the impact of deep-sea mining, researchers found more than 4,000 animals, 90% of which were new species, living on the seafloor in a remote area of the Pacific Ocean.

Some critics of the industry fear that before we have the chance to explore the full nature of life in the undiscovered deep ocean, it could be endangered.

The leatherback sea turtle is listed as endangered under the ESA

Norway was the first country in the world to approve commercial-scale deep-sea mining in 2024 .

Over 2,000 of the world's scientists met in 2025 to review the data on ocean health and they recommended governments halt deep sea exploration while further research on the impacts was carried out.

More than 30 countries supported this position and called for a moratorium.

Shortly before that meeting, President Trump published executive orders to push ahead with mining and "unleash America's offshore critical minerals and resources".

He said "these resources are key to strengthening our economy, securing our energy future, and reducing dependence on foreign suppliers for critical minerals".

Part of the plan aims to "counter China's growing influence over seabed mineral resources".

Deep-sea mining targets polymetallic nodules , external – potato-sized rocks found over 4,000 metres below the ocean surface.

These contain minerals including nickel, cobalt, and manganese which are used in manufactruring electronics and batteries.

They are also important for renewable energy technologies to tackle climate change, including solar panels, wind turbines and electric vehicles.

The International Energy Agency predicts that demand for the minerals could at least double by 2040. , external

The National Marine Fisheries Service and US Department of Commerce have been approached for comment.

Calvert-Lewin joined Leeds United in 2025 after nine years at Everton

Dominic Calvert-Lewin has signed a new contract to stay with Leeds United until 2029.

The former Everton striker, 29, has five goals and one assist so far in the Premier League this season, with Daniel Farke's side sitting 11th in the table.

Confirmation of Calvert-Lewin's deal follows speculation about his future at the club, with reports that he was interesting Manchester United .

Calvert-Lewin scored 15 goals across all competitions during his first season at Elland Road after joining in August 2025, and the form earned him an England recall in March.

He was also called up by Thomas Tuchel this autumn and came off the bench in England's wins against Czech Republic and Spain.

He scored a penalty and had an assist in Leeds ' 4-1 thrashing of Chelsea on Saturday.

Peter Krueger will lead Travelodge after a turbulent few months

Travelodge has appointed a former Tui executive to become its new boss from the start of December.

The former CEO of the Oxfordshire-based budget hotel chain Jo Boydell quit in the summer after safety issues were raised at many of its sites.

A woman staying at its Maidenhead hotel was sexually assaulted in December 2022 after a man lied to staff to get a key card to her room. Kyran Smith was jailed for seven-and-a-half years for the attack .

Peter Krueger will start his new role at Travelodge on Tuesday, replacing interim chief Ray Reidy who has led the company since Boydell quit.

Listen to the latest news from Berkshire

She left the company after facing significant criticism over the handling of the sexual assault incident and wider safety concerns.

It prompted former prime minister Sir Keir Starmer to urge her to "seriously engage" with the government on the issue after she cancelled a meeting with MPs.

An independent review by Paul Greaney KC published in October found the sexual assault victim was treated in a "disgraceful" way and "fundamentally failed" by the hotel chain.

In an update on Thursday, Reidy said the business is "continuing to make further investments into room security, and the safety and security of our guests remains our top priority".

Travelodge said it will be making additional investments in room security "over the course of 2027".

MN202611_fm01sxw16n.t:
Hanna Hattab has refereed in a number of competitions run by the Asian Football Confederation

Claims that a referee was drunk during an Asian Football Confederation (AFC) Champions League Two match are "entirely unfounded", officials say.

Syrian referee Hanna Hattab was replaced at half-time of the match between Iran's Gol Gohar and Al Jazira of the United Arab Emirates.

Reports claimed Gol Gohar staff accused the referee of being drunk following what has been described as some erratic decision-making in the first half.

Iranian news agency ISNA quoted one club official as saying: "The referee was not in a normal state," and suggesting they would not have played on had the referee not been removed.

Accusations of drunkenness were also widely shared on social media.

But Hattab, who is part of the AFC's elite refereeing group, has released a statement denying the allegation, saying he has been defamed and threatening legal action.

The fourth official took over for the second half, with Al Jazira winning the match.

Hattab said he will be "issuing an official statement that clarifies all the details and facts related to what happened".

Omani sports journalist Issa Said, who covers Asian competitions, claimed on social media that what happened to Hattab was "due to a drop in his blood sugar, which caused him to lose concentration and focus".

"He underwent a medical examination after the match and was not intoxicated, contrary to what has been circulating."

In their statement on the match, which was played in Asia's second tier continental competition, the Syrian Football Association backed Hattab.

"Following an assessment of his health, it has been confirmed - contrary to various claims circulating on social media - that the reports regarding his situation are entirely unfounded," they wrote.

"The Committee reiterates its unwavering support for him and is committed to thoroughly investigating all details and circumstances surrounding the incident."

MN202611_ebgb76cakw.t:
England Under-21s won Euro 2025 with an extra-time win in Slovakia against Germany

Lee Carsley has urged his England Under-21s to create a legacy as they aim for a third straight European title.

The Young Lions - who have won the past two European Championships in 2023 and 2025 under Carsley - have been drawn in Group A against France, Poland and co-hosts Serbia at Euro 2027.

Only Italy have won three successive European Under-21 tournaments - between 1992 and 1996 - but that was when just eight teams competed at the finals and not the current 16.

Head coach Carsley told BBC Sport: "The players I am privileged to coach and work with have a great opportunity to make history with three in a row in this format and create their own legacy within the under-21s."

He was speaking after Thursday's draw in Belgrade, with Serbia hosting the tournament with Albania.

"This group of players are in a really unique position and it will be a while before another group will be in this position," said Carsley.

"Let's go for it. Why not? Go all out to try to win it. That's what we're going to do. We have the players who can do that.

"They are highly motivated. We have seen that in the last two tournaments we have had, the players were so determined to win every game and it makes it a lot easier from a coaching point of view."

England will open their campaign against France - who they beat 3-2 in Bristol last week - on 16 June in Leskovac before facing Serbia in Belgrade on 19 June.

The Young Lions stay in the Serbian capital for their final group game against Poland on Tuesday, 22 June.

MN202611_1udnmpam2n.t:
Protests on the streets of France over students' concerns and the cost of living have been marked by looting and unrest in recent weeks

France's political mainstream faces wipe-out at the presidential election in April-May 2027, unless it acts fast to choose who it wishes to stand.

With every poll confirming the dominance of hard-right and hard-left leaders Marine Le Pen and Jean-Luc Mélenchon, candidates of the middle-ground – the old "legacy" parties – are being squeezed out of the game.

In theory any contender from centre-right or centre-left who was chosen in the first multi-candidate round of voting in April should be in a strong position to win in the play-off a fortnight later.

That is because at their separate ends of the spectrum both Le Pen and Mélenchon have more people who oppose than support them.

But personal rivalries, lack of preparation and differing political visions have so far put paid to any hope of a meaningful challenge.

"The game in the centre is totally blocked," says political writer François Fressoz at the left-leaning Le Monde newspaper. "The partisans of reason have lost their reason."

On the left – the old Socialist Party and its acolytes – there is at least agreement on a candidate: European Parliament MP Raphaël Glucksmann.

His problem is that allies who he might once have counted on – Greens, Communists and other small left-wing parties, not to mention many Socialist voters – are being pulled inexorably into the Mélenchon orbit.

The protests started as an expression of anger at conditions in high schools

In the last two weeks, Green party leader Marine Tondelier, a majority of Communist parliamentary deputies and one-time Socialist presidential hopeful Benoît Hamon have all thrown in their lot with the leader of France Unbowed (LFI).

Another prominent figure of the left – François Ruffin – has also withdrawn from the race, bowing to the unbowed Mélenchon's now almost total command of the field.

So with the soft-left emasculated, the main hope for an alternative to Le Pen and Mélenchon has to be focused on the right. But here the prospects – which until recently seemed bright – are now clouded with gloom.

"A Mélenchon–Le Pen duel in round two is not yet inevitable," says Guillaume Tabard, political analyst at the conservative Le Figaro newspaper. "But it is looking increasingly probable."

In recent weeks the poll ratings of the main centre-right hopeful Edouard Philippe – a former prime minister under President Macron – have fallen sharply, and he is now consistently placed behind Mélenchon in the first round of the vote. Marine Le Pen is way ahead of both.

Other candidates for command of this centre-right "space" are circling. They include another former Macron prime minister, Gabriel Attal; the leader of the right-wing Republicans (and former Macron interior minister), Bruno Retailleau; and now – a surprise new challenger – the mayor of Cannes, David Lisnard.

David Lisnard (centre) has seen membership of his micro-party Nouvelle Energie jump to more than 100,000

Lisnard, who stands on a liberal economic platform of less state and lower taxes, has emerged from nowhere to become the man of the hour. Membership of his micro-party Nouvelle Energie (New Energy) has shot up to more than 100,000, and he is being taken seriously as a possible Philippe replacement.

But this very multiplicity of names – not to mention others like judoka Teddy Riner, journalist Natacha Polony and former prime minister Dominique de Villepin – betrays the essential weakness of the centre-right challenge.

According to veteran commentator Nicolas Baverez, "If you want to win an election, it's quite simple: you need a strategy, a programme, and activists. Right now in the space between Le Pen and Mélenchon we have none of that: there is a total vacuum.

"The most glaring absence is digital. Mélenchon especially, but Le Pen too, are running extremely effective social media campaigns. In the middle… nothing."

Guillaume Tabard agrees that the lack of a shared platform is proving a serious handicap.

"In recent weeks we have seen Marine Le Pen issue her manifesto proposals for reforming pensions. We have seen Jean-Luc Mélenchon publish his programme in a best-selling book," he says.

"What do we have in between? Arguments about names and polling figures and whether or not there should be a primary. It's not, to put it mildly, an encouraging start."

For Fressoz, "There is no-one in the centre who is taking up the fight. When Le Pen makes her proposals about pensions, there is no-one saying, 'Hang on, that doesn't add up!'. Macron – who did after all take her on and beat her – is said to be furious."

Any mention of Macron, though, is most unwelcome for the camp that nominally is his heir. Philippe, Attal and Retailleau all served under a president who Baverez now calls "as toxic as Trump", so deep is his unpopularity in the country. Lisnard, by contrast, makes much of his refusal to serve under Macron – but he faces another handicap.

According to Fressoz, "Lisnard has shot up in the polls because he is on the right of the right, and there is always an appetite for a figure who is not Le Pen, but who speaks her kind of language on immigration.

"But Lisnard is an economic liberal, and in France that is a minority taste. He'll have his moment but then he will deflate."

Emmanuel Macron is now considered a politically toxic figure in France

With five months to go to until the election, all is not lost for the mainstream. Optimists in its ranks say that come the new year, opinion polls will start settling behind one or other centre-right candidate, and the others will feel obliged to step aside.

Talk of a centre-right primary – as occurred ahead of the 2017 election – is beginning to ebb. The two strongest candidates, Philippe and Lisnard, are opposed. Lisnard says he supports one but his conditions are designed to be unacceptable to the rest. Retailleau and Attal are in favour – but that, says Tabard, is "mainly as a way to keep their hopes alive."

In theory then it is possible a name will emerge in January or February, and start pulling behind him (or less likely, her) the mass of voters who do not want a disruptive radical as France's next head of state.

For Fressoz of Le Monde, "After years of Macron's 'neither left nor right', the left and right are once again shaping French politics. But now it is the extremes who are in control."

Le Pen and Mélenchon have both already run three times for the presidency. Their visions were defined long ago, their strategies laid, their activists trained. Polarisation is their friend, so is the social tension of recent weeks, and both are undisputed masters in their own camps.

The 2027 dénouement has been in their sights for years. That is their massive advantage.

At the Nyakabingo mine north of Kigali, huge amounts of Tungsten being extracted for whole export to U.S. by Trinity Metals (Photos by The New Times)

Rwanda earned more than seven times as much from tungsten exports in the first half of 2026 as it did during the same period last year.

The mineral’s average export price surged by 369.1%, according to data issued by the National Bank of Rwanda (BNR) Governor Soraya Hakuziyaremye.

she was speaking Thursday during the release the October 2026 Monetary Policy and Financial Stability Statement (MPFSS)

The average price of a kilogramme of tungsten, also known as wolfram, rose to $75.8 in the first six months of 2026, from $16.2 in the corresponding period of 2025.

The increase helped push Rwanda’s tungsten export earnings to $139 million, up from $19.1 million in the first half of last year, representing a rise of 628.6%.

The performance stands in sharp contrast with coffee and tea, two of Rwanda’s traditional agricultural exports, whose average export prices declined over the same period.

Coffee fetched an average of $5.4 per kilogramme, down 5.5% from $5.7 a year earlier. Tea prices edged down by 0.3%, from $2.9 to $2.9 per kilogramme.

The figures are contained in the October 2026 Monetary Policy and Financial Stability Statement published by the National Bank of Rwanda, which compares export performance in the first half of 2026 with the same period in 2025.

Tungsten is widely used in manufacturing hard cutting and mining tools, including drill bits and saw blades. Its exceptional hardness, high density and resistance to extreme heat also make it valuable in aircraft engines, electrical components, medical equipment and industrial machinery.

All that is mined in Rwanda is exported to U.S.

Tungsten was not the only mineral to record strong growth. It is primarily mined from Nyakabingo mine, Africa’s biggest Tungsten mine, north of the capital Kigali by Trinity Metals.

Rwanda’s other two major mineral exports, cassiterite (tin) and coltan, also benefited from higher prices and increased export volumes.

The average price of cassiterite rose by 47.2%, from $21.9 to $32.3 per kilogramme. Its export earnings increased by 62.4%, reaching $103.3 million from $63.6 million.

Coltan recorded an even stronger performance in value terms. Its average export price increased by 65.3%, from $47.2 to $78.1 per kilogramme, while earnings rose by 165.9%, from $60.1 million to $159.8 million.

Coltan generated the highest export earnings among the three minerals, followed by tungsten and cassiterite.

Combined, the three minerals brought Rwanda $402.1 million in the first half of 2026, compared with $142.8 million during the same period last year, an increase of 181.7%.

Their combined export volume also grew by 32.3%, from 5,400 tonnes to 7,100 tonnes, showing that the rise in earnings was supported by both higher prices and increased quantities exported.

The performance of coffee and tea was more subdued, although the two products recorded different results in export earnings.

Rwanda earned $41.1 million from coffee exports in the first half of 2026, down 4.8% from $43.2 million a year earlier. The volume exported remained almost unchanged at 7,600 tonnes.

The decline in earnings therefore largely reflected the lower average price received for coffee.

Tea, on the other hand, generated $67.3 million, an increase of 3.4% from $65.2 million in the first half of 2025. This was supported by a 3.7% increase in export volume, from 22,600 tonnes to 23,400 tonnes, despite the slight decline in its average price.

The figures show that higher export volumes can help maintain or increase earnings even when prices are stagnant or falling.

Gold and other commodities also recorded significant price increases on international markets.

Gold prices rose by 52.5% in the first half of 2026 compared with the same period last year, while the broader category of precious metals increased by 64.8%.

The World Bank projected a further 36.5% increase in gold prices and a 42.4% rise in precious metals prices for the full year.

International tin prices also increased by 56.3%, reflecting the favourable market conditions for mineral producers.

Food commodity prices rose by a more modest 5.1%, while cereals increased by 1.7%. Fertilizer prices, meanwhile, climbed by 29.9%, potentially increasing production costs for farmers and agricultural businesses that depend on imported inputs.

The strong performance of minerals contributed significantly to Rwanda’s overall export growth.

According to BNR, merchandise exports increased by 52.1% to $1.2565 billion in the first half of 2026, from $826.3 million in the same period of 2025.

Traditional exports, which include coffee, tea and minerals, rose by 101.3% to $514.4 million. The increase was driven primarily by mineral receipts, which grew by 181.7%.

Non-traditional exports, including horticultural products, processed foods, construction materials and locally manufactured goods, also increased by 31.7% to $279.1 million.

Re-exports rose by 34.9% to $373.4 million.

Despite the strong export performance, Rwanda’s merchandise trade deficit widened slightly by 1.1% to $1.552 billion, as imports increased by 18.9% to $2.8085 billion.

The export-to-import ratio, however, improved to 44.7% from 35% in the first half of 2025, meaning exports covered a larger share of the country’s import bill.

The figures underline the growing contribution of minerals to Rwanda’s foreign-exchange earnings, at a time when coffee and tea are receiving little or no improvement in export prices.

However, the sharp rise in mineral prices also raises questions about how much of the current growth can be sustained if international market prices change. The increase in earnings reflects both price movements and higher export volumes, and does not by itself establish how much additional value is being retained through local processing.

MN202611_12ce3846zoy.t:
There was none of last April's fanfare, the Rose Garden reveal, the gameshow blue board or "Liberation Day" rhetoric surrounding Trump's tariff announcement this week.

Instead there is something rather tentative about this latest exercise with talk of further negotiations.

"We expect to have a broad, even a plurilateral negotiation to talk about excess capacity and how to resolve it," US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer told CNBC.

Around the world the view is that this week's announcement is an attempt to shore up the domestic legal underpinning of these tariffs, more than a fundamental change in the Trump trade agenda.

The tariffs are also not due to come in until January or possibly February, after a period of consultation. There has already been eight months of process and hearings, and the rates announced are upper ceilings, often up for negotiation. It's quite the contrast to the overnight shock meted out to the world last April.

Still, the USA is making the argument that large swathes of the rest of the world, including allies, are harming the US goods trade position by supporting their own industries. This is the basis for the tariffs, in large part replacing the previous tariffs justified on "forced labour" provisions.

The UK, which was unaffected by the new tariff announcements, remains caught by the forced labour provisions, albeit at a rate of 10% extra on global tariffs. There was no move in response to the UK's digital services tax.

It means for many important countries there are now two legal bases upon which the Trump tariffs rest, after the Supreme Court struck down the original emergency basis earlier this year. A group of 25 states has taken the Trump administration to court to strike down the forced labour tariffs.

The tariffs will have to be finalised under a Democrat Congress, which has influence, but not power. The Speaker-designate Hakeem Jeffries said this week that the new House would in its first 100 days "move aggressively to… repeal the Trump tariffs".

The Chinese rate of 20% is the truce rate from last year's Trump-Xi deal. The truce is due to expire in mid-January. Beijing's response was muted, no retaliation, criticism of industrial overcapacity as a "false issue", and a call to implement the Xi-Trump deal. The leverage over China has weakened, with the US share of its exports dropping to around 10% this year, down from 15%, just two years ago, and 19% in 2018.

US announces new tariffs on host of countries including China

New UK-EU treaty has 10-year termination clause

Faisal Islam: This cost-cutting UK-EU deal doesn't mean lower prices will follow

However, the most interesting spot to focus on is closer to home for Trump. Over half of Canada tariffs are authorised under "Section 338" of the 1930s Smoot-Hawley act. There is already a Senate Bill to repeal them, and it is possible that there would be enough rebel Republicans in the House and Senate to threaten to over-ride any Presidential veto. The incoming Senate Finance Committee chair Ron Wyden last week said Democrats were focussed on "figuring out a way to beat Trump and his veto".

Before that an interim deal is being sought, and Democrat senators such as Chris Coons are appearing on Canadian TV, telling CBC , external : "Frankly, if you can get an interim deal, I'd take it, and then put it to us in the new majority to legislate an even better deal."

The rest of world is watching the machinations in Washington and also looking beyond Donald Trump's tenure.

It pays to look at how the initial Trump trade-quake has reshaped the pattern of world trade already.

The rest of the world has rerouted its trade flows around Donald Trump's tariff wall, proving far more resilient than expected. In cash terms, China's exports so far in 2026 are down about 8% on 2024, but that is more than 25 times made up for by its increased exports to everywhere else.

Canada has seen flat exports to the USA since tariffs, fewer cars and lumber, but pricier flows of energy. Its exports, especially commodities, to the rest of the world have rocketed.

This means that next month's G20 summit at the president's Miami resort is an important moment. In general US allies have not rocked the boat, accepting the lower level of tariffs as part of the new reality. Could the middle powers choose to upset their host in Florida next month?

The bigger question however, is how much the Democrats decide to keep of the America First trade agenda. It will not be all, but nor will it be nothing. Economists now expect some of these tariffs to stay in place for years.

KIGALI – For years, changing mobile network operators has come with a practical cost giving up a familiar phone number, updating contacts and, in some cases, adjusting services tied to that number.

But following Cabinet on Thursday, November 26, subscribers will be able to move from one telecommunications operator to another while keeping their existing phone numbers and mobile money accounts if they are not satisfied.

As part of efforts to expand consumer choice and strengthen competition in the sector, this change could make it harder for telecom companies to retain customers simply because switching providers is inconvenient.

Instead of customers having to weigh the inconvenience of changing numbers against the benefits of another network, providers may increasingly have to persuade them to stay through the quality, affordability and reliability of their services.

The stakes are significant in a market where two operators account for virtually all mobile-cellular subscriptions.

Rwanda had 14.5 million active mobile subscriptions by the end of June 2026, according to the Rwanda Utilities Regulatory Authority (RURA). MTN Rwandacell held 65.8 per cent of the market, while Airtel Rwanda accounted for 34.2 per cent. These figures represent subscriptions, not individual users.

The program comes as mobile services have become deeply embedded in everyday economic activity, extending beyond calls and text messages to internet access, payments and money transfers.

RURA recorded 8.9 million SIM cards linked to active mobile money accounts in June 2026, up from 7.7 million a year earlier. The figures underline why retaining mobile money accounts alongside phone numbers is an important part of the proposed portability arrangement.

For many subscribers, changing networks is not simply a matter of replacing a SIM card; it can affect services used to send, receive and store money.

By allowing customers to retain both their numbers and mobile money accounts, the program seeks to reduce some of the barriers that can discourage subscribers from moving to a competing provider.

The regulatory framework also provides that neither the operator a subscriber is leaving nor the one they are joining can charge for transferring the number. A replacement SIM card may attract a fee, but it cannot exceed the applicable SIM-swap price.

That could give customers greater leverage when choosing between operators, particularly where they are dissatisfied with network coverage, service interruptions, customer care or the cost of services.

It could also encourage providers to pay closer attention to customer experience, since dissatisfied subscribers would have fewer practical reasons to remain.

However, portability alone does not guarantee lower prices or better services. Its impact will depend on how easily customers can switch, whether the process is affordable and how effectively operators respond to the possibility of losing subscribers.

The Cabinet announcement comes after RURA had already established a regulatory framework for mobile number portability. The regulator lists a regulation governing the service among its telecommunications instruments, with the document published in August 2025.

Under the rules, subscribers will have to request the transfer through the operator they wish to join, provide identification and verify ownership of their existing numbers through an SMS confirmation.

In March 2025, a request for proposals issued by the Rwanda Mobile Network Operators Consortium, on behalf of RURA, sought a provider to administer the number-portability service.

The document said operators would be required to implement the service and identified the end of November 2025 as the anticipated launch date.

The Cabinet announcement therefore raises an important question about the program’s current stage and when subscribers will actually be able to use it. The statement did not provide an operational date or explain the procedures customers will follow when moving between networks.

The regulation also requires subscribers to remain with a new operator for at least 90 days before requesting another transfer. However, the Cabinet announcement did not indicate when the program will become operational.

That leaves questions about the readiness of the system, particularly how mobile money accounts, balances and transaction records will be handled when customers change networks.

MN202611_1u2c790lgr6.t:
BRALIRWA’s existing facility in Rubavu District, on border with DR Congo

BRALIRWA Plc is planning to establish a new beverage manufacturing plant in Rwamagana Industrial Zone, with the proposed facility expected to produce up to 250 million litres of beer and soft drinks annually.

The project, known as the Greenfield Brewery Project, received government approval after Cabinet endorsed an investment agreement between the Government of Rwanda and BRALIRWA at a meeting chaired by President Paul Kagame on November 26, 2026.

President Paul Kagame chaired the Cabinet Meeting at Village Urugwiro.

According to preliminary technical information about the project, the planned facility will have an ultimate annual production capacity of 2.5 million hectolitres, equivalent to 250 million litres.

Of this capacity, 1.5 million hectolitres, or 150 million litres, will be dedicated to beer production, while the remaining one million hectolitres, equivalent to 100 million litres, will be used for soft drinks.

The project will be established in Rwamagana Industrial Zone in Eastern Province, adding to BRALIRWA’s existing beverage manufacturing operations in Rwanda.

The proposed facility will include a brewhouse, packaging hall, fermentation and beer storage tanks, raw-material storage facilities and a plant for handling production materials.

It will also have a wastewater treatment plant and other infrastructure required to support large-scale beverage manufacturing.

The proposed Rwamagana brewery would be significantly larger than BRALIRWA’s existing facility in Rubavu District, bordering DR Congo.

The Rubavu brewery had an annual production capacity of approximately 1.3 million hectolitres (130 million litres) following an expansion in 2023, while the new Rwamagana plant is designed to produce 2.5 million hectolitres (250 million litres) annually.

This would make the Rwamagana facility almost twice the size of the Rubavu brewery, although the latter received another production line in 2024 whose additional capacity was not publicly disclosed.

One of the notable aspects of the project is its proposed use of Lake Muhazi as a source of water for industrial production.

Technical information associated with the project identifies plans for water abstraction and discharge pipelines connecting the facility to the lake.

Water is a major input in brewing and soft-drink manufacturing, making its availability and management important to the operation of the proposed plant.

The project also includes a wastewater treatment facility and a stormwater management pond. However, details of the planned water abstraction volumes and environmental safeguards have not yet been publicly established.

BRALIRWA, which has been part of the Netherlands-based HEINEKEN Group since 1971, is Rwanda’s leading beverage manufacturer, with a portfolio of local and international alcoholic and non-alcoholic drinks.

Established in 1957, the company currently operates two production sites in the country: a brewery in Rubavu District and a soft-drink manufacturing facility in Kigali.

Its portfolio includes brands such as Primus, Mützig, Heineken and Amstel, alongside non-alcoholic beverages.

According to the company’s published 2025 figures, BRALIRWA sold 2.799 million hectolitres of beverages during the year. It has more than 400 employees and distributes its products across all 30 districts of Rwanda.

The proposed Rwamagana facility would add a third production location and significantly expand the company’s manufacturing infrastructure.

The investment comes as BRALIRWA reports strong growth in its business.

In its financial results for the first half of 2026, the company reported a 20% increase in revenue, supported by higher sales volumes of beer and soft drinks, price adjustments and continued demand for premium products.

Its profit after tax increased by 37.6% to Rwf25.3 billion, compared with Rwf18.4 billion during the corresponding period in 2025.

The investment is also expected to strengthen Rwamagana’s position as an industrial destination.

Rwamagana is among four industrial parks selected by the Government for priority infrastructure development during the 2025/2026 financial year, alongside Musanze, Muhanga and Bugesera.

The Government allocated Rwf10 billion to improve infrastructure in the four industrial parks, including access roads, electricity, water supply and treatment facilities, as part of efforts to attract manufacturing investments.

BRALIRWA’s proposed investment adds to the growing range of industrial activities expected in the area.

The new brewery could also create opportunities for local suppliers, particularly agricultural producers supplying raw materials used in beverage manufacturing. However, BRALIRWA has not yet publicly disclosed how much of the new facility’s raw materials it intends to source from Rwandan farmers.

The project is expected to require substantial investment in production equipment, storage facilities, utilities and environmental management infrastructure.

The total investment value, construction timeline, expected number of jobs and planned commencement of production have not yet been publicly disclosed.

The Cabinet approval of November 26 marks an important step in the project’s development, although it does not in itself mean construction has started.

MN202611_nch4fm3ifk.t:
Leta y'u Rwanda yemeje gahunda yo kwimuka ku murongo w’itumanaho, umuntu akajya ku wundi murongo agumanye nimero ya telefoni asanzwe akoresha.

Ni bimwe mu byemezo by'Inama y’Abaminisitiri yateranye ku mugoroba wo ku wa 26 Ugushyingo 2026, iyobowe na Perezida wa Repubulika Paul Kagame.

Ni gahunda biteganyijwe ko izafasha abakoresha telefone ngendanwa guhindura ikigo cy’itumanaho badahinduye nimero zabo ndetse na konti za Mobile Money bakoresha mu koherezanya no kubitsa amafaranga.

Biteganyijwe ko bizongera guhatana hagati y’ibigo by’itumanaho, bigateza imbere serivisi nziza kandi zihendutse, byongere n’ikoreshwa ry’ikoranabuhanga mu by’imari.

Mu bindi Iyi nama yemeje gahunda yo gutangiza igihembwe cyo gutera ibiti n’amashyamba cy’umwaka wa 2026/2027, igamije kubungabunga urusobe rw’ibinyabuzima mu gihugu hose.

Guverinoma yashimangiye ko Abanyarwanda bose bakwiye kugira uruhare mu gutera ibiti no kubungabunga amashyamba asanzwe mu midugudu yabo n’aho batuye. Ibi bigamije guhangana n’ihinduka ry’ibihe, kurengera ibidukikije no guteza imbere imibereho myiza y’abaturage.

Mu byemezo bijyanye n’amategeko, Inama y’Abaminisitiri yemeje imishinga ibiri y’amategeko yo kwemeza burundu amasezerano y’inguzanyo u Rwanda rwagiranye n’Ikigega Nyafurika Gitsura Amajyambere, agamije gushyigikira ikigo cy’icyitegererezo mu buhinzi bukoresha ikoranabuhanga no gutanga serivisi z’ubuvuzi hifashishijwe ikoranabuhanga, mu cyiciro cya kabiri.

Yanemeje amasezerano atandukanye y’ishoramari n’ubufatanye, arimo amasezerano hagati ya Guverinoma y’u Rwanda na EH Venture Capital Rwanda Ltd, yerekeye icyiciro cya kabiri cy’umushinga wa Kigali Financial Square.

Hari kandi amasezerano na BRALIRWA Plc yo kubaka uruganda rw’ibinyobwa mu Cyanya cy’Inganda cya Rwamagana, ndetse n’andi na SteelRwa Industries Ltd yo kubaka uruganda rutunganya ubutare no gukora ibikoresho by’ubwubatsi.

Iyi nama yanemeje amasezerano yo gukusanya inkunga hagati y’u Rwanda n’Umuryango Nyafurika wita ku binyabuzima byo mu gasozi, agamije gushyigikira ibikorwa byo kubungabunga no guteza imbere Pariki y’Igihugu y’Ibirunga.

Yemeje kandi amasezerano y’ubufatanye hagati ya Leta n’inganda z’icyayi yerekeye imicungire y’amashyamba.

Mu bindi byatangajwe, Inama y’Abaminisitiri yamenyeshejwe ko Bwana Samuel Kamau Nganga ari we uzahagararira Banki y’Isi mu Rwanda.

Minisitiri w’Ubumwe n’Iterambere ry’Igihugu yagaragaje gahunda y’iminsi 16 yo kurwanya ingengabitekerezo ya Jenoside, izatangira ku wa 25 Ugushyingo ikageza ku wa 10 Ukuboza 2026.

Minisitiri w’Ikoranabuhanga mu Itumanaho na Inovasiyo na we yamenyesheje Inama ko i Kigali hazakirirwa irushanwa ngarukamwaka rya Hanga Pitchfest ku wa 2 Ukuboza 2026, rikazahuza abantu batandatu bageze ku cyiciro cya nyuma, bagahatana berekana imishinga itanga ibisubizo mu nzego zitandukanye.

Minisitiri wa Siporo yatangaje ko kuva ku wa 15 kugeza ku wa 22 Ukuboza 2026, mu turere twose tw’igihugu hazabera amarushanwa y’imikino ngororamubiri, agamije gushakisha no guteza imbere impano z’abakiri bato.

MN202611_1v6gu0302bl.t:
Icyakora, ibitaro n’amavuriro byinshi byo mu bihugu bifite ubukungu buri hasi n’ibiri hagati ntibifite ibikoresho n’imiti by’ibanze bikenewe kugira ngo abarwayi bahabwe ubuvuzi bufite ireme kandi ku gihe.

Ni yo mpamvu, uyu munsi, Umuryango wa Mohamed bin Zayed Foundation for Humanity watangaje ko uzashora miliyoni 135 z’amadolari ya Amerika mu rwego rwo kongera uburyo bwo kubona imiti, ibikoresho n’ikoranabuhanga by’ingenzi mu buvuzi, mu bihugu icyenda bya Afurika.

Iyi gahunda izafatanya na za guverinoma mu mushinga mugari ugamije kugabanya impfu z’ababyeyi n’impinja, no kongera ireme rya serivisi z’ubuvuzi bw’ibanze.

Iri shoramari ryatangarijwe mu nama mpuzamahanga ku buzima rusange muri Afurika (International Conference on Public Health in Africa - CPHIA), yabereye i Addis Ababa muri Ethiopia.

Rizagirira akamaro ibigo nderabuzima birenga 500 byo muri Ethiopia, Kenya, Liberia, Malawi, Nigeria, u Rwanda, Ghana, Sierra Leone na Mozambique.

Biteganyijwe ko inkunga y'uyu muryango izafasha kandi kubona andi mafaranga arenga miliyoni 550 z’amadolari, azatangwa na za guverinoma z’ibihugu bizafatanya na yo ndetse n’abaterankunga.

Ibi bizafasha kongera umusaruro w’ishoramari n’ingaruka nziza rizagira. Buri gihugu kizagira uruhare muri iyi gahunda kizasabwa gutanga amafaranga nibura angana n’ayo kizahabwa.

Dr Shamma Khalifa Al Mazrouei, Umuyobozi Mukuru wa Mohamed bin Zayed Foundation for Humanity, yagize ati: “Dufatanyije n’ibihugu, turaharanira ko hazabaho ejo hazaza aho nta mubyeyi, uruhinja cyangwa umwana uzongera gupfa azize impamvu zashoboraga gukumirwa. Abakozi b’urwego rw'ubuzima bafite ubumenyi n’ubushobozi ni ingenzi kugira ngo iyi ntego igerweho, ariko ubushobozi bwabo bwo kurokora ubuzima no kubunoza bushingira ku kuba babona ku gihe imiti n’ibikoresho bakeneye."

Yonegeyeho kandi ati “Mu bihugu bitandukanye bya Afurika, za guverinoma zikomeje gushyira imbaraga mu guteza imbere inzego z’ubuzima n’abakozi batanga serivisi z’ubuvuzi. Twishimiye uyu mwanya wo gukorana na byo, kugira ngo abakora mu rwego rw’ubuzima bahore babona ibikoresho bakeneye, bityo barusheho gutanga serivisi nziza ku barwayi no mu baturage muri rusange.”

Kubura imiti n’ibikoresho by’ubuvuzi ni ikibazo gikomeje kugaragara mu nzego z’ubuzima z’ibihugu byinshi. Ibi bituma abarwayi batinda kuvurwa kandi bikadindiza intambwe imaze guterwa mu guteza imbere ubuzima. Muri Afurika, impuzandengo y’imiti y’ingenzi iboneka mu bigo nderabuzima bya Leta ni 35% gusa, mu gihe ibigo nderabuzima bitageze kuri kimwe cya gatatu bifite ibikoresho byo gukora ibizamini by’ibanze byo gusuzuma indwara.

Mu guhangana n’iki kibazo, za guverinoma zo muri Afurika zikomeje kwitabira uburyo bwo gufatanya kwishyura ibikenewe mu buvuzi, aho amafaranga ava ku baterankunga ahuzwa n’ay’ibihugu ubwabyo, hagamijwe gushyigikira gahunda z’ibihugu zo kubona no gukomeza gutanga imiti n’ibikoresho by’ubuvuzi.

Muri Ethiopia, Mohamed bin Zayed Foundation for Humanity ni yo yabaye umuterankunga wa mbere wemeye gushyigikira gahunda y’icyo gihugu yiswe Reproductive, Maternal, Newborn, and Child Health (RMNCH) Compact, itanga miliyoni 20 z’amadolari.

Iyi nkunga yafashije kubona andi mafaranga angana na miliyoni 151.2 z’amadolari yatanzwe n’abafatanyabikorwa mu iterambere. Aya mafaranga na yo yahujwe n’andi angana na yo yatanzwe na Guverinoma ya Ethiopia, bituma haboneka miliyoni 342.4 z’amadolari yo guteza imbere serivisi z’ubuzima bw’imyororokere, ababyeyi, impinja n’abana mu gihugu hose.

Mu gihe cy’imyaka itatu, aya mafaranga azafasha ibigo nderabuzima bigera kuri 120 byo muri Ethiopia kubona ibikoresho bizafasha kurokora ubuzima.

Ishoramari rizaba ririmo ibikoresho bigezweho byo gusuzuma inda hakoreshejwe ikoranabuhanga ry’ubwenge buhangano (AI), bizafasha abakozi b’ubuzima kumenya vuba ibibazo bishobora kuvuka mu gihe cyo gutwita no mu gihe cyo kubyara, bakanabigiraho icyo bakora. Rizaba ririmo kandi imiti ya antibiyotike ifasha kugabanya ibyago byo kwandura indwara zikomeye ziterwa na mikorobe, zirimo sepsis.

Dr Mekdes Daba, Minisitiri w’Ubuzima wa Ethiopia, yagize ati:

“Ethiopia yakomeje gushyira imbere guteza imbere ubuzima bw’imyororokere, ubw’ababyeyi, impinja n’abana, mu rwego rwa gahunda yayo yo guhindura no guteza imbere urwego rw’ubuzima.

“Gahunda ya RMNCH Compact ishimangira iyi ntego binyuze mu buryo bushya bw’ubufatanye bushingiye ku ishoramari rihuriweho no kubazwa inshingano.

“Ubu bufatanye buzatuma serivisi z’ubuvuzi zirushaho gutangwa neza, imiti n’ibikoresho by’ingenzi bikenerwa mu buvuzi biboneke ku buryo buhoraho, kandi burusheho gukomeza serivisi abagore, impinja n’abana bakeneye. Intego yacu irasobanutse: kugabanya impfu z’ababyeyi, impinja n’abana zishobora gukumirwa, aho baba hose muri Ethiopia.”

Mu Rwanda, Mohamed bin Zayed Foundation for Humanity izatanga miliyoni 15 z’amadolari yo kugura no kugeza ibikoresho by’ingenzi by’ubuvuzi mu bigo nderabuzima 170, birimo ibitaro by’uturere n’ibitaro byigisha ubuvuzi. Iyi nkunga kandi izafasha gushakisha andi mafaranga angana na miliyoni 40 z’amadolari.

Iri shoramari rizashingira kuri gahunda u Rwanda rusanzwe rushyira mu bikorwa, rigamije gutuma kubyara birushaho kuba mu mutekano no kunoza ubuvuzi bw’impinja.

Mu bikoresho bizatangwa harimo ibyifashishwa n’abakozi b’ubuzima mu guhangana n'ikibazo cyo kuva nyuma yo kubyara, ibyuma bifasha impinja kuvuka zidashyitse gukura neza (incubators), ndetse n’ibikoresho bifasha impinja zitagejeje igihe cyangwa zirwaye guhumeka.

Dr Sabin Nsanzimana, Minisitiri w’Ubuzima w’u Rwanda, yagize ati: “Mu myaka 20 ishize, u Rwanda rwateye intambwe ikomeye mu guteza imbere ubuzima bw’ababyeyi n’abana, bituma imiryango myinshi ibona serivisi z’ubuvuzi bufite ireme."

“Kugira ngo ibyo twagezeho bikomeze, ntibihagije kugira abakozi b’ubuzima bafite ubumenyi n’ibigo nderabuzima. Hakenewe kandi ko haboneka ku buryo buhoraho imiti, ibikoresho n’ikoranabuhanga bikenerwa mu gutanga serivisi z’ubuvuzi.

“Ubufatanye dufitanye na Mohamed bin Zayed Foundation for Humanity bushingiye ku ishoramari u Rwanda rumaze igihe rushyira mu rwego rw’ubuzima. Dufatanyije, turaharanira ko intambwe tumaze gutera ihinduka imibereho myiza n’ubuzima bwiza kuri buri mubyeyi, uruhinja n’umwana.”

Muri Liberia, Mohamed bin Zayed Foundation for Humanity izatanga miliyoni 10 z’amadolari, azongerwaho andi mafaranga angana na yo azatangwa n’abaterankunga. Aya mafaranga azafasha ibitaro bikuru byigisha ubuvuzi muri icyo gihugu n’ibigo nderabuzima bifitanye isano na byo, mu rwego rwo kunoza serivisi z’ubuvuzi bw’abagore, impinja n’abana.

Mu bikoresho biteganyijwe kugurwa harimo ikoranabuhanga rizafasha guhangana n’ibibazo bikomeye bishobora kuvuka mu gihe cyo kubyara, gutabara impinja n’abana barembye, ndetse no gusuzuma indwara vuba hifashishijwe ibikoresho biri hafi y’umurwayi.

Uretse ibikoresho, iyi nkunga izanakoreshwa mu mahugurwa n’ubujyanama mu kazi ku baganga, abaforomo n’ababyaza, kugira ngo bashobore gukoresha neza ikoranabuhanga rishya mu kazi ka buri munsi.

Iyi gahunda kandi izafasha Liberia guteza imbere ubumenyi bw’inzobere mu bijyanye n’ubwubatsi n’imicungire y’ibikoresho by’ubuvuzi (biomedical engineering), kugira ngo ibyo bikoresho bibashe gusanwa no gukomeza gukora neza mu myaka iri imbere.

Dr Louise Mapleh Kpoto, Minisitiri w’Ubuzima wa Liberia, yagize ati: “Liberia yiyemeje gukomeza guteza imbere urwego rw’ubuzima, kugira ngo buri wese abone serivisi z’ubuvuzi bufite ireme, aho yaba atuye hose.

“Ubufatanye dufitanye na Mohamed bin Zayed Foundation for Humanity buzadufasha kugera kuri iyi ntego, binyuze mu kunoza serivisi zitangirwa mu bitaro byacu bikuru no kongerera ubushobozi abakozi b’ubuzima.

“Dufatanyije, turimo kunoza serivisi z’ubuvuzi zihabwa abaturage bacu muri iki gihe, tunategura urwego rw’ubuzima ruzashobora guhangana n’ibikenewe mu gihe kizaza.”

Mohamed bin Zayed Foundation for Humanity ni umuryango utanga inkunga ugamije guteza imbere ubushobozi bwa muntu no kumufasha kubona amahirwe yo kwiteza imbere.

Uyu muryango ushora imari mu nkingi z’ingenzi z’iterambere ry’abantu, zirimo gukomeza inzego z’ubuzima, kugabanya indwara zishobora gukumirwa no gufasha abaturage kwiteza imbere.

Binyuze mu bufatanye n’ibihugu ndetse n’abaturage, uyu muryango ushyigikira gahunda z’iterambere zigamije kugira impinduka zirambye, ku bantu bariho ubu ndetse n’abazabakomokaho.

Mohamed bin Zayed Foundation for Humanity ni umuryango wunganira Erth Zayed Philanthropies.
